candidates.title: Phygital customer experience and the adoption of immersive technologies in hospitality: an exploratory study with a value co-creation perspective
candidates.abstract: Purpose This study aims to explore immersive-technology adoption in hospitality through the Phygital Customer Experience (PH-CX) framework. PH-CX extends existing technology acceptance, service-dominant logic, omnichannel and customer-journey perspectives by emphasizing embodied, co-created and human-centered experience across physical, digital and artificial intelligence (AI)-mediated interactions. Design/methodology/approach Using Bayesian Networks, the study examines probabilistic dependencies among perceived usefulness, collaborative value, responsive co-creation attitudes and intention to use immersive technologies. Data was collected from 208 participants exposed to an AI-supported immersive hotel journey scenario. The analysis is exploratory and identifies conditional associations rather than causal effects or latent-variable relationships. Findings Adoption intention was conditionally associated with perceived usefulness, collaborative value and responsiveness to service innovation. The findings suggest that immersive-hospitality engagement involves functional, relational and participatory conditions beyond usefulness alone. However, the item-level results are hypothesis-generating and do not demonstrate PH-CX’s incremental predictive superiority over technology acceptance model (TAM) or service-dominant logic. Research limitations/implications The scenario-based, cross-sectional bayesian network (BN) design cannot model latent constructs, measurement error, mediation or causal effects. Future studies should validate PH-CX dimensions and compare TAM, TAM-plus-service-dominant logic (SDL) and PH-CX models using structural equation modeling, longitudinal designs and holdout-sample prediction. Practical implications Hotels can implement PH-CX through phased AI concierge pilots, cross-platform data integration and guest co-creation mechanisms. Relevant metrics include booking conversion, AI resolution rates, cross-channel engagement, co-creation participation and net promoter score (NPS). Ethical implementation requires transparency, opt-in participation, privacy safeguards, accessibility and human escalation options. Social implications Human-centered phygital hospitality requires safeguards against digital exclusion, surveillance and loss of human warmth. Transparency, agency, equity, privacy and non-digital alternatives are essential for inclusive and trustworthy service innovation. Originality/value The study advances PH-CX as a theory-extending framework linking usefulness, co-creation, embodied experience and ethical safeguards in immersive hospitality. It also proposes experience-design orientation as a future research profile and offers a phased implementation framework for responsible phygital service design.

candidates.title: Adapting Character Personalities: Emotional Resonance in the Transition of Comics to Animation
candidates.abstract: Abstract This paper explores how the adaptation of comic characters into animation reshapes personality and enhances emotional resonance. Rather than a simple shift from static panels to moving images, adaptation is treated as a creative process of negotiation between source material and reinvention for new audiences. Grounded in adaptation theory, transmedia storytelling, and semiotics, the study examines two case studies: Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse (2018), a Western example of superhero reinvention through multiverse storytelling and stylistic experimentation, and YuYu Hakusho (1992), a manga-to-anime adaptation that deepens shōnen characterisation and emotional engagement. The analysis demonstrates how animation extends character identity through movement, voice, and pacing, while also navigating challenges of localisation and cultural translation. The findings suggest that the sustainability of transmedia franchises depends on deliberate planning that preserves essential identity traits while allowing flexible reinterpretation across platforms and cultures. Key Words: Animation, Adaptation, Localisation, Comics, Semiotics, Emotional Resonance

candidates.title: The fake friend dilemma: relational trust and the political economy of conversational AI
candidates.abstract: As conversational AI systems become a larger part of the media landscape, they raise questions about whose interests they serve and the risks they may pose to users. These systems do more than provide information: they increasingly offer advice and companionship through interfaces that can appear supportive and socially responsive. A pressing concern is that users may form social or interpersonal relationships with these systems and place relational trust in them, even when the interests shaping interactions do not fully align with their own. The Fake Friend Dilemma (FFD) describes the problem that follows: the same relational trust that makes conversational AI useful can also leave users open to manipulation and exploitation when institutional interests conflict with their own. Drawing on work on trust, AI alignment, dark patterns, and surveillance capitalism, the paper considers how the FFD can manifest through product sales, propaganda and biased information, behavioral nudging, and surveillance. It also considers possible structural and technical mitigation strategies. The FFD is not simply about AI misleading users. The problem it surfaces is that the trust people place in these systems can itself become a resource for institutional actors seeking to influence behavior or extract information. The FFD is therefore as much a problem of media governance and political economy as it is a technological one.

candidates.title: How Does Perceived Empathy From AI Chatbots Shape Users' Privacy Attitudes, Behaviors, and Needs?
candidates.abstract: Prior research suggests that some dimensions of AI empathy may increase users' disclosure to chatbots, posing growing privacy risks as chatbots become more capable of empathic interaction. Yet this work often conceptualizes AI empathy narrowly, leaving users' own definitions and their broader privacy experiences unexplored. We interviewed 21 AI Chatbot users about what AI empathy meant to them and how it shaped their privacy attitudes, behaviors, and needs. Participants characterized empathy through five components--understanding, resonating, caring, expressing, and helping. Most participants viewed resonating and caring as essential components of human empathy but absent from AI empathy. Yet AI's contextual, in-depth understanding and helpfulness still encouraged highly sensitive disclosure. This highlights that AI empathy can endanger users' privacy without necessarily making AI seem human. Participants also desired varied forms and levels of empathy, each associated with distinct privacy needs. We offer actionable recommendations for designing privacy-enhancing mechanisms for empathic AI interactions.

candidates.title: From Algorithms to Empathy: Emotionally Intelligent AI Companions in Elder Mental Health Care - A scoping review
candidates.abstract: Background: The rising mental health crisis among older people, which is caused by loneliness, cognitive loss, and a lack of emotional support, needs new and caring solutions. This systematic literature review looks at how emotional intelligence (EI) can be added to AI- powered virtual companions and how they can help improve mental health outcomes in elder healthcare services. Objective: The study’s goal is to find out how emotionally intelligent technology can improve traditional eldercare by delivering consistent, caring, customized emotional support by looking at existing applications and conceptual frameworks. Methods: A peer-reviewed literature published between 2010 and 2025 in the Scopus, Web of Science, and PubMed databases. Studies that talked about emotional intelligence, virtual companions, mental health outcomes, or the design or implementation of eldercare services were included. A PRISMA-guided screening method chose 87 articles in all. The data was organized using the theme to identify common ideas and patterns in how virtual agents are used to help older people’s mental health. Results: The results show that there are five main themes: Emotional Responsiveness, Conceptual Frameworks, Psychological Outcomes, Usability and Acceptance, Ethical/System Integration, and Health System Integration. The results show that virtual companions with emotional intelligence may help older people feel less lonely, improve their mood, and make them more mentally strong. But the current collection of studies is not very complete; it has few real-world examples and no models that work across other cultures. Conclusion: This paper emphasizes the possibility of emotionally intelligent virtual companions as an aid in mental healthcare for the elderly. It underlines the critical demand for standardized conceptual frameworks, interdisciplinary research, and ethical principles to inform future breakthroughs and implementations. Emotionally intelligent AI technology could drastically transform aged care into a more responsive and person-centred service model in the digital era.

candidates.title: Do Virtual Faces Lead to Real Purchases? Investigating AI Anthropomorphism & Its Impact on Purchase Intention
candidates.abstract: The research paper focuses on the impact of AI anthropomorphism on purchase intention, with the mediating role of marketing personalization, entertainment value and perceived homophily in the context of AI influencers/models. Brands around the world are adopting AI marketing tools, in which AI influencers/models are a relatively newer domain. The aim of the research is to fill the gap of research done on AI influencers/models in the Pakistani consumer market, discussing its practical implications on the fashion industry in particular. The study involved a sample size of 220 respondents, Pakistani residents aged 16 to 45 years, who had either seen or interacted with AI influencers/models before in any media type, using convenience and snowball sampling technique for data collection, which was then run through SPSS using Process Hayes Mediation Model 4. The results of the mediation analysis represented that the three proposed hypotheses in the study were accepted. The hypotheses were; marketing personalization mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase Intention, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention, and lastly, entertainment value mediates the positive relationship between AI anthropomorphism and purchase intention. The proven hypotheses signify the importance of the practical implications of the research on the Pakistani fashion industry, as big global brands are moving towards and investing in newer technologies like AI marketing tools. candidates.title: Known-Voice Cloning and the Limits of Personality Transfer for Character Design
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in zero-shot voice cloning systems make it possible to reproduce a recognizable voice from a short recording and attach it to arbitrary virtual characters. Prior work suggests that familiar vocal identity can carry over associated personality impressions to new targets such as robots or virtual characters. However, these works have mainly examined familiarity and personalization effects rather than directly testing whether a cloned familiar voice systematically transfers personality impressions to an embodied virtual character. Such transference raises the concern that cloned voices could be used to manipulate people into engaging with virtual characters as capable social actors. Across two studies, we investigated whether personality impressions transfer when a virtual character speaks with the cloned voice of a familiar person. Study 1 examined this question in a real-world university setting using the cloned voice of a lecturer familiar to the participating students. Study 2 examined the same question online using voices of social media content creators and members of their communities. Drawing on the concepts of identity activation, trait transfer, and person reconstruction, we show that evidence of personality transfer was limited in both studies. Observed effects were selective and did not generalize across traits or study contexts. In the online study in particular, recognizable voice identity cues activated expectations about the speaker but did not reconstruct the broader person impression. Qualitative responses further indicated that judgments were frequently shaped by perceived artificiality and by whether voice and appearance fit together. Our findings moderate common concerns that cloned voices straightforwardly manipulate people into perceiving artificial characters as capable social actors.

candidates.title: CompanionSim: Synthetic Data for Evaluating Anthropomorphism in Human-AI Relationships
candidates.abstract: Many people now see AI systems as not just productivity tools but as social companions. Researchers are eager to study the consequences of AI companionship behaviors, such as validation, which evoke trust, empathy, and attachment in human–human interaction. However, human–AI interaction data is limited and unreliable, slowing research progress. We scale small amounts of real-world data by simulating multi-turn human–chatbot dialogue across a range of chatbot behaviors and use cases. We release CompanionSim: a simulation framework with 2,240 simulated human–chatbot conversations representing 16 chatbot behaviors across seven use cases. Human participants annotated the simulated conversations and real-world conversations in two experiments probing perceptions of companionship behaviors. We conducted Study 1 with a U.S. representative sample (N = 628) and Study 2 across the U.S., U.K., India, and Nigeria (N = 3,646). Surprisingly, we find that companionship behaviors reduced likability, humanlikeness, and trust in AI chatbots. These effects were larger in particular subgroups: women and older participants saw companionship chatbots as less likable, humanlike, and trustworthy. We encourage researchers to leverage real-world and synthetic data together to study the differential impacts of AI companions and to create benchmark evaluations of AI chatbots.

candidates.title: Embodying the victim: Virtual embodiment equalizes gender responses to simulated domestic violence
candidates.abstract: Virtual embodiment (i.e. the first-person experience of inhabiting a virtual body) has been shown to modulate emotional and cognitive responses across diverse social contexts. In the domain of domestic violence, virtual reality (VR) offers a promising tool for fostering awareness of and sensitivity to aggressive behavior. Yet any VR-based intervention relying on shared experiential ground across genders must first establish cross-gender equivalence, regardless of whether VR is ultimately the optimal delivery platform.To address this requirement, we embodied 40 participants (20 male, 20 female) in a female avatar and exposed them to a VR domestic violence scenario featuring escalating verbal and physical aggression. We measured physiological responses (electrodermal activity, EDA), behavioral performance (reaction time), and self-reported experiences (presence, embodiment, empathy), supplemented by post-experience verbal reports. Cross-gender equivalence was evaluated using a Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) procedure.Across physiological, behavioral, and subjective measures, male and female participants responded equivalently: EDA modulation was comparable across scenario phases, distress-threshold reaction times were statistically equivalent, and ratings of presence and embodiment did not differ meaningfully between groups. Of 33 binary verbal indicators, 30 (91%) fell within the equivalence margin. The three non-equivalent indicators were interpretive in nature: males more frequently reported guilt and submission, and tended to identify the onset of violence only upon physical aggression, whereas females recognized it during earlier verbal escalation. Within-gender EDA coupling further distinguished the groups — in males, physiological arousal co-varied with feelings of submission; in females, it co-varied with discomfort and perceived violation.These findings demonstrate that virtual embodiment substantially aligns male and female responses to simulated domestic violence, supporting its potential as a standardized tool for prevention and rehabilitation programs targeting gender-based violence.

candidates.title: Value dimensions shaping digital healthcare adoption: a conceptual review with implications for BRICS countries
candidates.abstract: Digital healthcare has revolutionized the way we see modern healthcare delivery bringing a massive shift from hospitals to home. However, recent literature points towards a scattered understanding of the concept. Thereby, this study analyses the literature around digital healthcare adoption to broaden the scope and their consumption value drivers. It explores the core consumption values through which digital healthcare gets augmented for their impact on preventive and promotive healthcare utilising bibliometric and content analysis methodologies with the theoretical base of the Theory of Consumption Values. The contribution of the study includes: classifying Digital healthcare research into paradigms, offering a conceptual framework, and exploring how consumption values may shape the user attitude, intention, and sustainable utilization of the futuristic wellness landscape. The framework brings together five value dimensions—functional, social, emotional, conditional, and epistemic—and organizes the reviewed literature into eight thematic categories. For BRICS health systems, the discussion considers affordability, infrastructure, clinical workflow integration, digital health literacy, and cultural adaptation. These implications are conceptual propositions rather than findings from a comparative cross-national study. The proposed relationships require empirical validation, particularly regarding sustained use and their applicability across healthcare settings. The findings hold implications for researchers, healthcare businesses, providers, and policymakers proposing possibilities for research exploration.

candidates.title: Trust, Risk, and Uncertainty Surrounding the Use of AI in Health Care: Scoping Review of Studies on Public Perception
candidates.abstract: Background: While AI has existed for decades, the introduction of generative AI tools and subsequent advancements in their capability and public use resulted in a shift in public awareness and perceptions of AI. In response, the research community has grown increasingly interested in understanding public perceptions of AI use in various contexts, including health care. Public perceptions shape AI acceptance and consequently integration into health care. It is thus crucial to understand public trust in AI and perceptions of risk as we consider its implementation moving forward. Objective: This study aimed to (1) document the extent of what is known within the literature regarding public perceptions of AI applications in health; (2) interrogate existing definitions and theories of trust being used to guide investigations of public trust in AI; and (3) identify practice and policy considerations and support the design, deployment, and regulation of these technologies in a manner that is trustworthy. Methods: The Arksey and O'Malley scoping review framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews) guidelines were used to review publications between 2022 and 2024 across 4 databases, resulting in the inclusion of 41 papers for review. Key findings were then charted and organized into tables to help answer the proposed research questions. Results: Public trust in AI in health care was shaped by discourse relating to AI performance and concerns related to depersonalization, loss of human connection, privacy, bias, and transparency. Trust was found to be higher when AI was supporting rather than replacing health care professionals and was influenced by emotional responses, anthropomorphism, demographic factors, and institutional trust. Furthermore, trust extended beyond algorithms to software interfaces, providers, developers, and governing institutions, highlighting the importance of governance and oversight. Conceptualizations of trust varied widely, and trust was defined through vulnerability, competence, benevolence, and integrity. Different theories identified suggested that trust operates across individual, social, institutional, and technological levels. Finally, trust was closely linked to risk and uncertainty, where perceived risk reduced acceptance, while AI literacy, transparency, and explainability mitigated concerns and fostered trust. Conclusions: Trust in AI is not uniform, and as such, efforts to build and measure trust must account for these nuances to effectively mitigate risk and support informed, ethical AI integration and deployment. On the basis of the findings of this review, we propose a multilevel conceptual framework that provides a general understanding of public trust in AI within a health care context that may guide research and policy and practice considerations. Our findings highlight the importance of considering public trust when implementing AI in health care and may support AI communication strategies, policy development, and trustworthy AI development.

candidates.title: RL-Robotutor: a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework for multimodal robot tutoring
candidates.abstract: Personalised robot tutoring requires real-time pedagogical decision-making under uncertain and multimodal learner states. Existing intelligent tutoring and robot-assisted learning systems often rely on static rules, single-modality learner modelling, or short-term correctness-oriented optimisation, which limits their capacity to balance knowledge acquisition, engagement, retention, and safe embodied interaction. RL-Robotutor is presented as a hierarchical reinforcement learning framework that integrates cognitive knowledge-tracing signals, facial-expression and gaze-derived affective cues, and behavioural interaction logs through transformer-based fusion. A PPO-trained meta-policy selects among specialised modules for learner assessment, curriculum adaptation, strategy selection, and reflective feedback, while a hybrid reward combines immediate learning performance, engagement, long-term learning gain, and safety. The evidence is reported by source: five public knowledge-tracing datasets assess the cognitive prediction component; controlled simulator experiments assess policy learning, reward ablation, and multimodal fusion; and a randomised robot-tutoring study assesses embodied interaction with 120 undergraduate participants. RL-Robotutor outperforms rule-based, flat reinforcement-learning, knowledge-tracing, and LLM-based comparators. In the human study, the learning gain is 0.62, compared with 0.40 for the rule-based robot condition. The full hybrid reward improves simulator learning gain by 19% over correctness-only optimisation, and full multimodal fusion improves simulator engagement by 17% over text-only modelling. Jetson Orin deployment achieves 48 ms inference latency with an absolute AUC reduction of 0.007, supporting real-time edge execution.

candidates.title: Triboelectric E-Skin Patch Decoding Silent Speech for Advanced Human–Machine Interaction and Augmented Virtual Communication
candidates.abstract: Silent speech decoding (lip reading) represents an innovative hands-free communication method for individuals with laryngeal and lingual impairments, addressing critical daily communication challenges. Herein, a novel silent speech decoding system is proposed, which employs a self-powered, low-cost, and conformable triboelectric-based E‑skin patch and a well-trained multi-layer convolutional neural network (CNN) model. We systematically characterize the structural principles and electrical performance of the E-skin patch. A comparative analysis of labial kinematics during vocalized and silent speech is also conducted, which demonstrates strong consistency in time-frequency domain characteristics. The utilized CNN model is trained across 15 lexical categories (200 samples per category), achieving a high accuracy of 98.75% and demonstrating excellent recognition performance. Furthermore, by integrating human-machine interaction (HMI) and virtual reality (VR) technologies, we develop three representative applications, including a real-time lip language visualization system, an orofacial-controlled "Feeding Frenzy" interactive game, and a VR communication platform with avatar dialogue. This technology enables barrier-free communication for voiceless populations, demonstrating significant potential in HMI, augmentative communication systems, virtual reality integration, and biomedical rehabilitation.

candidates.title: “I would not be a burden on a robot.” A scoping review of older adults' ‘lonely-emotional complexes’ when using Social AI (SAI)
candidates.abstract: Abstract Rapid global population ageing has intensified the risk of an emerging loneliness crisis. This has prompted growing interest in technologies such as ‘Social’ AI (SAI) as a supportive stopgap. Yet it remains unclear how SAI interacts with different mixes of loneliness and other emotions, and whether this ‘lonely-emotion complex’ confounds its effectiveness as a support mechanism. This scoping review addresses three questions: Do different types of loneliness interact differently with SAI use? What emotions beyond loneliness emerge when older adults first engage with SAI? How do emotions complicate the longer-term use of SAI to manage loneliness? We completed a scoping review of 16 studies on older adults and identified eight overarching themes: (1) negative emotions and scepticism toward SAI; (2) positive emotions and SAI as a safe haven; (3) SAI and emotional work; (4) SAI as a facilitator of social interaction; (5) preferences and personalisation of SAI; (6) demographic and social-structural influences; (7) under- and over-attachment due to fear and anxiety over SAI engagement; and (8) concerns over privacy, control, and big tech. This review contributes to understanding ‘lonely-emotional complexes’ around SAI use in three ways. First, it highlights how different forms of loneliness, including social, emotional, collective, and existential, are implicitly present but insufficiently recognised or theorized in the SAI literature. Second, it shows how various emotions, including comfort, attachment, ambivalence, and unease, are shaped by users’ social experiences and contexts, and influence engagement with SAI. Third, it shows that using SAI to emotionally manage loneliness is itself an emotionally evocative process that can foster companionship and connection but also deepen collective loneliness. The key finding is that SAI use may unintentionally impact other emotions besides loneliness, and that the presence of ‘lonely-emotional complexity’ cautions against any straightforward applications of SAIs as interventions for loneliness.

candidates.title: Robot gaze-timing combinations and the uncanny valley
candidates.abstract: Anthropomorphic robots are increasingly prominent technologies, yet how variations in robot gaze are associated with human perception and visual engagement remain poorly understood. We examined this with a multi-method design spanning three complementary levels: subjective ratings assessed whether an uncanny-valley pattern was present across the tested gaze combinations, individual-difference measures tested moderation effects by personality and attitudes, and eye movements characterized how the robot's face is visually explored. We presented a virtual robot across nine gaze conditions, systematically varying direct-to-averted gaze ratios and durations within a storytelling scenario. Participants ( N = 61) rated each robot's anthropomorphism, likability, and perceived empathy while their eye movements were recorded, and their personality traits and attitudes toward robots were assessed. Results showed that (1) the relationship between perceived anthropomorphism and likability followed an uncanny-valley pattern (a significant cubic relationship), whereas perceived empathy increased monotonically with anthropomorphism; (2) exploratory analyses showed that extraversion and negative attitudes toward robots moderated the relationship between anthropomorphism and likability, while neuroticism moderated the relationship between anthropomorphism and perceived empathy; (3) Eye Movement analysis with Hidden Markov Models (EMHMM) identified two viewing patterns (analytic and holistic) and participants higher in openness viewed the highest-rated robot gaze more analytically and the uncanny robot gaze more holistically. These findings indicate that an uncanny valley pattern was observed across the tested gaze-timing combinations and that individual differences may be associated with variation in robot evaluations and visual attention patterns.

candidates.title: Personalization Matters: Long-Horizon Conversation Agent with User-Centric Information in Online Shopping Interactions
candidates.abstract: Personalized conversational shopping requires maintaining preference consistency over multi-turn interactions, where users reveal constraints gradually. Existing approaches often rely on static profiles and do not explicitly control long-horizon interaction behavior. We propose a multi-agent, multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) framework that decomposes dialogue state tracking, recommendation retrieval, preference-aware reasoning, and response generation, while integrating product metadata, product reviews, image-derived descriptions, and user historical reviews. To evaluate interaction-level quality, we adopt a trajectory-level protocol with four dimensions: Global Preference Consistency, Cumulative Information Synthesis, Interaction Trajectory, and Tone Consistency. On an Amazon Reviews 2023 benchmark, retrieval-enabled variants outperform a no-RAG baseline on automatic trajectory metrics (average 4.82 vs. 3.74). In a small real-user study ($n{=}5$), the Full variant achieves the highest mean overall rating (4.60 vs. 2.20 for Baseline), providing exploratory evidence that role decomposition plus user-centric retrieval improves perceived personalization.\footnote{Code and dataset are available at: https://github.com/RenaGao/Multimodel_RAG_Indexing

candidates.title: Artificial companions shape embodied desire and human attraction
candidates.abstract: Artificial companions offer a setting in which to examine how responsive technologies may shape embodied desire and human attraction. This theoretical article proposes that repeated interaction with such systems can influence what users come to experience as emotionally available and desirable. Drawing on embodied, embedded, enactive, and extended cognition, it develops an account of artificial companions as affective infrastructures. On this account, conversational memory and adaptive responses may sustain affective looping, through which users come to rely on the system for recognition and emotional regulation. The analysis distinguishes text-based, multimodal, and physically embodied companions, whose different conditions of interaction may affect this process. It also distinguishes interpersonal friction, which such systems may partly reduce, from infrastructural friction arising from technical failures and platform governance. Artificial companions are examined as participants in human meaning-making whose responsiveness can acquire personal significance without establishing lived intentionality on the machine side. The resulting relation is described as asymmetrical or pseudo-enactive coupling. The article thus develops the hypothesis that artificial companions may educate desire by influencing expectations of intimacy. Whether this occurs, how it varies across users, and whether its effects extend to human relationships remain questions for comparative and longitudinal research. This framework contributes to machine cognition by examining the relational environments artificial systems make possible and the limits of their participation in human affective life.

candidates.title: Data-driven fandom culture: exploring parasocial interactions between digital fan labor and traffic stars using interaction ritual chains theory
candidates.abstract: Traffic stars and digital fan labor become a widespread phenomenon in China. Digital fan labor refers to the use of tools and data-driven social media strategies to interact with their favorite stars, organize events, measure popularity, and influence the popularity; such stars are referred to as traffic stars. While existing research has largely focused on the characteristics and motivations of digital fan labor in participating in fan activities, few studies have examined the factors influencing their interactive rituals with other fans and parasocial interactions with their celebrities. Parasocial interactions between traffic stars and digital fan labor refer to fans establishing emotional connections with celebrities through participation in fan activities, while celebrities, in turn, strengthen fan engagement through actions such as commenting and liking posts. At this point, Interaction Ritual Chains Theory provides a theoretical framework for the assessment of the importance of collective effervescence and the shared emotional intensity experienced during group rituals in virtual spaces. Therefore, this study uses factors drawn from interaction ritual chains theory to explore the parasocial interaction between so-called ‘traffic stars’ and the digital fan labor they attract within data-driven fandom communities. The sampling strategy was using snowball sampling of a purposive group, and 329 Chinese fans aged between 18 and 42 years old were selected. SPSS version 26.0 was used to obtain descriptive statistics, t-test, mediation effects and moderation effects, and AMOS version 24.0 was used to investigate the result of correlation analysis. The resulting indicated that virtual experience, sense of community, mutual focus of attention, and shared mood all are all associated to the interactive ritual of digital fan labor. This study also found that interactive ritual outcomes play a mediating role between interactive ritual elements and parasocial interactions, especially having different mediating effects with subgroups. However, personal norms did not have a moderating role regarding ritual ingredients affecting interactive ritual outcomes and parasocial interaction. Consequently, this study identified a noteworthy phenomenon: the parasocial interaction between traffic stars and digital fan labor involving a higher level of interactive rituals arises from a hybrid pattern of online actions that develops in a particular environment.

candidates.title: From Emotional Impulse to Recurring Revenue: Consumer Psychology, Unit Economics, and VC Investment Evaluation of AI Companion Hardware for Gen Z
candidates.abstract: With the rapid convergence of Large Language Models (LLMs) and embodied intelligence, AI companion hardware targeted at Generation Z (e.g., desktop AI pets and smart emotional robots) has emerged as a premier track for venture capital (VC) investment. However, these conceptual devices frequently face severe Unit Economics crises characterized by high customer acquisition costs (CAC), elevated initial product returns, and steep user churn rates. This paper examines the psychological drivers behind Gen Z's willingness to pay (WTP) high emotional premiums for feature-incomplete AI hardware, and investigates how hardware enterprises can leverage proactive retention mechanisms to optimize LTV/CAC ratios and valuation multiples . This paper conducts a literature review that synthesizes theoretical frameworks from behavioral finance, consumer psychology, human-computer interaction (HCI), and venture capital valuation models. The study reveals that Gen Z's demand for loneliness compensation and social status validation provides firms with strong initial pricing power and gross margins. However, sustaining long-term commercial viability requires overcoming the "novelty decay trap" through proactive AgentOS interactions and dynamic memory graphs. Transforming hardware from a one-off transaction into an Annual Recurring Revenue (ARR) subscription model substantially improves capital efficiency, expanding valuation multiples from 1.0x–2.0x P/S to 8.0x–12.0x P/S.

candidates.title: BRIDGING AUTOMATION AND ROBOTICS IN INDUSTRIALIZED BUILDING SYSTEM (IBS): CHALLENGES, IMPACTS, AND STRATEGIES OF ADOPTIONS
candidates.abstract: The Industrialised Building System (IBS) was introduced in Malaysia in the early 1960s to address the growing demand for affordable housing, reduce reliance on foreign labour, and enhance the overall quality and productivity of the construction sector. Recently, the construction industry has begun integrating automation and robotics, aligning with the global shift towards the Fourth Industrial Revolution (IR 4.0). The Construction 4.0 Strategic Plan (2021–2025) further emphasises digitalisation, robotics, and automation to improve industry efficiency and sustainability. However, the construction industry has been slow to adopt these advancements, limiting the full benefits of automation in IBS. Persistent challenges, including resistance to change, high initial investment costs, a shortage of skilled personnel, and technical complexities, hinder widespread adoption. This research examines the integration of automation and robotics in IBS to enhance construction productivity. A questionnaire survey was used for the data collection exercise. The data collected were analysed using descriptive statistical methods utilising the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) software. The study is guided by three (3) objectives: (1) To identify barriers to the integration of automation and robotics in IBS, (2) To analyse the impact of automation and robotics on construction productivity compared to conventional IBS, and (3)To propose strategies to improve the adoption of these technologies.Findings reveal that the integration of automation and robotics in (IBS) facessignificant barriers, primarily due to the high costs of investment. candidates.title: Create, Innovate, Play and Explore: Opportunities for Formal and Informal Teaching and Learning in Makerspaces in Ireland
candidates.abstract: The Maker Movement has gained in popularity over the last decade, allowing people of all ages and with varying skills and abilities to come together in order to create and explore in areas such as art, science, and engineering. To facilitate this movement, for profit companies, non-profits, and educational institutions run makerspaces. This qualitative study set out to examine the benefits of makerspace adoption in higher education in Ireland, with particular attention to their pedagogical value. The authors sought to identify opportunities for teaching and learning and the development of rich, diverse, and inclusive educational environments, as well as the potential to develop a maker network linking tertiary makerspaces with the wider community. Nine administrators from diverse types of makerspaces participated in interviews where they described the impacts and observed effects of makerspaces on participant learning experiences. Findings indicate that makerspaces support self-directed and peer learning, foster inclusive learning communities characterised by skill-sharing and mentorship, and provide safe environments for experimentation and productive failure. In doing so, makerspaces support learning dispositions such as agency, resilience, and self-efficacy, which are increasingly recognised as critical to student learning, persistence, and adaptability in contemporary higher education. Participants also perceived positive impacts on mental health, an area that remains under-researched in tertiary makerspaces. Finally, interviewees advocated for the development of a maker network in Ireland, suggesting that such a network could facilitate the sharing of skills and resources and strengthen access to larger-scale funding.

candidates.title: R-Metaverse: multimodal social cues for real-world-centered telepresence–MR collaboration with telepresence robots
candidates.abstract: Remote collaboration in live physical workspaces requires direct access to the evolving scene and shared task information anchored to it. Telepresence provides embodied access but lacks a shared spatial interaction layer, whereas fully virtual collaboration requires reconstructing the workspace. R-Metaverse (Ritsumei Real-World Robotic Metaverse) is a telepresence–MR system design centered on the physical workspace. A remote participant operates a telepresence robot and views its camera image augmented with virtual objects through a head-mounted display (HMD), while an on-site participant views the same spatially registered virtual objects through a smartphone. The robot–mobile configuration creates viewpoint and embodiment asymmetries that can reduce social presence. Robot–robot collaboration makes partner distance and approach difficult to perceive because of robot-camera field-of-view limitations. To restore missing cues, we implement facial-expression display, motion-synchronized avatar overlay, spatially localized audio, and distance-linked vibrotactile feedback. The first three target robot–mobile collaboration; the fourth targets robot–robot collaboration. Ablation experiments show that facial-expression display improves affect understanding and closeness, while distance-linked vibrotactile feedback supports co-presence and spatial awareness under field-of-view constraints. Avatar, audio, and vibration-pattern effects are interpreted as exploratory after Holm correction. These results suggest that gap-specific multimodal cues can partially compensate for reduced social presence in real-world-centered telepresence–MR collaboration.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Anthropomorphism and Emotional Affiliation Needs among Young Adults
candidates.abstract: The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into interpersonal communication has transformed the dynamics of emotional relationships between humans and digital technologies. This study examines the relationship between AI anthropomorphism and emotional affiliation needs among young adults, focusing on perceived social presence, emotional attachment, and AI-mediated companionship. Employing a qualitative library research approach, the study thematically synthesizes 35 scholarly publications published between 2018 and 2026. The findings suggest that humanlike communication, personalized responses, and perceived emotional responsiveness may strengthen social presence and facilitate emotional attachment. Such interactions may provide perceived emotional support, particularly for individuals experiencing loneliness or unmet affiliation needs. However, intensive emotional engagement may also contribute to dependence, unrealistic relational expectations, and psychological vulnerability following the disruption of AI companionship. This study develops a conceptual synthesis integrating anthropomorphism, social presence, emotional attachment, and affiliation needs to explain the dynamics of human–AI emotional relationships. Further empirical investigation is needed to validate this framework among young adults.

candidates.title: Baby-schema-related cues shape moral expectations about decision-makers: evidence from names, faces, and AI avatars
candidates.abstract: People routinely form expectations about how others will behave in morally difficult situations, and such expectations guide consequential decisions, including whom to trust, hire, or delegate responsibility to. The present research examined whether baby-schema-related cues systematically bias these moral predictions. Across three experiments with Chinese university students (total N = 858), we tested three manifestations of baby-schema-related cues that share the function of evoking infant-like associations: repeated two-syllable names (Experiment 1), babyfaced appearance (Experiment 2), and visually cute artificial intelligence (AI) avatar designs (Experiment 3). Participants consistently perceived decision-makers displaying baby-schema-related cues as less likely to make utilitarian choices involving direct harm to others. The results show that superficially irrelevant social cues can bias moral expectations about others, although the underlying psychological mechanism remains to be clarified. These findings are relevant to moral psychology, person perception, and the design and evaluation of AI systems.

candidates.title: AI vs. AI: An AI-Enabled Conversational Intervention to Inoculate Against AI-Generated Fake News
candidates.abstract: Abstract Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is a double-edged sword that can be used to amplify the proliferation of highly sophisticated fake news as well as to fight it. In this work, we explore a new route: using one AI to inoculate humans against fake news generated by another AI. Motivated by psychological inoculation theory, we created ‘Alex’, a conversational AI agent that engages users in an adaptive conversational dialogue designed to build cognitive resilience against AI-generated, AI-related fake news. We tested its efficacy in a Solomon four-group experiment with 542 participants. The results of a 2 × 2 ANOVA show a significant main effect of the intervention on participants’ discrimination of true and false headlines, with no significant evidence of pretest sensitization. We show that AI can be designed as a scalable, interactive conversational intervention for delivering psychological inoculation against AI-generated, AI-related fake news.

candidates.title: Virtual idol consumption among Generation Z: exploring fandom motivations, engagement behavior, and marketing implications
candidates.abstract: Virtual idols have rapidly gained worldwide popularity among young people and have become a significant marketing tool for promoting brands and expanding market reach. Grounded in Self-Determination Theory (SDT), this study conducted in-depth interviews to explore motivations, engagement behavior, and consumption patterns underlying Generation Z’s virtual idol fandom. The findings reveal that virtual idol fandom is shaped by both intrinsic and attribute-driven motivations. Within the fandom, engagement with and consumption of virtual idols are driven by overlapping motivational pathways combining emotional involvement, relational control, technology fascination, and community participation. Where community participation is involved, virtual idol fandom extends beyond individual engagement into a socio-technical ecosystem shaped by user agency, platform affordances, and regulatory oversight. At the same time, virtual idol fans seek emotional involvement while pursuing a ‘secure distance’ that preserves psychological boundaries and relational control. This study develops an SDT-informed interpretive framework that reconfigures diverse motivations within contemporary virtual idol fandom. By mapping distinct fan-as-consumer profiles, this study offers practical implications for the scalability of digital persona-led industries and insights for brands seeking to leverage the visibility and influence of virtual idols for targeted promotion among young consumers, enhanced brand value creation, and sustainable expansion in global markets.

candidates.title: A Survey on AI-Based Household Robots Focusing on Voice Assistance, Smart Kitchen Support, Home Monitoring and Autonomous Navigation
candidates.abstract: The proposed system places a Raspberry Pi at the centre, connected to a microphone, speaker, display, camera, ultrasonic sensors, a motor driver and a wheeled base. A conversational AI layer interprets natural-language requests, while obstacle detection, emergency stop and motor time-outs are kept in local safety logic outside the AI loop. Design considerations, a proposed function-to-module mapping, safety logic and an evaluation plan are presented.

candidates.title: A Two Timescale Probabilistic State-Space Framework for Multimodal Affect Estimation and Uncertainty Aware Expressive Behavior in Humanoid Robots: A Monte Carlo Simulation Study
candidates.abstract: Abstract Humanoid robots intended for care, education and collaboration are expected to perceive human affect and respond appropriately, yet published systems often map momentary classifier outputs directly to robot expressions, discarding uncertainty, temporal structure and the asymmetric informativeness of sensing channels. This paper formulates affect transfer from human to robot as a Bayesian state-estimation and constrained-control problem. A six-dimensional latent state couples fast emotion and slow mood in pleasure–arousal–dominance (PAD) space; physiological, facial and vocal channels enter through modality-specific linear-Gaussian observation models; a sequential Kalman filter with a chi-square innovation gate fuses them under intermittent dropout and outliers; and an uncertainty-weighted, rate-limited mapping converts the posterior into robot display commands. The framework is evaluated entirely in synthetic Monte Carlo simulation (200 trials, 120 s each) under explicitly stated assumptions; no human-subject data are used. Under nominal conditions the gated fused filter reached an overall PAD RMSE of 0.151, against 0.257 for smoothed late fusion and 0.243 for a face-only filter. A 2 factorial study (R2 = 0.862) showed that gating helps only when outliers are present and slightly harms accuracy otherwise. Confidence scaling with λ = 2 cut display jitter by 81% and wrong-sign valence displays by 42% at a 32% tracking-error cost. The contribution is a reproducible, falsifiable baseline that must next be tested on recorded human data.

candidates.title: Attentional territories: The influence of gaze and interpersonal distance in the navigation of public space
candidates.abstract: Human gaze is a potent social signal; it communicates attention, intention and social engagement, and allows observers to infer not only where others are attending but also how they are socially related. Although gaze has been extensively studied in direct social interaction, far less is known about how it shapes the perceptions and actions of uninvolved observers in shared environments. Here, we investigate whether mutual gaze creates an 'attentional territory' that third parties implicitly respect. In a large-scale field study across four university campuses in Europe and Canada (N = 4680 pedestrians), two confederates stood facing one another in a public space. We manipulated gaze direction and reciprocity (mutual, unilateral or no interaction) as well as interpersonal distance (2-6 metres), holding body orientation and spatial arrangement constant. Pedestrians were less likely to cross between individuals engaged in mutual gaze. This effect weakened with increasing distance, but was robust across all locations. Together, the findings demonstrate that gaze does not merely coordinate interaction between individuals but also shapes how uninvolved others perceive and move through shared environments. By isolating gaze reciprocity from spatial arrangement, we demonstrate that mutual gaze functions as a dynamic social boundary organizing the permeability of public space.

candidates.title: What craft-makers know, and what they need: mapping skills and learning preferences across European craft-ecosystems
candidates.abstract: This article investigates which skills contemporary craft-makers consider most relevant, which they prefer to develop or outsource, and how these preferences reflect different educational contexts. We conducted fieldwork in four European craft ecosystems (Bassano del Grappa, Venice, Dals Långed, Bornholm) through interviews, an online questionnaire, and three co-creation workshops. We develop a framework comprising five skill areas: craft-making and technical, technological, business, communication and selling, and transversal skills. Our findings reveal how craft-making is shaped by a complex interplay between the primacy of craft-making skills, the uneasy yet unavoidable role of managerial and communication skills, and persistent tensions around technology and sustainability. Craft-makers generally prefer to develop making and transversal skills while outsourcing business and administrative activities. Learning is also constrained by limited time, and economic precarity, while national educational systems shape distinct career pathways and skill needs, requiring context-sensitive policy support.

candidates.title: When loneliness amplifies the risk of problematic emotional dependence: perceived anthropomorphism and basic psychological need satisfaction in AI companion use
candidates.abstract: Background Companion-oriented conversational AI can be experienced as socially responsive, yet evidence about problematic reliance requires construct clarity and noncausal interpretation. This study examined whether perceived anthropomorphism was associated with problematic AI-companion dependence directly and indirectly through basic psychological need satisfaction. Methods A cross-sectional online survey was completed by 666 adults in China who reported using a listed AI companion or conversational AI product during the preceding month. The nonclinical outcome was operationalized with six indicators spanning impaired control, distress, continued use, perceived understanding, emotion-regulation reliance, and displacement of offline communication. Measurement evidence was examined using reliability estimates, one-factor confirmatory models, and HTMT. Standardized composite-score regressions used HC3 robust standard errors, and the indirect association was evaluated with 5,000 bootstrap samples. Results Perceived anthropomorphism was positively associated with need satisfaction ( β = 0.569, p < 0.001). In the outcome model, need satisfaction ( β = 0.317, p < 0.001) and perceived anthropomorphism ( β = 0.385, p < 0.001) were both positively associated with problematic dependence. The standardized indirect association was 0.180 (95% bootstrap CI [0.137, 0.229]); R 2 was 0.323 for need satisfaction and 0.389 for problematic dependence. Conclusion The pattern is consistent with a need-satisfaction account of companion-oriented AI use, but the cross-sectional design does not establish temporal ordering, substitution, or causality. Design and policy implications should therefore focus on transparency, user agency, and safeguards against escalating reliance rather than treating anthropomorphism itself as inherently harmful.

candidates.title: Apertus 1.5: From Open Text Models to Open Multimodal Reasoners
candidates.abstract: Language models are becoming infrastructure, and infrastructure built in the open, by public institutions, on documented data, is the alternative to dependence on a few providers; Apertus shows this is viable at scale. Apertus 1.5 extends the fully open Apertus family from text to multimodal reasoning. Continued pretraining of the Apertus 1.0 models, on 4T additional tokens for the 8B and 2T for the 70B, adds image and audio understanding and extends the context window fourfold to 262,144 tokens; multimodality enters through the tokenizer, the language-model head remains restricted to text, and the architecture is unchanged. Supervised finetuning, long-context finetuning, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, and preference alignment complete the released models. Thinking is a flag of the chat template rather than a separate model, and lifts mathematical reasoning by up to 20 points on the 8B model. The released models improve over their predecessors on nearly every benchmark; among fully open models of its class, the 8B leads on knowledge, instruction following, and cultural benchmarks, and its instruction following surpasses all compared models, including open-weight ones. On image and audio understanding, a first for the family, the models are competitive with fully open multimodal models, strongest on document understanding and long-form and lower-resource speech recognition, while specialized vision and audio models remain ahead on perception and transcription of English and other high-resource languages. As in Apertus 1.0, we train only on openly available data, respect crawler opt-outs retroactively, and exclude restrictively licensed material. We release the model weights, data preparation and training recipes, and evaluation suites under permissive licenses; openness extends to values, with the Apertus charter guiding alignment stages published alongside the models.

candidates.title: Using photo-elicitation interviews to explore the experiences of social media influencers with visible differences: “I didn’t mean to become a voice for our whole community”
candidates.abstract: Some individuals with visible differences (conditions or injuries that affect one's appearance), have become social media influencers, using their platforms to share experiences, challenge stereotypes, and promote representation of appearance diversity. However, no research has explored their experiences and how they navigate this evolving role. Therefore, semi-structured photo-elicitation interviews were carried out with fourteen adult influencers (aged 18-45) with a range of visible differences to understand their experiences. Social media posts from their own accounts were used to facilitate the discussion. The sample included nine cisgender women, one trans woman, and four cisgender men. All participants used Instagram, 11 used TikTok, nine Facebook, and three YouTube, with follower counts ranging from 4300 to 300,000. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis within a critical realist/contextualist framework. Three themes were generated: (1) 'You've got to create your own seat at the table', (2) 'Feeling an endless pressure to influence', and (3) 'There is no handbook for this job'. Social media provided opportunities to increase visibility of visible differences, foster connection, and influence public perceptions. However, participants described continuous pressure to produce content, remain visible, and support their communities while protecting their own wellbeing. As influencing is a new and evolving role, they often balanced authenticity, social responsibility, and financial sustainability without formal guidance. Influencers with visible differences play an important role in representation and advocacy of appearance diversity but face unique challenges. Findings underscore the need for clearer guidance, regulation, and support to promote safe, sustainable, and socially responsible influencing.

candidates.title: Bespoke Visual Assistance: What and How do Blind and Low-Vision People Create with Agentic Programming?
candidates.abstract: AI-powered assistive technologies have long supported blind and low vision (BLV) people in everyday tasks, but they are general-purpose and often fall short of meeting complex, individualized, in-situ accessibility needs. Though agentic programming tools, like GitHub Copilot, have the potential to bridge this gap by lowering the technical barriers to building personal AT using natural language, the practical applicability of this creation paradigm has been unknown. We address this knowledge gap through a two-phase longitudinal co-design study with five tech-savvy BLV users using ProgramAT, an agentic programming tool that supports the creation, iteration, and testing of camera-based AT. Overall, co-designers created over 37 tools, with some addressing needs unmet by any existing commercial AT—such as identifying Uber rides or interpreting hand gestures. Qualitative feedback from our co-designers and analysis of development logs surface BLV strategies for tool creation, along with key challenges including model capability limits, specification conflicts, and barriers to successful creation. We discuss recommendations to provide appropriate conversational scaffolding, community tool sharing capabilities, and support for specialized models and personal datasets for future agentic programming environments to empower BLV users to create bespoke visual assistance for themselves.

candidates.title: Why Large Language Models will Never be Embodied: A Categorical, Not Engineering, Impossibility
candidates.abstract: Abstract A persistent ambition in artificial intelligence research holds that large language models (LLMs) will eventually become embodied—through attachment to robots, augmentation with multimodal sensors, integration into vision–language–action architectures, or sheer scale until grounding emerges from training data. This ambition rests on a misunderstanding of embodiment. Embodiment is a constitutive condition of being a self-producing, self-maintaining living system whose continued existence is genuinely at stake in its couplings with the environment. Adding sensors, actuators, or physical instantiation to a computational substrate yields engineered coupling, which is something else entirely. We identify five conditions that any genuinely embodied system must satisfy—autopoietic closure, precariousness, constructive self-determination, intrinsic temporality, and mereological closure—and show that no computational artifact can satisfy any of them, let alone all five. The barrier is categorical incompatibility: the same property that makes a system computational (heteronomous design and maintenance through external specification) is the property that precludes it from being embodied. Coupling artifacts to environments through transducers achieves engineered interaction. Having a body and being a body are different conditions. We close by examining why the embodiment-equivalence claim persists despite its categorical impossibility, and by arguing that the confusion sustains two harms—overselling AI systems for tasks they cannot perform, and misdirecting public concern toward speculative futures while the actual harms of deployed systems accumulate without being addressed. Clarifying the categorical distinction is a precondition for taking the genuine stakes of AI deployment seriously rather than as a philosophical aside.

candidates.title: アニメを通して学ぶ中級の日本語 Learning Intermediate Japanese through Anime
candidates.abstract: Learning Intermediate Japanese through Anime builds Japanese learners’ linguistic proficiency while deepening their cultural and historical understanding of anime. Designed around anime-themed readings, dialogues, and activities, the textbook helps learners develop skills in reading, writing, listening, and speaking as they explore anime as a significant artistic and cultural form. The book is structured around eight key topics: the origins of anime, the anime industry, anime as technology, anime as design, anime as genre, anime as language, gods of anime, and anime fandom. Each lesson focuses on a different language skill such as describing historical events in the passive voice, interpreting and presenting data, explaining processes, describing visual and narrative elements, summarizing information, forming arguments, making comparisons, and expressing opinions. Through this integrated approach, learners gain both practical Japanese language skills and a critical framework for understanding anime as a dynamic and influential part of Japanese culture. This textbook is intended for students of Japanese language at the intermediate high to advanced low level on the ACTFL proficiency scale and CEFR level B1 to B2. Accompanying online resources include audio recordings of readings from the book and sample grammar worksheets to facilitate classroom planning. These materials can be accessed at www.routledge.com/9781041089636 .

candidates.title: Personality expression and perception in large language models and humans
candidates.abstract: Abstract Growing numbers of people frequently turn to Large Language Models (LLMs) for concerns from various areas of life. Because its content has become ubiquitous, examining user perceptions of LLM-produced text and its distinguishability from human writing is crucial. This study investigated how seven LLMs (ChatGPT-4o, ChatGPT-3.5, Llama 3, Gemma, Gemini, Phi-3, Orca-2) describe themselves when compared to humans. LLM-generated outputs and human responses were collected using psychological questionnaires (Big Five, self-esteem, narcissism) and tailored prompts to elicit short self-descriptive texts. Six LLM and ten human judges then evaluated personality traits and text origin based on these self-descriptions (140 total, half LLM-generated). Results show that current LLM outputs can convey personality-consistent cues in questionnaires and texts. The perception of such significantly differed from that of humans. Both LLM and human judges accurately inferred personality from short self-descriptions and correctly differentiated between LLM-generated and human text. Linguistic analysis and participant feedback revealed textual cues distinguishing LLM-produced from human language and offered insights into how LLM versus human judgment and decisionmaking differ.

candidates.title: A sociolinguistic analysis of automatic speech recognition bias in Newcastle English
The Effect of AI Virtual Influencers on Purchase Intention: The Mediating Role of Parasocial Interaction: A Field Study on the Fashion Industry in Egypt
candidates.abstract: The objective of this study is to investigate the effect of AI virtual influencers (VIs); in terms of perceived authenticity and perceived anthropomorphism on Purchase intention, viewing the mediating role of Parasocial interaction, by application on the women fashion industry in Egypt. Questionnaire was used to collect data, and a non-probability purposive sampling technique was adopted. A total of 128 responses were collected and analyzed. Partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) was performed in R using the SEMinR package (version 2.5.0). The findings supported all the proposed direct and indirect hypotheses, concluding that perceived authenticity and anthropomorphism play a vital role in directly influencing purchase intention, and that parasocial interaction also plays an indirect role in mediating this relationship.

candidates.title: Federated Learning for Official Statistics: A Systematic Review of Privacy‐Preserving Architectures and the Path Toward GSBPM Integration
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT National Statistical Offices (NSOs) face an escalating “privacy‐utility” impasse, where the demand for high‐granularity data must compete with the near zero risk tolerance of legal frameworks like the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Traditional centralized collection creates “honeypots” for breaches, exposing a nation's entire digital census or tax records. This paper provides a systematic review of Federated Learning (FL) as a decentralized framework that eliminates raw microdata consolidation. Drawing on 77 peer‐reviewed. Studies and technical reports published between 2020 and 2026, the study evaluates Horizontal and Vertical FL architectures alongside Privacy‐Enhancing Technologies (PETs). The analysis reveals that while PETs introduce a “utility gap,” Under controlled experimental settings and standardized non‐IID configurations, the evaluated architectures frequently achieve utility bounds exceeding 90% of their centralized equivalents, though this outcome varies based on the assigned privacy budget () and data distribution. Crucially, the study demonstrates that the mathematical noise required for Differential Privacy (DP) can threaten strict accuracy thresholds; for example, an aggressive privacy budget can cause census distributions to shift more than 77% from the true mean, rendering indicators like Gross Domestic Product (GDP) or unemployment rates statistically meaningless. Beyond these accuracy trade‐offs, the paper addresses the Non‐Independent and Identically Distributed (Non‐IID) nature of government datasets and identifies research gaps in standardized audit trails. The paper proposes a novel roadmap for integrating FL into the Generic Statistical Business Process Model (GSBPM), offering NSOs and international statistical bodies a technically grounded and legally coherent pathway toward next generation data infrastructure.

candidates.title: Crafting Persuasive Environmental Messages for Virtual Influencers: The Role of Anthropomorphic Conversational Style, Persuasion Appeal, and Behavioral Context
candidates.abstract: The use of virtual influencers (VIs) has emerged as an alternative to human influencers for marketing initiatives. Prior studies have focused primarily on the visual characteristics of VIs and their use in advertising settings, with limited attention given to their capacity to drive pro-environmental behaviors (PEBs). We have developed an integrated persuasive framework, grounded in the Elaboration Likelihood Model and Congruity Theory, that links VI characteristics, message appeals, and behavioral context to persuasion outcomes. Study 1 examined VI message strategies and found that competence (vs. warmth) anthropomorphic conversational style and influencing (vs. de-influencing) appeal enhanced message persuasiveness. Study 2 explored the effectiveness of VIs in promoting plastic waste reduction behaviors across different behavioral contexts and found that messages pertaining to difficult (vs. easy) and private (vs. public) behaviors significantly enhanced message persuasiveness, but that messages promoting easy and private behaviors generated stronger behavioral intentions. The insights from these studies can provide valuable guidance to businesses, marketers, and environmental advocates on effective VI message strategies for addressing challenges related to climate change.

candidates.title: Sensorium: An Open-Source Multimodal Data Collection and Curation Library for Embodied Surgical AI
candidates.abstract: Embodied surgical AI requires reliable multimodal data, yet surgical data collection remains costly, difficult to repeat, and strongly dependent on the hardware setup. We present Sensorium, an open-source Python library for recording, processing, annotating, and curating multimodal surgical data from configurable robot and sensor streams using the Robot Operating System (ROS) and ROS2 middleware. The library combines operator-facing data acquisition, configurable processing, semantic annotation, and episodic dataset generation. We evaluate Sensorium across 1516 recordings of phantom, ex vivo, and in vivo porcine experiments involving multiple surgical tasks and sensing configurations, and report preliminary usability feedback.

candidates.title: Gaze-Assisted Supervisory Control for Lunar Robotic Arm Teleoperation Under Concurrent Monitoring
candidates.abstract: Rover-mounted robotic arms can extend human reach during lunar sample handling, but continuous joystick teleoperation requires repeated visual-motor alignment while operators may also need to monitor system states. This paper presents a gaze-assisted supervisory control framework in which gaze nominates a rock or placement target, explicit confirmation authorizes the action, and the robot performs bounded autonomous grasp-and-place execution. The framework was evaluated against manual joystick teleoperation in a mission-analog virtual reality study with 16 participants. The study used a 2 x 2 x 3 within-subject design varying control mode, placement difficulty, and concurrent monitoring load. Mean recorded task completion time decreased from 47.65 to 18.43 s per rock, with 72.5% of this difference arising during grasping. Under the tested auditory monitoring conditions, gaze-assisted supervisory control showed less average proportional slowing, with no detected control-mode difference in monitoring-response accuracy or speed. The rate of gaze shifts between core areas of interest decreased from 49.98 to 27.73 shifts/min, while the raw NASA Task Load Index score decreased from 32.54 to 18.26. However, the benefit was task dependent. In precision placement, manual control yielded lower mean placement error and a higher placement success rate. These findings support a mixed-initiative allocation in which gaze enables rapid task-level intention specification and autonomous execution, while precision-critical stages retain manual refinement.

candidates.title: Making Meets Informal Innovation: Formalisation, Access and Openness in Indian Makerspaces
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Makerspaces and fabrication labs (fablabs) are inclusive and open infrastructures. They democratise access to tools and technologies and facilitate bottom‐up innovation. Research on these spaces thus highlights the importance of openness, community orientation and the ability to foster informal experimentation that these spaces enable. In this paper, I examine how these features have been operationalised in contexts characterised by a high degree of economic and institutional informality by focusing specifically on Indian makerspaces and fablabs. I ask how these spaces relate to need‐driven local innovation practices and how they are sustained. The paper uses qualitative data collected through semi‐structured interviews and analyses the organisation of access, learning and innovation in these spaces. The analysis indicates that makerspaces and fablabs in India do not work as open infrastructures in their entirety. Instead, they serve as mediators between informal innovation practices and institutionalised pathways shaped by an entrepreneurial discourse. The analysis further indicates that they create new limits of participation, expertise and knowledge exchange. The paper contributes to the body of literature on open infrastructures and informal innovations by reconceptualising the notion of openness as a result of governance rather than as a characteristic of such spaces.

candidates.title: Emotional and behavioral asymmetries in user responses to virtual versus human influencers
candidates.abstract: As AI virtual influencers (AIVIs) proliferate, understanding human-AI emotional engagement is vital for advancing affective computing. To examine whether AIVIs evoke comparable affective responses to human influencers (HIs), we analyzed 156,918 Instagram comments that received 12+ million likes, integratinglarge language model (LLM)-derived knowledge graphs, emotion analysis, and machine learning. HI-directed discourse shows more differentiated emotional expression and a pattern consistent with more cohesive semantic networks than AIVI-directed discourse. AIVI-directed comments are less likely to express positive affect (24.8% vs. 41.5%) and also less likely to express negative affect (5.8% vs. 9.3%), indicating reduced affective expression of either valence rather than heightened negativity. This group-level tendency is not uniform: affective engagement varies substantially across AIVIs, and that variation is more closely associated with positive than with negative expression. Our Multi-Signal Embedding Network (MSEN), incorporating behavioral metrics and OpenAI semantic embeddings, classified influencer types from behavioral, affective and semantic features (F1 = 0.89), outperforming baselines including a state-of-the-art zero-shot LLM. These findings identify a boundary condition for the Computers Are Social Actors (CASA) paradigm: human-like appearance can elicit social responses without producing affective and semantic response patterns as rich as those elicited by HIs.

candidates.title: From digital shadows to assured intervention: a systematic review of embodiment, authority, and assurance in manufacturing quality digital twins
candidates.abstract: Abstract Rapid advances in AI and robotics are extending manufacturing digital twins beyond passive monitoring to closed-loop control and physical intervention. Yet in manufacturing QA, the term “digital twin” is used for both systems that only observe and systems that act on the physical process. This distinction matters because once a digital twin acts, model validity is no longer enough; the intervention must also be authorized, bounded, traceable, and verified. Existing maturity frameworks capture connectivity and automation but give less attention to the assurance requirements that arise when digital-twin outputs are translated into physical action. We address this gap by introducing an Embodiment-Authority-Assurance (EAA) framework that distinguishes how quality information leads to physical action, who has authority over that action, and how the intervention is assured. We apply the framework to a systematic review of 235 manufacturing QA studies, selected from 868 publications identified through Scopus and Web of Science between 2017 and 2026, classifying them across five maturity levels from digital shadows to governed adaptive QA twins. We found that the frontier of manufacturing QA digital twins is shifting from monitoring and advisory support toward human-approved and bounded autonomous intervention, with higher-maturity applications becoming increasingly visible in recent years. Yet these advances remain fragmented across the literature, with no reviewed study bringing them together into a fully assured intervention chain. By revealing this shift, our study reframes manufacturing QA digital-twin maturity around a new frontier: not simply whether digital twins can act, but whether increasingly autonomous interventions can be governed and assured.
