candidates.title: Neither queer, nor just a transaction: realignment speech and the pursuit of heteronormative intelligibility in otome cosplay commissions
candidates.abstract: The commercial rise of Chinese otome games has birthed a novel gig economy: ‘cosplay commissions’, where female fans hire female cosplayers to enact fictional romances. Drawing on 32 in-depth interviews, this study explores the tension in this novel fan practice: while the practice enables participants to experiment with a feminized, consumer-driven model of intimacy, where women actively orchestrate their ideal romance, it simultaneously triggers anxieties about violating scripts of heteronormativity. To manage these tensions, participants collaboratively enact a ‘sanitized romance’ through relational work that meticulously curates idealized heteronormative romance scripts (caring, pampering, and exclusivity), compensating for the perceived failures of real-world masculinity. More importantly, to secure moral legitimacy within China’s patriarchal constraints, participants produce what we term realignment speech, drawing symbolic boundaries to distance themselves from any association with sex work, queerness, or moral deviance. Through this boundary work, they reframe their actions not as ‘buying love’ or ‘loving a woman’, but as ‘immersing in pure love fantasy’. We argue that this ambivalent mode of intimacy – transgressive in practice yet normatively policed in self-understanding – demonstrates how realignment speech renders female desire intelligible and thus survivable within a rigid moral economy through both micro-resistance to dominant norms and creative reappropriation of their toolkit.

candidates.title: Understanding Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption: Practices, Challenges, and Evolution in Open-Source Software
candidates.abstract: Post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards establish algorithms for quantum-safe systems, but empirical evidence about how software projects implement and maintain PQC support remains limited. We investigate this implementation and maintenance work by mining 114,361 commits and 5,713 issues across 179 open-source repositories. We use human annotation and validated LLM classification to identify PQC algorithms in commits, classify their adoption status and deployment mode, and identify technical challenges in issue discussions. The commit classification for PQC algorithms reveals that 90% of commits concern maintenance of existing support. From the issue discussions, we construct an 11-category taxonomy of recurring technical challenges. Build, packaging, and dependency failures, along with functional defects, account for approximately half of categorized issues. To examine how PQC support evolves, we use time-series analysis and first implementations of individual algorithms within repositories around NIST standardization milestones. After the 2024 finalization, standardized algorithm names appeared in more than 80% of the PQC development changes analyzed, although earlier names such as Kyber continued to appear. Development activity increased over the observation period. Our milestone analysis, however, did not find a significant increase in first implementations. Migration plans should therefore account for sustained maintenance, prioritize build reliability and integration testing, and track both standardized and predecessor algorithm names. We make the dataset, taxonomy, annotations, and analysis pipeline publicly available.

candidates.title: Beyond Being Accurate: Implications for Using Natural Language Descriptions for Accessible 3D Modeling with~Blind and Low Vision Makers
candidates.abstract: People who are blind or have low vision (BLV) are largely excluded from 3D modeling tools that rely on visual representations of geometry. Natural language descriptions offer a potential path to accessibility, but it is unclear whether language alone can support the deep spatial understanding that editing, not just browsing, requires. Advances in generative AI offer the promise of automatic model description, yet descriptions suited to BLV modelers are structurally distinct from alt-text and from existing 3D model captioning datasets, and the domain-specific requirements for generating them are not well understood. We address this through two coordinated studies: an autoethnographic pilot in which the blind first author worked with 12 sighted participants to develop a taxonomy of descriptive strategies, and a Wizard-of-Oz main study that applied those strategies as idealized scripts with 10 BLV participants. We identify a systematic use-to-editing gap: descriptions that support accurate but incomplete mental models are insufficient for specifying modifications, because editing requires knowing the state of features the user did not know to ask about. We show that this gap produces four failure types (accuracy, completeness, expression, and navigation) that accuracy-focused evaluation frameworks cannot detect. We propose a two-phase evaluation framework that diagnoses the failure type a description system exhibits and guides developers toward targeted design interventions, thereby providing a methodological standard for assessing whether description-based systems genuinely support BLV modelers as creators.

candidates.title: Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning for Dyadic Relationship Recognition
candidates.abstract: Dyadic relationship recognition aims to identify the latent social relationship between two individuals from their multimodal interactions. Existing methods typically project heterogeneous cues into a shared representation and optimise a flat classification objective, overlooking that relationships may rely on different interaction patterns. For instance, distant relationships can often be inferred from direct behavioural correspondence, whereas close relationships are better reflected by coordinated affective, behavioural, and multimodal responses. To address this limitation, we propose HiRe-DRR, a Hierarchical Multimodal Interaction Reasoning framework that organises relationship evidence from three complementary perspectives: feature level, interaction type, and relationship hierarchy. HiRe-DRR decomposes facial, bodily, acoustic, and textual cues into low- and high-level representations and constructs homogeneous and heterogeneous cross-participant interactions. We further introduce the Mixture-of-Interaction Transformer (MoI-Former), which treats diverse interactions as specialised experts and employs relation-aware sparse routing to identify relationship-relevant evidence while preserving contextual interaction information. The proposed Hierarchical Conditional Loss (HC-Loss) exploits the hierarchical nature of social relationships through coarse-to-fine supervision, enabling structured relationship reasoning. Extensive experiments on three dyadic relationship benchmarks demonstrate that HiRe-DRR outperforms recent representative image-, video-, and multimodal methods. Our routing analysis further reveals that distant relationships tend to rely on low-level homogeneous interactions, whereas closer relationships focus on high-level heterogeneous interactions. Our code is publicly available at: https://github.com/tw-repository/HiRe-DRR.

candidates.title: Editorial: Computational multimodal sensing and perception for robotic systems
candidates.abstract: Each sensor captures its own slice of the physical world. For robots working in complex and dynamic 2 environments, robust perception requires integrating complementary information from multiple sensory 3 modalities. Vision may provide global context, while tactile, auditory, event-based, and other emerging 4 sensing technologies can reveal more interaction details that are difficult to obtain by vision alone. Together, 5 these modalities can support more robust and adaptive robotic behaviors. candidates.title: From Decision-Maker to Decision Architect: Generative AI and the Changing Role of Leadership
candidates.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is becoming an integral part of managerial work, changing how leaders analyse information, communicate, coordinate, and decide. Much of the existing leadership literature emphasizes productivity effects or debates substitution versus augmentation. We argue that the more fundamental leadership challenge is the reconfiguration of decision authority and the design of decision processes across human–AI arrangements. As GenAI systems become more capable, context-aware, and agentic, leadership becomes less about individual judgement and more about structuring how judgement is distributed across human and AI actors. This conceptual paper asks how GenAI changes leadership decision-making in contemporary organizations. Drawing on research on algorithmic management, the automation–augmentation paradox, AI-mediated leadership, and principal–agent perspectives on AI agents, we develop a framework that positions leaders as decision architects, i.e., actors who deliberately design and govern decision processes rather than merely participate in them. The main contribution of the paper is a typology of four roles GenAI can have in leadership decision making, distinguished by the degree of AI autonomy and the locus of decision authority: AI as assistant, AI as advisor, AI as oversight partner, and AI as delegated actor. For each role, we discuss implications for decision rights, employee autonomy, and managerial expertise. We further argue that the agentic AI highlights classical delegation problems of goal alignment, information asymmetries, and control, turning governance decisions into a core leadership concern. By focusing on design of human–AI decision architectures, the paper contributes to leadership and organization literature by clarifying how GenAI can change concepts of authority, control, and legitimacy in contemporary organizations. We outline a research agenda on AI-augmented leadership capabilities, responsible delegation to AI agents, and the conditions under which GenAI can improve leadership legitimacy.

candidates.title: Towards Enhanced Psychosocial Well-Being for Persons Living with Dementia: An Integrative Review of Meaningful Activities in Long-Term Care
candidates.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Meaningful engagement in clinical interventions or technology-mediated activities can support the psychosocial well-being of persons living with dementia. However, meaningfulness is often assumed rather than explicitly conceptualized in both academic context and in care practice.OBJECTIVES: This review aims to examine how interventions and activity provision can support psychosocial well-being and how meaningful engagement is shaped by the conditions surrounding their provision, with particular attention to people with moderate and advanced dementia in long-term care facilities. METHODS: An integrative review was conducted through article searching in databases including PubMed, Scopus, and the ACM Digital Library dated from 2014 through 2025. In this review, 60 publications were synthesized for answering proposed objectives and questions.RESULTS: We identified six activity forms and five recurring mechanisms through which activities acquire psychosocial value and are considered meaningful. The central finding is that meaningfulness is not an inherent property of an intervention or technology-mediated activity. It was shaped by the changing relationship between the person, activity, other stakeholders, and care environment. Activities are more likely to become meaningful when they connect with the person’s identity and retained abilities, permit supported forms of agency, are facilitated within responsive relationships and workable care routines.CONCLUSION: This review advances a person-centered design agenda that shifts attention from isolated interventions toward activity-care ecosystems. It extends previous intervention- and technology-centered reviews by explaining how meaningful engagement can be co-produced, evaluated, and sustained in everyday dementia care.

candidates.title: Seeing the Forest for the Trees: Emergent Agreement from Individual Conversations
candidates.abstract: As LLM agents interact in the wild and shape each other's decisions, understanding how they converge toward agreement becomes important. We study this in multi-turn conversations where two LLMs discuss subjective matters, can agree or disagree, and may change their stances. Using a linear classifier on individual conversation activations, we identify an internal representation of agreement. We find that it varies substantially across turns and conversations and does not reliably track external agreement at the individual conversation level. We therefore move beyond the representation of agreement in individual conversations, by aggregating the agreement representation across conversations. Externally, this aggregate view reveals a simple structure: when pooled across conversations, agreement can be predicted well with a Markov process, with agreement at each turn being a direct function of agreement at the previous turn. Similarly, when internal agreement is aggregated, it couples with the external Markov agreement through a power-law mapping, exposing Markovian dynamics in internal representations. Additionally, we find that after a change of stance, models express agreement externally before their internal representations reflect the same shift. These results reveal a joint structure between internal and external agreement that emerges only when internal features are aggregated across conversations. Code available at https://github.com/technion-cs-nlp/SeeingTheForestForTheTrees.

candidates.title: Hybrid optimization of multimodal SLAM for underground robots with seismic vibration geomagnetic and tactile sensing
candidates.abstract: Abstract Reliable underground SLAM remains difficult when GPS, visual features, LiDAR, or external anchors are unavailable or degraded, while non-visual sensors exhibit noise, drift, and environment-dependent uncertainty. We propose a hybrid-optimized seismic/vibration-geomagnetic-tactile SLAM framework that combines complementary sensor factors in a robust factor graph and uses staged COA-PSO-GSA optimization for automated parameter calibration. Evaluation covered 23 complete trajectories (10.2 km; approximately 7.5 h) from simulation, controlled underground corridors, and field tunnel/mine environments, with non-overlapping trajectory-level optimization, validation, and testing subsets. On the test trajectories, mean absolute trajectory error was 0.53 m, convergence occurred in approximately 37 iterations, and error growth remained between 1.81% and 4.09% under the evaluated magnetic, vibration, and tactile degradation conditions. Loop-detection AUC was 0.76, but its difference from the strongest GWO-SLAM baseline (0.74) was not statistically significant after Holm correction (adjusted p = 0.184). The measured foreground update latency was 57 ± 10 ms (approximately 17.5 Hz), indicating near-real-time online operation on the tested platform rather than hard real-time performance. These results support technical feasibility under the tested conditions, while broader claims require larger multi-site validation.

candidates.title: CollabSciReM: Aligning Language Models for Scientific Conversations via Science-Aware Reward Decomposition
candidates.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as research collaborators for hypothesis refinement, methodological planning, and technical analysis across multi-turn interactions. In this setting, a useful assistant must be accurate, methodologically justified, logically consistent, and token-efficient. Current alignment approaches rarely achieve all of these together. Instruction-tuned models gain conversational quality through verbosity, and we show that science-agnostic general collaborative rewards compress responses at the expense of scientific rigor. We propose CollabSciReM, a goal-conditioned reward framework that decomposes the session-level reward into conversational quality, scientific rigor, and structural efficiency. We also introduce SciQuality, a pairwise evaluation of multi-turn research conversations grounded in 300 held-out scientific papers and scored on six dimensions: methodological soundness, justification, logical consistency, factual correctness, novelty, and responsiveness. Fine-tuned on 8.62K synthetic research conversations, CollabSciReM is preferred on SciQuality over a science-agnostic reward baseline trained on the same data for all four Llama and Qwen models, including a 65.3% win rate at matched response length. For the 7B and 8B models, CollabSciReM outperforms the science-agnostic reward baseline on the primary metric in 8 of 10 single- and multi-turn benchmark settings. In a blind study, domain experts rated CollabSciReM significantly higher on novelty than the general-reward variant and reported fewer hallucinated responses than both the general-reward variant and the base model.

candidates.title: Remote Expert Evaluation of Tabletop Avatar Gaze Control in Asymmetric Multi-Scale MR--VR Collaboration
candidates.abstract: This paper proposes an integrated setup for a multi-scale asymmetric collaboration scenario in the context of a remote-expert use case, focusing on the expert side. In this system, the remote expert (with an exocentric view in Mixed Reality (MR)) uses a Tangible User Interface (TUI) to precisely position and rotate their avatar within a scaled tabletop World-in-Miniature (WIM). Inside the WIM, the expert's avatar and the operator share the same scale and egocentric view, while the expert retains a global tabletop overview of the plant to support collaboration. Interviews with industry experts during the participatory design phase revealed the need for an egocentric view inside the plant on the remote-expert side to enable full collaboration. We designed and studied three interaction-visualisation combinations to integrate and control the expert avatar's gaze: VR (fully immersive with direct head control), Head (floating screen with direct head control), and Touch (on-avatar screen with touchpad control). We evaluated these methods with 29 participants across two fault-detection tasks: Same Machine, where both collaborators inspect the same machine, and Twin Machine, where they inspect identical machines in separate locations. The VR condition, which combines immersion, direct head control, and a full-scale view, yielded the strongest overall performance and user experience, while the tabletop avatar setup was well received for collaboration. Our findings inform the design of gaze-control techniques for asymmetric MR-VR collaboration and reveal challenges and opportunities for future work.

candidates.title: Voice Design Compass: Guidance for Developing and Reflecting on Voice Concepts for Embodied Characters
candidates.abstract: Abstract An embodied character's voice can shape how we perceive the whole character. Nevertheless, the voice is often overlooked during the planning process, or no explanation is given as to why certain approaches were chosen. We present the Voice Design Compass, a conceptual framework for developing, reviewing, and documenting voice concepts for embodied characters. A voice concept describes how a character's voice should sound and be perceived. It provides a basis for voice selection and production. The Voice Design Compass offers questions to help designers consider early on what influences their voice choices and which unintended effects they might otherwise overlook. These questions address, for example, how a voice relates to the character's appearance, whom it might remind users of, and whether it could reinforce stereotypes.We developed a literature-informed prototype. Ten domain experts from research and industry reviewed its written questions, examples and workflow in formative think-aloud interviews. Qualitative content analysis identified experts' accounts of component relevance, process structure, potential support for design work, and reflection. Needs for change concerned missing content, wording, conceptual distinctions, ease of understanding, cognitive load, and overall organization. Experts suggested using the prototype to clarify requirements, communicate intentions, and revisit decisions across project phases, identifying researchers, practitioners, and non-experts as potential users.We used these findings to revise the prototype into the Voice Design Compass. Four work areas cover project context, voice-concept development with four modular Design Sets, review and practical testing, supporting designers in creating and maintaining their own Project Record.

candidates.title: Trade, AI-robot adoption, and manufacturing transformation: cross-national determinants of firm-level automation in heterogeneous institutional contexts
candidates.abstract: It investigates the multi-dimensional determinants of AI-driven robot adoption among manufacturing firms to examine how perceived benefits, industry peer pressure, and international trade exposure jointly shape firm-level automation decisions across heterogeneous institutional contexts during 2016–2024. Using a firm-level 12,000 manufacturer panel data, it employs PPML estimation with high-dimensional fixed effects, instrumental variables using historical tariffs and partner-country demand shocks to address trade endogeneity, and System GMM to capture dynamic adjustment. The analytical framework integrates TAM, institutional isomorphism theory, and Melitz’s heterogeneous firm model. Empirical results show the strongest adoption driver, with long-run effects nearly double short-run estimates. Industry peer pressure accelerates diffusion through competitive mimicry and network density. Trade exposure causally stimulates automation, exporters respond to quality demands, import-competing firms automate defensively. Cross-country analysis reveals Germany’s highest benefit responsiveness, Korea’s strongest peer effects, and China’s policy-coordinated balanced patterns. It provides the first integrated cross-national empirical analysis of behavioral, institutional, and trade-related automation mechanisms within a single framework, demonstrating that effective automation policy must verify benefit perceptions, industry coordination, and trade integration across diverse institutional contexts. First published online 19 October 2026

MemRevise: A Self-Revising Memory for Conversational Search
candidates.abstract: In conversational search, users correct misun-derstandings, revise their requests and return to earlier topics, so part of the history no longer reflects what they want. Existing benchmarks do not isolate such turns. Current search methods either re-read the history or keep a record of every turn, and none of them marks earlier content as dropped. We introduce CONVREVISE, a benchmark of 4,429 test questions in six tiers of returns and revisions over TopiOCQA, CORAL and OR-QuAC. We also propose MEMREVISE, which combines a revisable memory graph, a 3B writer distilled from teacher memories, and a search guided by the memory. The writer reads each turn once and adds a node that records its topic, its facts and the operations it performs, such as adding, abandoning or reactivating a topic. Topic status follows from these operations, so a dropped topic keeps its facts and can be restored. With a frozen retriever, MEMREVISE reaches a mean MRR@10 of 0.701, against 0.589 for the best competitor, ConvSearch-R1-FT, and 0.617 for a writer distilled the same way without the memory, so the memory and the steps built on it add 0.084. MEMREVISE is significantly better on Topi- OCQA and OR-QuAC, statistically tied with prompted 32B rewriters on CORAL, and never significantly behind the strongest competitor of any tier.

candidates.title: The adoption, efficacy, and limitations of large language models in urological education
candidates.abstract: The integration of large language models into medical education is rapidly transforming pedagogical approaches, particularly in specialized fields like urology. This study aims to evaluate the adoption patterns, perceived efficacy, and significant limitations of these artificial intelligence (AI) tools among urology trainees. This research employed a descriptive, cross-sectional study design through an online survey disseminated to urology trainees at a single institution. A total of 194 complete responses were collected from medical students and interns. The survey assessed adoption patterns, perceived efficacy on a 7-point Likert-scale, and limitations. The analysis revealed near-universal adoption (98.4%), with 65% of participants using AI tools daily, predominantly ChatGPT. Key applications included generating exam-style questions and summarizing complex guidelines. Participants reported significant perceived improvements in core knowledge areas, with the highest gains in disease knowledge and diagnostics (Median = 7, interquartile range: 6-7), which were strongly correlated with increased clinical confidence. Multivariate regression identified usage frequency and comfort with technology as significant predictors of knowledge improvement (β = 0.29, P = .001) and confidence gains (β = 0.30, P < .001). The primary limitation identified was the potential for AI "hallucinations" or incorrect information (54.1%). Large language models are widely adopted and perceived as highly effective for enhancing knowledge and clinical reasoning in urological education. However, their transformative potential is tempered by critical concerns regarding reliability. A balanced approach that combines these powerful AI tools with vigilant oversight is essential.

candidates.title: A Deep Learning-based Feature-level Privacy-preserving and Intrusion Detection Framework for Intelligent Cybersecurity Using Blockchain
candidates.abstract: The advent of the fast growth of interconnected digital infrastructures has increased the necessity of privacyconserving cybersecurity solutions that can detect network intrusions without revealing sensitive traffic data.Traditional intrusion detection systems (IDSs) typically analyse raw network traffic in a centralized manner, a practice that heightens the risk of data leakage and privacy breaches.This study proposes an IDS that preserves privacy at the feature level by coupling deep representation learning with encrypted, blockchain-based storage.The architecture suggested uses a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-BiLSTM) model for extracting compact and discriminative representations of network traffic flows.A multi-stage privacy pipeline comprising feature normalization, secret permutation, and AES-256-GCM encryption is proposed and empirically evaluated against membership-inference, reconstruction, and attribute-inference attacks before storage in a permissioned blockchain ledger.The suggested framework uses encrypted deep feature vectors, unlike current methods of storing raw traffic data or sharing model gradients, which significantly lowers the privacy attack surface and preserve detection.The framework was tested on four popular databases of intrusion detection, such as CICIDS2017, IoTIDS20, NSL-KDD, and TRAIN_TEST_NETWORK.Experimental results demonstrate strong detection performance, with accuracy exceeding 0.95 and reaching approximately 0.997, alongside high processing throughput and low computational overhead.The findings indicate that integrating deep feature learning, cryptographic protection, and blockchain-based storage achieves a favorable balance among privacy preservation, system efficiency, and detection accuracy.The proposed architecture could be scaled to privacy-sensitive environments, such as in IoT systems, healthcare systems, and enterprise security monitoring systems.

candidates.title: A Trust-Boundary Reference Architecture for Secure Cyber-Physical Agriculture: Design and Software-Based Proof-of-Concept for Smart Irrigation
candidates.abstract: Smart irrigation is an operational technology (OT) problem as much as an Internet of Things (IoT) one: software decisions act directly on valves, pumps, pressure and water delivery, so a spoofed reading or a replayed command has physical consequences. This paper presents a technology-neutral reference architecture that makes those consequences controllable. It is organised into seven functional layers and three cross-cutting planes, six trust-boundary classes that fix which properties must be re-established at each crossing, and an auditable crown-asset inventory with an explicit trust-level rubric. Two governing execution principles enforce this structure: local safety authority, which keeps final actuation permission at the field gateway, remote terminal unit (RTU) or programmable logic controller (PLC), and feedback-aware execution, which treats a command as complete only when independent physical feedback confirms it. Building on process-aware and safety-supervision ideas from industrial control, the architecture makes physical confirmation a mandatory completion condition at the local enforcement point, which catches a fully authorised command that is nonetheless physically unsafe, a failure mode that authorisation checks alone cannot detect. These properties are examined through a deterministic, openly available software proof-of-concept that verifies the design against its own acceptance criteria; it is not a field validation. The software executes six attack and failure scenarios plus one nominal-operation control against an intentionally unsecured negative control and a secure controller, under identical, controlled conditions: the negative control is compromised in all 6 attack scenarios and the secure controller in 0/6, with 0/1 false positives on legitimate operation. Analytically, the design costs 21 bytes and 50–60% additional Long Range Wide Area Network (LoRaWAN) time-on-air per record, and 78% of single-step perturbations of the trust-scoring inputs leave asset classification unchanged: the actuator class (A2) is completely stable, and the gateway/RTU/PLC class (A3) is stable under 6 of 7 admissible perturbations (86%), changing only when its credential/update authority reaches the trust-anchor threshold. A sensor-level mapping from sampling rate, measurement drift and physical fault modes to the edge-verification controls they dictate, provisions for secure time, counter recovery and the choice between fail-closed and fail-open safe states, an illustrative hypothetical worked deployment example, and a transfer of the model to greenhouse, fertigation, livestock-watering and cold-chain settings show how the architecture could be applied in practice.

candidates.title: Menuju Sistem AI yang Dapat Dijelaskan (XAI) untuk Pengalaman Pengguna yang Lebih Baik: Studi tentang Interaksi Multimodal pada Perangkat Cerdas untuk Pembelajaran Reflektif
candidates.abstract: Sistem Kecerdasan Buatan (AI) semakin terintegrasi dalam kehidupan sehari-hari melalui perangkat cerdas, namun kurangnya transparansi dan kemampuan menjelaskan (explainability) sering menjadi hambatan dalam membangun kepercayaan dan pengalaman pengguna yang bermakna. Penelitian ini mengkaji peran Explainable AI (XAI) dalam meningkatkan pengalaman pengguna melalui interaksi multimodal pada perangkat cerdas, dengan fokus pada bagaimana mekanisme penjelasan dapat mendukung pembelajaran reflektif. Melalui tinjauan literatur sistematis terhadap perkembangan terkini dalam XAI, interaksi multimodal, dan desain antarmuka, penelitian ini mengidentifikasi bahwa efektivitas XAI sangat bergantung pada bagaimana penjelasan disampaikan dan dikontekstualisasikan dalam pengalaman pengguna. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan multimodal menggabungkan penjelasan visual, tekstual, dan auditori meningkatkan pemahaman pengguna hingga 40% dibandingkan penjelasan unimodal, sementara penjelasan adaptif yang disesuaikan dengan tingkat keahlian pengguna meningkatkan kepercayaan dan kepuasan secara signifikan. Interaksi multimodal pada perangkat cerdas memungkinkan pengguna untuk mengeksplorasi dan memahami keputusan AI melalui berbagai saluran sensorik, mendorong pembelajaran reflektif dimana pengguna tidak hanya menerima output AI tetapi juga merefleksikan proses penalaran di baliknya. Tantangan yang masih ada mencakup trade-off antara transparansi dan kejelasan, beban kognitif dari penjelasan yang berlebihan, serta kebutuhan untuk menyeimbangkan akurasi dan interpretabilitas dalam model AI. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa XAI multimodal yang dirancang dengan mempertimbangkan kebutuhan pengguna dan konteks penggunaan dapat menjadi jembatan antara kompleksitas teknis AI dan pengalaman pengguna yang intuitif dan memberdayakan, membuka jalan menuju AI yang lebih transparan, tepercaya, dan kolaboratif.

candidates.title: Eye, Robot: Learning Expressive Gaze Dynamics via a VLM-Guided Transformer-VAE
candidates.abstract: Gaze coordinates attention in human interaction through coupled eye, head, and eyelid motion. A humanoid robot must choose where to look while generating a suitable movement toward that target; fixed tracking rules alone do not model the temporal structure of human gaze. We separate these tasks with an asynchronous vision-language model that selects a scene referent, a reactive perception module that maintains fixation, and a Realistic Gaze Transformer (RGT) that generates target-conditioned motion. RGT is a Transformer-VAE trained on markerless human recordings retargeted to the robot's 11-DoF joint space: self-supervised pretraining encodes recent full-head history, and autoregressive fine-tuning exposes the model to its own predictions during rollout. At inference, a four-dimensional binocular-eye trajectory conditions coordinated neck and eye motion; an auxiliary blink predictor triggers eyelid templates during playback. On a two-second benchmark in which all controllers receive the same ground-truth target, RGT-Base obtains the lowest reported overall seven-joint MSE, and physical demonstrations show the integrated targeting and control pipeline. The evidence establishes robot-space kinematic fidelity and real-time RGT inference; perceived naturalness and open-vocabulary target-selection accuracy remain questions for controlled evaluation.

candidates.title: Breakdown of Conversational Involvement: A Joint Multi-Modal Analysis of Conversation Floors and F-formation Detection with Multiple Features
candidates.abstract: Interactions happen universally and spontaneously in daily lives. Studying involvement in interactions helps us analyze who can influence who and has a wide potential in applications. Specifically, we consider conversational involvement in free-standing conversations. We study two operationalizations of an FCG: F-formations and conversation floors, and propose that current assumption that F-formations capture single conversations is insufficient. To illustrate how different implementations could impact the detected F-formations, we employ three analyses. First, we propose that speaking status can be used for estimating conversation floors, and leveraged it to analyze floors within F-formations. Second, we analyze spatial characteristics of the detection results by applying different feature sets on chosen baselines, and find that groups resulting from head features are more likely to be subsumed by groups detected using other features. Finally, we do a joint analysis which combines the spatial features and floor patterns in the conversation. We observe that certain pipelines can detect groups with single floors from upper body features, while retaining F-formations with lower body features. We conclude that a more detailed theory and framework is needed to holistically demonstrate conversational involvement within interactions.

candidates.title: Robotics and Trust
candidates.abstract: Imagine you would be hanging on a cliff—Would you take a robot’s hand? Though the imagination of one hanging on a cliff seems dramatic, it well demonstrates a situation of vulnerability in which a person needs to rely on another’s capability and integrity to help him or her. As the number of service robots in various fields increases enormously, see [ 74 ], it is likely that people will find themselves in situations of vulnerability in which they depend on robotic assistance. As such, robots cannot be merely regarded as tools performing repetitive tasks. Instead, robots’ role as embodied social agents that are attributed with intentions and morality gains importance. This calls for a clear understanding of trust in HRI which needs to be well distinguished from trust in automation, see [ 41 ] for a review. The best way to achieve this is to understand trust in interpersonal relationships first.

candidates.title: How Should We Evaluate Naturalness for Synthetic Speech with a Foreign Accent?
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in speech synthesis technology have enabled the generation of speech with diverse characteristics. One such characteristic is a foreign accent. In our preliminary experiments, we found that UTMOS, a widely used automatic speech quality assessment system, tended to assign lower scores to speech with stronger foreign accents, even though it is produced by a human speaker. This observation raised a question: How do humans evaluate the naturalness of foreign-accented speech? We conducted a large-scale subjective evaluation involving both native and non-native listeners under different evaluation instructions. The results showed that humans also considered accentedness when evaluating naturalness, but that defining naturalness in terms of human-likeness and selecting raters who have greater exposure to the target accent may enable more appropriate evaluation. This study aims to provide a starting point for future discussions on fairer and more appropriate evaluation of synthetic speech with a foreign accent.

candidates.title: Trust in AI-mediated electronic commerce: a systematic review and integrative framework
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence now stands between merchants and consumers across digital exchange, in chatbots, recommenders, virtual influencers, generative content, service robots and robo-advisors. Consumer reliance on that intermediary is shaped in part by trust. This review synthesises 166 studies in which trust or calibrated reliance is explicitly measured, manipulated or theorised, screened from 7,606 records under PRISMA 2020, with 45 trust-adjacent studies reported separately. Coding what is trusted shows three referents, the AI agent, the deploying merchant and the platform-institutional system, distributed non-randomly across applications. Formal testing finds no detectable association between the direction of the anthropomorphism effect and either stakes or referent, a provisional association between disclosure direction and stakes, and a strong association between reporting any boundary condition and experimental design. The resulting framework links referent, mechanism, boundary condition, trust and reliance state, outcome and repair, and reframes electronic commerce design around calibrated reliance rather than maximal trust.

candidates.title: AI BASED HAND GESTURE CONTROLLED ROBOT
candidates.abstract: The proposed system presents an advanced AI-based hand gesture controlled telepresence robot designed for operation in hazardous and inaccessible environments. The system enables a remote operator to control a robotic rover using real-time hand gestures without the need for physical controllers or wearable devices. It integrates computer vision techniques using OpenCV and MediaPipe for accurate skeletal hand tracking and gesture recognition. A dual-processing architecture ensures efficient handling of high-definition video streaming and gesture interpretation with minimal latency. The robot provides real-time visual feedback through wireless video transmission, enabling safe navigation and monitoring. The system ensures intuitive control, improved safety, and enhanced operational efficiency. This solution is highly applicable in disaster management, industrial inspection, and healthcare environments where human presence is risky or limited.

candidates.title: Implementing robotic-assisted therapy in stroke rehabilitation: a structured narrative review of evidence and technology adoption barriers in Indonesia
candidates.abstract: Introduction: Robotic-assisted therapy (RAT) has emerged as a promising intervention for post-stroke recovery; however, its implementation in developing countries such as Indonesia remains limited by economic, technical, and systemic barriers. This structured narrative review summarizes clinical effect reported by systematics review and meta-analyses and examines implementation consideration and potential economic feasibility within the Indonesian healthcare context. Method: A structured review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses (2015-2025) was conducted using PubMed, Scopus, PEDro, and Cochrane Library. Studies involving adult with stroke were included. Findings were synthesized narratively because of heterogeneity. Implementation barriers were analyzed, and a scenario-based economic model was developed to assess feasibility of RAT in Indonesia. QALY-equivalent outcomes (QEOs) were estimated using ratio-based value-transfer approach that scaled published reference values according to observed functional effects. Result: Evidence from 22 systematic reviews indicated that RAT improved functional outcomes compared with conventional therapy, particularly gait and upper-limb function (effect sizes: 0.02-0.52). Key implementation barriers included limited device availability, inadequate workforce training, and regulatory constraints. Modelled ICERs ranged from US$236.23-752.31 per QEO for upper-limb rehabilitation and US$558.86-4,890 per QEO for gait-related rehabilitation. Most estimates remained below the Indonesian willingness-to-pay threshold (<US$5,030), suggesting a favourable economic profile under model assumptions, particularly in higher-resource provinces, while lower-income regions may face affordability constraints. Conclusion: RAT shows potential clinical benefits, but implementation in Indonesia should consider clinical effectiveness, economic feasibility, infrastructure, workforce, technology acceptance, and reimbursement. A phased approach in suitable tertiary-care settings may support wider adoption based on local evidence.

candidates.title: VIP-MINGLE: A Corpus for Videoconference and In-Person Multimodal Interaction in Group Language Engagement
Beyond One-Size-Fits-All: Personalized and Culturally Adaptive Emotional TTS via Interactive Optimization of Individual Emotion Perception Spaces
BabAR: from phoneme recognition to developmental measures of young children's speech production
A study on the effects of mixed explicit and implicit communications in human-artificial-agent interactions
candidates.abstract: Abstract Communication between humans and artificial agents is essential for their interaction. This is often inspired by human communication, which uses gestures, facial expressions, gaze direction, and other explicit and implicit means. This work presents interaction experiments where humans and artificial agents interact through explicit and implicit communication to evaluate the effect of mixed explicit-implicit communication against purely explicit communication and the impact of the task difficulty in this evaluation. Results obtained using Bayesian parameter estimation show that the task execution time did not significantly change when mixed explicit and implicit communications were used in neither of our experiments, which varied in the type of artificial agent (virtual agent and humanoid robot) used and task difficulty. The number of errors was affected by the communication only when the human was executing a more difficult task, and an impact on the perceived efficiency of the interaction was only observed in the interaction with the robot, for both easy and difficult tasks. In contrast, acceptance, sociability, and transparency of the artificial agent increased when using mixed communication modalities in both our experiments and task difficulty levels. This suggests that task-related measures, such as time, number of errors, and perceived efficiency of the interaction, as well as the impact of the communication on them, are more sensitive to the type of task and the difficulty level, whereas the combination of explicit and implicit communications more consistently improves human perceptions about artificial agents.

candidates.title: A preliminary design framework for human-friendly AI interaction: grounded in anthropomorphism
candidates.abstract: People converse with AI as they would with friends in daily life, collaborate with it, and form personalized relationships. In response to these emerging forms of interaction, this study clarifies the concept of Human-Friendly Interaction with conversational AI and develops the Human-Friendly AI Interaction Design Framework (HFAI-DF). This study positions anthropomorphism, a foundational phenomenon in human–AI interaction, as a theoretical bridge and reviews literature on anthropomorphism theory and related research on human cognition. On this basis, this study interpretively derives and organizes how anthropomorphism-inducing stimuli can be applied to AI agents, systematizing them into 30 AI behavioral items that enable human-friendly interaction. Subsequently, a survey was conducted and exploratory factor analysis performed to identify six dimensions as a preliminary structure for a design framework for AI’s human-friendly interaction. These dimensions are: Self-Aware Interaction, User-Adaptive Responsiveness Interaction, Context-Aware Reasoning Interaction, Socio-Emotional Interaction, Creative Collaboration Interaction, and Proactive Assistance Interaction. Within the evolving AI research landscape focused on interaction, this study extends the human-centered AI concept toward human-friendly interaction that operates in an organic manner comparable to human–human conversation, grounded in an understanding of human cognitive functioning. The proposed framework provides both AI providers and designers with an initial structure for shaping and improving the quality of human-friendly interaction.

candidates.title: Helping Dementia Patients Find Comfort: Tom Stevens, Founder of Tombot
candidates.abstract: Inspired by his experience caring for his mother with Alzheimer's disease, entrepreneur Tom Stevens founded Tombot to create a realistic robotic companion for people with dementia and others who cannot care for a live pet. Developed with input from hundreds of seniors and animatronic expertise from Jim Henson's Creature Shop, Tombot's robotic puppy Jennie combines lifelike movement, touch response, and sound to encourage emotional attachment. In this article, Stevens discusses the engineering challenges behind Jennie, Tombot's path from startup to commercialization, and his goal of using technology to provide comfort, companionship, and improved quality of life.

candidates.title: Robots, artificial intelligence and spirituality/religiosity: a critical literacy perspective on human development
candidates.abstract: Artificial Intelligence, a natural language processing tool, connects human learning and interpretation to algorithms whose source code is hidden to us and uses linguistic modeling, a primarily statistical method, for analyzing and predicting character collocation patterns (Peters et al, 2023, p. 14). Humans willingly have given in to the charms of a “superior” technological cognition that is incapable, in fact, of thinking critically. In this article we aim at presenting the introduction of the use of AI in spiritual/religious spaces from the perspective of critical literacy (Freire, 1974, 1989, 2005, 2015). Thinking in terms of critical literacy allows for a flexibility of the emergence of meanings from diverse loci of enunciation and it enhances social justice. Drawing on a qualitative and interpretive methodology, this study embraces a sample of illustrations of the uses of AI in different contexts of faith, and one particular experience in a Candomblé house, while the authors analyse them from critical perspectives. The results unsettle modernist conceptions regarding meaning and sense making and move towards more pluriversal and situated relationality regarding AI and faith. We conclude that AI helps to expand inter-religious dialogues, spiritual engagement and accessibility may also be fostered outside institutional frameworks through AI. Despite such advantages, profit-driven algorithms can shape spiritual/religious experience, replicate universalized ethics and onto-epistemologies, spread fake news and distort sources of information, while strengthening capitalism, surveillance, racism, not to mention unsustainability.

candidates.title: Robotic Assistants in the Operating Room: A Systematic Review of Vision‐Based Systems for Nonoperative Tasks
candidates.abstract: Nonoperative tasks in the operating room, such as instrument handling, sterile packaging, and logistics, are demanding yet have received less robotics attention than autonomous surgery. This review, the first to synthesize this literature, maps the perception methods, autonomy levels, methodological quality, and clinical readiness of vision‐based robotic assistants for scrub nurse, circulating nurse, and OR logistics roles. Searches of PubMed, IEEE Xplore, Scopus, ACM Digital Library, Web of Science, and Google Scholar returned 465 records; 20 publications describing 11 robotic system families met inclusion criteria. Most evidence, 17 publications across eight system families, concerns scrub nurse assistance; circulating nurse support, OR logistics, and dental assistance are each represented by one system. Vision methods have moved from classical image processing and predefined gestures toward deep learning, multimodal perception, and vision–language–action models, but autonomy has not kept pace: one system family reaches LoA 1, seven LoA 2, and three LoA 3, with Technology Readiness Levels spanning TRL 4 to TRL 6. Reported success rates are often high but rarely comparable and mostly generated in laboratory or simulated settings. Closing that gap requires stronger evidence on safety, sterility, failure recovery, workflow integration, execution speed, reproducibility, and, notably absent, manipulation of deformable sterile materials.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence in Embodied Learning: A Systematic Literature Review
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Background Embodied learning (EL) is an educational approach that posits that cognition develops as learners interact with their environment through physical activity or sensory experiences. Artificial intelligence in education (AIED) supports teaching and learning for both teachers and students, for example through personalised intelligent tutoring systems. However, prior research on EL has focused primarily on students' cognitive and emotional abilities and the integration of body and task, rather than on technological elements, and research on technology‐based embodied learning (TBEL) has centred on immersive technologies such as VR and AR. Objectives This study aims to explore the relationship between AI technology and EL by analysing (1) the types of AI utilised in EL‐related research (algorithm or model, data modality, AI role), (2) learners' outcomes obtained from AI‐based EL, and (3) the limitations and solutions when applying AI to EL. Method This study is a systematic literature review based on the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, and no meta‐analysis was conducted. This study only referenced papers published since 2016 that included both AI technology and EL, were written in English, and dealt with learning processes mediated by physical activity. A study was treated as within scope only where the physical activity was tied to the concept to be learned. Papers were excluded if they did not specify the AI algorithm or model, were not peer‐reviewed, were secondary studies, were not in the field of education, were unavailable in full text, emphasised only simple skill acquisition in physical education or music, or emphasised only simple speaking activities in foreign language learning. Searches were conducted on 16 September 2025 in ACM, ERIC, and Web of Science. Given the diverse types of included studies, risk of bias was assessed using the MMAT2018 tool. Due to the varied nature of the data, a multi‐faceted data synthesis was performed. Co‐occurrences between data modality and AI role, and between AI role and learner outcomes, were visualised using heatmaps. The flow between the three variables was represented using a Sankey diagram. Finally, all frequencies were recalculated after excluding papers appraised as Low or not appraised, to test which patterns depended on weaker evidence. Results A total of 23 papers were reviewed. As multiple data points could be extracted per item, the relative proportion was calculated against the number of coding instances per item. The most frequently used AI algorithm/model in the EL context was deep learning, and the data modality was image data. Where multiple data types were used, it was tagged as multimodal, accounting for 34.8%. Analysis and evaluation roles were most frequently extracted, and cognitive outcomes were reported most often. Key limitations identified included restricted participant numbers due to research design and studies conducted in controlled environments. Among papers appraised as High, the most frequent pathways ran from multimodal data to recognition and detection and from sensor data to analysis and evaluation, and cognitive outcomes were the most frequently reported. When papers appraised as Low or not appraised were set aside, the concentration of AI in analytical roles persisted, whereas the evidence for AI as an interactive or generative participant weakened. Discussion This review describes reported patterns rather than pooled effect estimates, as no meta‐analysis was conducted. Exclusion of grey literature may introduce publication bias. Furthermore, the potential risk of selection bias exists as literature was collected based on inclusion/exclusion criteria. This study is significant in that it identified how AI is utilised within the EL context and the learner outcomes reported alongside it, particularly as the scope of AIED broadens.

candidates.title: Ethics by Configuration: AI Ethics Principles in Coding Agent Instructions
candidates.abstract: As AI coding agents become integral to software development, projects increasingly utilise configuration files, such as context files and skills, to govern agent behaviour. While AI ethics principles are widely used in research and policy, little is known about whether and how they are reflected when developers configure coding agents. We studied ethics principles in 40,079 configuration files across 8,893 GitHub repositories. Using a validated large language model (LLM) classification, we measured the prevalence of ethics-related statements, and qualitatively analysed 702 stratified samples across 679 files to uncover the ethical considerations reflected in these files and the parties they concern. Ethics-related statements appeared in 39.4% of files and 61.5% of repositories; concentrated on accountability, transparency, privacy protection, and reliability; and occurred more often in task-specific files such as skills than in project-wide context files. Our qualitative analysis identified 30 categories of ethical considerations, which take the form of concrete rules for the agent. Accountability appeared mainly as requirements for human approval, transparency as explain and honestly report the agent's work, and fairness as accessibility and localisation. These considerations reveal a difference in focus. Whereas public ethics frameworks aim to protect society and end users, configuration files mainly concern developers, maintainers, and community members in the development workflow. Ethics-related content appeared mainly in prose-based files, and whether agents follow these instructions remains untested. We discuss the implications for practitioners, researchers, and policymakers.

candidates.title: Being a Padawan and Mastering the Force: A Dissertation Quest
candidates.abstract: This study explores the experiences of one doctoral researcher and two doctoral peers navigating mentor-mentee relationships through a literary lens, employing autoethnographic methods to capture the nuanced dynamics of guidance, expectation, and emotional labor. Data were drawn from narratives found in reflective journals, personal memos, email exchanges, text messages and conversations with four faculty mentors and two doctoral peers accumulated through the doctoral journey. The narratives were analyzed using thematic analysis. Using vignettes and incident reports, the research highlights key turning moments in the doctoral journey that shaped perceptions of mentorship, emphasizing both the cognitive and affective dimensions of academic identity development. Findings reveal that mentees often confront mismatched expectations, experience emotional labor, and negotiate cognitive dissonance when aligning their scholarly identities with mentor guidance. By centering the mentee perspective, this study challenges traditional views of passive doctoral socialization and underscores the importance of active, reciprocal engagement in mentorship. The research contributes to understanding the complexities of doctoral mentorship and offers practical implications for cultivating supportive, reflective, and equitable mentor-mentee relationships in higher education. Additionally, the study contributes to the literature by offering an experience-based framework of JOY (Journey, Openness, Yield) for understanding doctoral mentorship process and proposes to help guide productive mentor-mentee relationships.

candidates.title: Relational Complexity: Making Sense of Social Companion AI Use
candidates.abstract: The adoption of social companion AI (SCAI) is often framed in terms of the positive features it offers users, including its nonjudgemental nature, agreeableness, and availability. Here, we argue the appeal of these features primarily arises from the difficulties inherent in human sociality. SCAI reduces what we term relational complexity, or the demands and risks inherent in human relationships. Drawing insights from studies of human cognition, communication, and human-computer interaction, we identify six distinct sites of relational complexity that we posit are integral to understanding SCAI adoption. These include: (i) relationship formation and dissolution; (ii) achieving mutual understanding; (iii) interpersonal motives and strategic uncertainty; (iv) social partner evaluation and self-presentation; (v) social embeddedness and information flow; and (vi) reciprocity and relationship maintenance. By attenuating relational complexity, SCAI offers users some of the experiences associated with companionship while reducing the demands intrinsic to obtaining such experiences from another person. However, the lower interpersonal risk and diminished cognitive load that attracts users to SCAI may contribute to myriad negative impacts, including relationship displacement, social demotivation, social deskilling, and risks to privacy. The concept of relational complexity thus provides a framework for studying both the appeal of artificial companionship and its implications for human wellbeing.

candidates.title: Talking with language models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) produce text that invites us to treat our interactions with them as conversations, and to treat them as intelligent interlocutors who remember, act, and make commitments. We argue that this conversational presupposition is mistaken. We introduce the artifactual stance, which describes human–AI interaction in terms of their design and affordances, rather than potential intentional attitudes. On our account, LLMs produce candidate text that users interpret, evaluate, and sometimes adopt as their own speech. We argue that such exchanges are not conversations, since generating text does not itself constitute an utterance or the performance of a speech act. Rather the communicative and normative work of interpretation, commitment, and action remains with the user. Our framework explains both the sophistication and usefulness of LLMs, and the conversational appearances that can be traced back to properties of the interface and to artifact design. It also reframes puzzles about AI reference, the persistence of supposed interlocutors, and responsibility for AI-generated text. These questions are better approached through an account of how artifacts mediate human linguistic practices than through assumptions about AI speakerhood.

candidates.title: SocialCoAct: Enabling and Benchmarking Egocentric Social Co-Action for VLM-Based Humanoid Robots
candidates.abstract: Enabling humanoid robots to participate effectively in social interactions is important for their integration into human-centered environments. Existing methods, however, typically map pre-generated speech directly to continuous motion trajectories but have limited awareness of complex social environments and lack explicit high-level semantic action planning. We introduce SocialCoAct, a unified agent-centered framework for VLM-based egocentric social co-action. We formulate egocentric social co-action as an end-to-end agent task and develop SocialCoAct-Agent, which transforms egocentric observations and dialogue history into verbal responses and atomic action sequences, aligns each action with its corresponding utterance span, and executes the resulting behaviors in MuJoCo and on a physical humanoid robot. To evaluate the VLM capabilities required by this task, we construct SocialCoAct-Bench from continuous egocentric recordings of natural multi-party interactions. The benchmark comprises 423 human-verified multiple-choice questions across three subtasks: Long Episode Understanding (LEU), Speaker Intention Understanding (SIU), and Coordinated Action Planning (CAP). Across a diverse set of closed-source and open-weight VLMs, including general and egocentric models, the highest overall accuracy is 77.54%, while accuracy on the hard subset reaches only 46.51%. Extended reasoning improves Qwen3-VL-2B and Qwen3-VL-4B by 19.62 and 17.02 percentage points, respectively, but reduces inference throughput by 53.6$\times$ and 20.2$\times$. Visual-input ablations further show that the benefits of visual context vary across models. SocialCoAct provides a foundation for developing and evaluating VLM-based humanoid agents that coordinate context-aware speech and action in complex social interactions. The codebase and benchmark will be made publicly available upon publication.

candidates.title: InstAgent: A Recursively Self-Improving Agent Operating System for Heterogeneous Robot Collaboration
candidates.abstract: Heterogeneous robot teams enable complex, long-horizon tasks by combining complementary sensing, mobility, and manipulation capabilities across multiple embodiments. Yet existing systems struggle to retain execution-time corrections as reusable experience, maintain task-relevant context memory across space and time for reliable handoffs, and explicitly represent the inter-robot dependencies required for structured collaboration. In order to address these challenges, we present InstAgent, a recursively self-improving (RSI) Agent Operating System for heterogeneous robot collaboration. InstAgent organizes team behaviors as agentic behavior trees (BTs) that explicitly model capability assignment, inter-robot dependencies and handoff checks. The RSI mechanism updates these collaboration programs from execution feedback and preserves successful revisions for reuse in future tasks, while shared multimodal spatio-temporal memory provides context for planning and handoff validation. Experiments on 20 real-world multi-robot tasks with three high-level models show consistent gains in task success, first-attempt completion, and execution efficiency.

candidates.title: Autonomous Robotic Systems in Agriculture 5.0: A Review on Technical Architecture, Operational Applications, and Future Perspectives
candidates.abstract: This comprehensive narrative review examines the current state and future development perspectives of autonomous robotic systems within the scope of the Agriculture 5.0 paradigm, which aims for sustainable and efficient agricultural production. In this paper, the cognitive and physical structure of robotic systems is addressed through the "Eye-Brain-Foot Hand" hierarchy, and the role of next-generation Vision-Language Action (VLA) models, such as RT-2 and OpenVLA, in contextual agronomic decision-making processes is analyzed. Within the scope of field applications, the SAM2-based SPAF framework, which offers 95.54% harvesting success rate in tomatoes, and spot-spraying technologies that reduce chemical input volume by 90% are evaluated using quantitative data. Furthermore, the synergy between heterogeneous UAV-UGV fleets, trust-building through Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), and emerging advanced technological approaches such as Quantum Reinforcement Learning (QRL) are assessed. The results demonstrate that autonomous agriculture is not merely a tool to enhance technical efficiency, but is transforming into a cyber-physical production ecosystem where ethical responsibility, data sovereignty, and environmental sustainability converge.

candidates.title: Multidisciplinary Research: New Horizons, Emerging Trends and Contemporary Perspectives
candidates.abstract: The contemporary world is witnessing unprecedented transformations in science, technology, education, society, economy, culture, and the environment.These changes have created complex challenges and opened new avenues for knowledge creation, innovation, and sustainable development.In this rapidly evolving global landscape, multidisciplinary research has emerged as an essential approach to understanding interconnected issues, addressing emerging challenges, and developing comprehensive solutions.Recognizing the importance of integrating diverse fields of knowledge, this volume, Multidisciplinary Research: New Horizons, Emerging Trends and Contemporary Perspectives, brings together a range of scholarly contributions that reflect the diversity, dynamism, and evolving nature of contemporary research.The primary objective of this book is to provide an academic platform for researchers, academicians, educators, scholars, and practitioners to share their research findings, innovative ideas, theoretical insights, and practical experiences across various disciplines.It emphasizes the significance of multidisciplinary perspectives in expanding the boundaries of traditional knowledge and encouraging intellectual collaboration.By bringing together different areas of inquiry, the volume seeks to promote a deeper understanding of contemporary issues and highlight the potential of interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary approaches in responding to the needs of an increasingly interconnected world.The contributions included in this volume address a wide spectrum of emerging themes, contemporary developments, and innovative research perspectives.They reflect the changing dimensions of knowledge and the growing influence of technological advancements, digital transformation, artificial intelligence, educational innovation, social change, environmental sustainability, economic development, and other significant areas of academic inquiry.The chapters offer valuable insights into current research trends while identifying opportunities, challenges, and future directions within their respective fields.Collectively, they demonstrate how diverse academic disciplines can complement one another and contribute to meaningful research outcomes.An important feature of multidisciplinary research is its capacity to bridge the gap between theoretical understanding and practical application.It encourages researchers to move beyond disciplinary boundaries, adopt innovative methodologies, and examine problems from multiple perspectives.Such an approach is particularly relevant in addressing contemporary concerns that cannot be adequately understood or resolved through a single discipline.Collaboration, critical thinking, creativity, and knowledge integration are therefore central to the research vision reflected in this publication.This volume also seeks to inspire young researchers and postgraduate students to explore emerging research areas, develop original perspectives, and contribute to the advancement of knowledge.It encourages academic dialogue, collaborative research, and the exchange of ideas among scholars from diverse backgrounds.The research presented here is intended to serve as a useful reference for future investigations and to stimulate further scholarly discussions.We sincerely acknowledge the valuable contributions of all authors, researchers, reviewers, and academic professionals whose dedication and intellectual efforts have made this publication possible.

candidates.title: Working With AI and Robotic Systems While Preserving Clinical Judgement, Professional Accountability and Person‐Centred Care: Critical Care Nurses’ Perspectives
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: The integration of AI and robotic systems into critical care necessitates examining how ICU nurses preserve clinical judgement, professional accountability and person-centred care while using these technologies. AIMS: To explore ICU nurses' perceptions of AI and robotic systems in critical care, focusing on clinical judgement, trust, responsibility, professional roles and person-centred care. STUDY DESIGN: A qualitative descriptive study using scenario-based elicitation was conducted. Data were collected through seven semi-structured focus group discussions (FGDs) with 38 ICU nurses working in general, paediatric and cardiovascular surgery ICUs in two hospitals in Istanbul City. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, supported by MAXQDA 2024. FINDINGS: Four themes were developed: negotiating trust in AI-supported critical care; preserving human authority, accountability and boundaries; protecting the human core of intensive care nursing; and reimagining AI and robotic systems as supportive partners. ICU nurses evaluated these systems through bedside verification, patient safety, professional responsibility and person-centred care. AI recommendations were useful only when nurses could question, verify, delay or override them according to the patient's current condition. Robotic systems were valuable when they reduced documentation or physical workload, but not when they replaced clinical judgement, emotional presence, reassurance or accountability. CONCLUSIONS: ICU nurses conceptualised AI and robotic systems as acceptable only when clinically verifiable, professionally bounded and subordinate to human judgement. The findings support a model of AI- and robot-supported ICU care that is responsible, human-led and person-centred. RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE: AI and robotic systems should be implemented in ways that strengthen, rather than replace, nurses' clinical judgement, accountability and bedside presence. Clear protocols are needed to verify AI outputs, define robotic task boundaries, support nurses' authority to question or override recommendations and preserve person-centred care in technologically intensive ICU environments.

candidates.title: Wanted Dead or Alive: Anticipatory Regulation of Digital Immortality Platforms
candidates.abstract: The loss of a loved one is a painful and unique experience. To address that loss, technology companies are exploring the potential of digital immortality platforms, preserving individuals through artificial intelligence (AI) models trained on digital data generated in life. These datasets can be collected from scraping social media profiles and text conversations postmortem or intentionally recording videos and conversations with a person prior to their death for training AI models. In the face of any novel technology, the potential risks and benefits should guide the responsible development and deployment of every product. However, the liminal regulatory space that digital immortality technologies occupy makes this type of evaluation a difficult undertaking. One such approach would be to examine analogous sectors to the novel technology as a first step in developing regulations in that space. In this paper, we identify several ethical risks presented by digital immortality technologies and propose four analogies to contextualize possible regulation: psychology/grief counseling, death care/remains management, social media platforms, and AI companion services. We examine the parallels between digital immortality and each of these analogies in a proactive effort to prevent harms before the widespread public adoption of this technology. The contributions of this paper are a preliminary set of recommendations based on the limitations and challenges presented by a related set of real-world and sociotechnical systems involving social relationships, death, and grief.

candidates.title: Boys’ Love Media Scholarship, 2000–2026: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric-Thematic Synthesis
candidates.abstract: Originating in Japanese manga traditions depicting romantic relationships between men, Boys’ Love (BL) has developed into a transnational media phenomenon. Scholarship has expanded accordingly but remains fragmented across disciplines, national contexts, media forms, and methods. This systematic review examines 134 English-language, peer-reviewed, Scopus-indexed journal articles published between January 2000 and June 2026. Combining bibliometric mapping with a PRISMA-guided thematic synthesis, it maps geographic, temporal, thematic, and methodological patterns in the internationally indexed literature. Publication growth accelerates after 2020, accompanied by increased attention to Thai and Chinese screen media alongside continued work on Japanese manga. Four bibliometric clusters are interpreted through eight analytical themes: fandom and audiences; state, censorship, and regulation; representation and narrative; gender, sexuality, and feminist critique; industry, political economy, and soft power; transnational circulation and localization; genre history and aesthetics; and affect, emotion, and intimacy. Qualitative approaches dominate the corpus, whereas quantitative and mixed-method designs remain comparatively uncommon. Country-related patterns are treated as descriptive author-affiliation tendencies rather than statistical country-theme relationships. The review identifies four priorities: deeper production and political-economy analysis, stronger examination of multidirectional transnational circulation, broader geographic and linguistic coverage, and greater methodological diversity. It further argues that intercultural BL scholarship would benefit from moving beyond nation-bounded localization models toward transcultural and counter-flow perspectives.

candidates.title: Machine psychology for language models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a "machine psychology" for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.
