candidates.title: Design and Validation of a Robotic Knee Exoskeleton with Musculoskeletal Simulation-Derived Biological Torque Control
candidates.abstract: Data-driven controllers have enabled lower-limb robotic exoskeletons to adapt assistance to the user across many tasks. A leading example is biological torque control, which estimates the user's own joint moment from onboard sensors and assists in proportion to that estimate. However, its estimators are trained on data recorded with the target device, so deploying the controller on new hardware requires collecting new data. Existing open-source efforts release hardware, software, or controllers separately, so this data collection must still be repeated on the assembled device. Here, we present an open-source knee exoskeleton, built from off-the-shelf components and widely available fabrication tools, with a biological torque controller derived entirely from simulation. A muscle-driven imitation policy reproduces squatting motions from an open biomechanics dataset, and the resulting knee moments are distilled into an estimator that uses only onboard sensors, so no training data are recorded on the device. In seven able-bodied participants, assistance reduced peak biological knee extension moment by 21.5% and peak vastus medialis activation by 26.7% during squatting, relative to squatting without the exoskeleton (p<0.05). Our results demonstrate that a biological torque controller derived from simulation can transfer to physical hardware without device-specific data collection. Because the hardware and training pipeline are released together, research groups can train and compare knee exoskeleton controllers on shared hardware without additional data collection overhead.

candidates.title: Perceived Anthropomorphism and Learner Agency in Self‐Directed Use of GenAI for Informal Language Learning: A Metaphor Study
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT GenAI has the potential to empower self‐directed informal language learning. Yet, given its mixed blessings for learner agency, understanding factors that shape agency enactment in actualizing this potential is essential. Perceived anthropomorphism is central to learner agency with GenAI, as the extent to which learners anthropomorphize GenAI may frame relationships of engagement. This study explored the relationship of perceived anthropomorphism with learner agency by complementing a survey study with 397 Chinese undergraduate English language learners with an interview study with 22 participants. MANCOVA analysis revealed that anthropomorphic perception was a significant predictor of learning proxy agency and spatial agency. Interview responses further revealed that anthropomorphic perceptions are situation‐specific and varied in nuanced ways according to how learners perceived their power relations with GenAI and the symbolic resources they attributed to it, potentially contributing to divergent trajectories of learner agency with GenAI. Moreover, perceived anthropomorphism was intertwined with an array of individual, socio‐educational, and socio‐technical factors in shaping agency enactment. The findings advocate metaphor interventions to expand learner agency with GenAI for self‐directed informal language learning, underscoring a differentiated but integrative approach to cater support on different agency dimensions.

candidates.title: META-Robot: Self-Cognition and Capability Scaling in Agentic Robots
candidates.abstract: LLM-based robotic agent systems can generate programs for robot control, yet their generalization to new tasks often depends on elaborate scaffolding. Expanding their skill repertoires alone offers limited guidance on how to assess new capabilities or identify what remains beyond their reach. We introduce META-Robot, a framework that couples self cognition with capability scaling by expanding the criteria through which an agent evaluates and develops its skills. At its core, action-level predicates make execution outcomes explicit and available for LLM reasoning. The agent uses these assessments to identify its own limitations, extend relevant evaluation criteria, and guide the structured expansion of its skills. Proprioceptive feedback further grounds this process in the robot's physical state, enriching the evidence available for self-cognition. Experiments in simulation and on real robots demonstrate stronger overall task performance, generalization to new tasks, continued expansion of skills and evaluation criteria, and effective use of non-visual proprioceptive signals.

candidates.title: Environmentally Symbiotic Plant Robot
candidates.abstract: The increasing deployment of robots in natural environments exacerbates the risk of environmental damage, while realizing eco‐friendly and sustainable autonomous systems remains challenging. Here, an unprecedented robotic framework is presented: an environmentally symbiotic robot that externalizes its drive system to plants and soil, achieving locomotion through a closed cycle of seeding, germination, growth, and reseeding. The robot employs a modular wheel architecture that sows seeds onto the soil and converts the forces generated during plant germination and growth into rotational motion that triggers subsequent seeding. To validate this concept, a kinematic model linking plant growth to robot locomotion is developed, and the feasible design space is analyzed using the growth and mechanical characteristics of radish sprouts ( Raphanus sativus ). Based on this analysis, a 70 mm‐diameter physical robot is fabricated. The measured locomotion agrees well with the model predictions, and the robot autonomously travels a cumulative distance of 240 ± 20 mm on soil over 30 days using only the sown plants and the surrounding environment. These results demonstrate the feasibility of externalizing robotic drive systems to the environment by harnessing plants and environmental resources.

candidates.title: Characterizing the extrusion bioprinting process and microalgal photosynthetic efficiency in bioprinted constructs during parabolic flights
candidates.abstract: Extrusion-based bioprinting is a promising technology for in-space biofabrication, yet peer-reviewed process data derived in real microgravity remain rare. In the presented study, we used parabolic flights as a platform to characterize extrusion-based bioprinting of an alginate-methylcellulose bioink in short-term microgravity. Layer-by-layer printing was performed successfully at different layer distances (260-610 µm), and unsupported filament bridges of up to 13 cm were successfully printed under microgravity. We performed what is, to our knowledge, the first "green" bioprinting of microalgae-laden hydrogels under microgravity, with the cell viability of the thereby created samples exceeding 99% for Scenedesmus sp. and reaching 97% for Chlorella vulgaris on day 7 post-printing. Real-time pulse-amplitude modulated (PAM) fluorometry showed that the effective quantum yield of photosystem II remained stable across all gravitational phases in both liquid cultures and bioprinted samples while maintaining species-specific differences in non-photochemical quenching between the two species. The results of the study indicate that extrusion-based green bioprinting is functionally achievable under short-term microgravity conditions and that cultivation of the thereby created photosynthetically active structures is possible without loss of photosynthetic performance.

candidates.title: Liquid-metal physical unclonable functions resistant to both physical and digital cloning
candidates.abstract: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) leverage device-specific randomness for hardware security, yet their static, persistently accessible responses allow attackers to collect sufficient data for digital cloning. We present a liquid-metal PUF (LM-PUF) that integrates physical unclonability with material-driven resistance to digital attacks. Randomly mixed, visually indistinguishable LM particles form thermally unique microstructures, ensuring physical unclonability. Digital protection arises from two concealment mechanisms: time-limited accessibility restricts meaningful data collection, while decoy obscuration prevents reliable key identification. At equilibrium, the device remains cryptographically silent, but heating through a transient non-equilibrium window reveals thermal patterns convertible to cryptographic keys. Outside the predefined temperature range, misleading thermal patterns conceal the authentic key among decoys. LM-PUF supports scalable patterning, demonstrated in secure labels and QR codes, highlighting its potential for secure supply chains and physical unclonable authentication. Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) secure hardware identity but can be digitally cloned by machine-learning attacks. Here, authors report a liquid-metal PUF whose thermal keys appear only briefly during heating and are hidden among decoys, resisting both physical and digital cloning.

candidates.title: The Role of Human Rights in Transforming Economies
candidates.abstract: Abstract This chapter explores the role of human rights in reimagining our economies to prioritize the inter-connections between vital life-supporting systems and the well-being of people and the planet. The chapter illuminates the capacity of human rights to shift economic thought away from traditional narratives towards a framework centred on care, community, and ecological balance through the documentation and prevention of foreseeable negative rights impacts of fossil fuel-based economies (Morgera, 2025a). In addition, human rights analysis of the environmental and socio-cultural challenges of the rush towards energy transition minerals supports a paradigm shift in economic thought, by revealing—and at the same time requiring the moving away from—extractivist, colonial, and neo-colonial economic practices, that still privilege fossil fuels-related profits over the protection of life (Morgera, 2025b).

candidates.title: Robot Navigation and Canine Welfare: A Pilot Study Surfacing Challenges for Cross-Species Legibility and Proxy Validity in Animal-Machine Interaction
candidates.abstract: Autonomous delivery robots increasingly share residential spaces with companion animals, yet navigation behavior is rarely designed with animal welfare in mind. This paper presents a pilot study evaluating a curve-out maneuver, a laterally arcing pass-by trajectory triggered at the dog's alert distance, proposed as a candidate welfare-informed navigation intervention grounded in canine social communication research and legible motion theory. Following a research through design approach, we developed and evaluated a first design iteration of the artifact in a naturalistic home environment with a companion dog. Contrary to our hypothesis, the curve-out produced a more acute stress response than the straight-line baseline. We argue that discontinuous execution limitation, the robot stopping and reorienting multiple times to approximate the arc, undermined legibility, which in itself became a stressor. The pilot surfaces the legibility of robot behavior to non-humans' eyes and proxy stimulus validity as structural challenges for AMI and repositions the design problem for future work.

candidates.title: UMI-Live for In-The-Wild Bimanual Robotics Data Collection
candidates.abstract: Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) devices allow human experts to demonstrate tasks for robot learning without teleoperating physical robots. Using these demonstrations as training data still requires a consistent hardware setup, calibration, and data processing. We present UMI-Live, a full-stack open-source bimanual UMI system for in-the-wild data collection. We design our custom UMI-Live hardware to integrate camera and LiDAR--inertial sensing, onboard compute, and power, without external tracking equipment or calibration within the collection environment. We implement a simple user interface for recording data while an asynchronous pipeline performs parallel SLAM reconstruction and publishes training-ready datasets. We also release software that supports dual-YAM teleoperation and VLA policy training and inference. We validate UMI-Live data quality by fine-tuning $π_{0.5}$ and MolmoAct2, achieving success rates of 10/10 and 8/10, respectively on a bimanual pick-and-place task. Furthermore, we release 40 hours of UMI-Live data across three tasks, and complete hardware designs, software, and reproduction guides at our $\href{https://umi-live.github.io/}{\text{project website}}$.

candidates.title: VLM-based multi-agent architecture for multifunctional robotic health attendant (RHA) using phase-prompt task design
candidates.abstract: Healthcare robots are increasingly needed to support clinicians whose work involves diverse tasks and frequent task switching. However, most healthcare robots developed to assist clinicians either perform a single function or implement multiple functions as fixed task pipelines that are difficult to adapt to different patients, rooms, or care teams. This study presents a vision language model (VLM) based multiagent architecture for a multifunctional Robotic Health Attendant (RHA). In this architecture, each task can be designed by writing natural language phase specifications that describe how available tools should be used during task execution. A main agent interprets natural language requests from clinicians or patients and routes each request to the appropriate task agent. During execution, the VLM uses language, visual input, and contextual information to select tools and interpret their results. A shared Model Context Protocol (MCP) tool layer provides elemental robot functions such as navigation, manipulation, and perception across tasks. The architecture was implemented on a TIAGo Pro robot and evaluated in an unoccupied patient room across five tasks including object delivery, documentation, visual monitoring, patient education, and medication reminders. The case study demonstrated the feasibility of the proposed architecture as a reasoning core for a multifunctional healthcare robot by executing multiple tasks and adapting task behavior by editing natural language phase specifications. The comparison across three VLMs showed that longer tool-call sequences led to skipped steps and, in some cases, false reports of task success, which is a key reliability concern for healthcare robots performing long, multi-step tasks. The study also identified technical limitations and future research needs that must be addressed to make the architecture more robust in realistic care settings.

candidates.title: THE ROBOTIC SERVER PARADOX: UNPACKING THE MEDIATING ROLES OF NOVELTY AND PERCEIVED EFFICIENCY ON CUSTOMER SATISFACTION IN SAUDI RESTAURANTS AND EWOM
candidates.abstract: Integrating robotic servers in Saudi Arabia's rapidly evolving hospitality sector presents a paradoxical challenge: while robotic assis⁠tance enhanc⁠es operat⁠ional efficiency and add⁠s e⁠xperiential nove⁠lty, its impac⁠t on customer satisfaction and electronic word-of-mouth (eWOM) remains⁠ complex and underexplore⁠d. Anchored in the Stimulus-O⁠rganism-Respon⁠se (S-O-R), Expectation Confirmation Theory (⁠ECT), and Technolo⁠gy Acceptance Model (TAM) framework, this study investigates the mediating impact of perceived novelty (P⁠N) and⁠ perceived efficiency (PE) on the relationship between the use of robo⁠tic assistance (URA) and customer satisfacti⁠on (CS), subsequently influencing eWOM. Addition⁠ally, it examines the moderating role of service context (SC)⁠ on the satisfaction-eWOM linkage wit⁠hin Saudi cu⁠ltural settings. Data were c⁠ollecte⁠d from 348 restaurant customer⁠s across Jeddah, Riyadh, and Madinah wh⁠o experience⁠d robotic service encounters and analyzed using partial least s⁠quares structural equ⁠ation modeling (PLS-SEM).⁠ The findings confirm that URA⁠ significantly enhances both PN and PE, with efficiency showing a stronger mediating effect on customer outcomes. Service context significantly moderates the CS-eWOM relationship, highlighting th⁠e i⁠mportance of cultural and⁠ environmental factors. The results provide actionable insights for restaurant managers to deploy robotic assistance strategically by balancing te⁠chnological functionality with cu lturally resonant service de⁠sign, optimi⁠zing⁠ customer satisfaction an⁠d fostering positive el⁠ectronic advocacy⁠ in the Saudi Arabian hospit⁠ality market. The study distinguishes the experiential appeal of robotic novelty from the functional contribution of service efficiency and examines their sequential indirect associations with electronic word-of-mouth through satisfaction. The analysis focuses on restaurant customers with first-hand experience with robotic service in three Saudi cities, allowing the model to be examined in an emerging, technology-enabled dining context. By assessing these pathways alongside the conditional role of service context, the study clarifies how customer evaluations of robotic assistance relate to post-encounter communication.

candidates.title: When culture becomes AI infrastructure: copyright and the emergence of chokepoint capitalism in Europe
candidates.abstract: Lawful cultural extraction may leave chokepoints intact while making them harder to see. This article examines that risk in European Union copyright and AI governance. Combining doctrinal legal analysis with legal political economy, it applies Giblin and Doctorow’s account of chokepoint capitalism to cultural inputs and AI-generated outputs, distinguishing barriers, practical dependency, intermediary control and capture. The analysis identifies how rights reservations, licensing and transparency duties may protect cultural interests while leaving authors, performers, cultural heritage institutions and communities dependent on intermediaries for access, representation and remuneration. It proposes interoperability and portability, collective representation and remuneration, contractual safeguards, public or cooperative infrastructure, platform accountability and cultural contestability. These measures are assessed for their capacity to reduce dependency and their potential to create new intermediaries whose authority cannot readily be challenged. The article concludes that cultural accountability requires attention to the practical conditions for exercising rights and participating in decisions about culture.

candidates.title: Securing the Robotics Supply Chain
candidates.abstract: This paper sets out what a sustained federal research and investment agenda would need to include to close that gap--not within a single budget cycle, but over the decade such an undertaking will realistically require. It identifies where the gap is most pronounced today: in the methods needed to verify and certify components of uncertain origin, in the foundational hardware research that has long been underfunded relative to software, in the physical infrastructure researchers need to test systems at scale, and in the workforce required to build and sustain all of it. Robotics should not be treated merely as a downstream beneficiary of a broader artificial intelligence investment strategy. It constitutes its own supply chain, with its own points of failure, and merits its own sustained federal commitment.

candidates.title: Democratizing Drug Discovery: A Scalable Open-Source Pipeline for Massive Specific Protein Target QSAR Modeling Using ChEMBL
candidates.abstract: Abstract The proprietary nature of AI/ML tools in drug discovery limits access to advanced virtual screening methodologies. To address this, we present an open-source, automated pipeline for large-scale Quantitative Structure−Activity Relationship (QSAR) modeling utilizing ChEMBL. Our batch processing system constructed 2263 predictive models across multiple protein targets, applying both regression and classification strategies with strict quality control thresholds. The pipeline integrates ErG and RDKit descriptor families, employs Random Forest and XGBoost algorithms with Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization, and handles class imbalances using SMOTE. Models are saved only when achieving R2 ≥ 0.7 for regression or MCC ≥ 0.55 for classification. Data is stratified by assay and measurement types to maintain biological relevance. Additionally, we feature an interactive EDA visualization tool with ErG heatmaps and external validation via the DELTA database. This work democratizes industrial-grade QSAR infrastructure, empowering the research community to reproduce and extend computational workflows.

candidates.title: A Review of the Evolution and Shifts in Research on Chinese Online Fan Fiction Culture
candidates.abstract: With the development of online media, fan fiction has gradually evolved from a niche creation by fans into a network cultural practice with a stable community base, and related research has continued to expand. This paper focuses on the period from 2000 to 2026, using a combination of platforms such as CNKI, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. It also employs a snowballing tracing method to select representative results and divides the research into stages based on changes in research subjects, problem awareness, and media environment. A review reveals that related research has generally gone through three stages: research on concepts and online communities, research on media and cultural practices, and research on creators and platform governance. The research objects have gradually expanded from texts and groups to the relationship between creators, communities, and platforms. However, existing research still has shortcomings in terms of research types, cross-platform comparisons, and the boundaries of related concepts.

candidates.title: A Three-Dimension Perspective of Individual, Community and Platform in the Literature Review on the Motivational Mechanisms of Fan Labour in the Digital Age
candidates.abstract: Digital technology has changed the ways fans participate in cultural activities. Practices such as chart voting, comment control, and data production gradually become unpaid, organized, and affective digital labor. In available research, scholars either emphasize capitalist exploitation or highlight fan autonomy, and the concept of affective labor is inconsistently used. The three-level dynamics of individual psychology, community culture, and platform regulation lack integration. With this background, this paper reviews the literature on affective labor, audience commodity, digital labor, and fan culture, in order to figure out why fans continue to labor voluntarily and how multiple dynamics interact. Through comparison of theoretical genealogies and literature integration, the research constructs a three-dimensional framework of individual, community, and platform, which thereby explains that fan labor is neither pure exploitation nor complete liberation, instead, it is a complex practice pulled by three forces. Meanwhile, this paper hopes that future research can move beyond the either/or judgment of exploitation and liberation, and focus more on fans’ own role in labor and how fans produce meaning.

candidates.title: Topologically adaptive ant colony optimization for scheduling mega-structure pile foundations with endogenous spatio-temporal constraints
candidates.abstract: Pile foundation scheduling of super-large engineering structure presents significant concerns and challenges due to the dynamically triggered and evolved vibration exclusion zones generated by impact boring. However, conventional re­source-constrained project scheduling theories often exhibit spatial blindness, resulting in cascading construction critical path delays. Therefore, this study proposes a Topologically Adaptive Ant Colony Optimization (TA-ACO) algorithm embedded within a state-dependent simulation environment. The algorithm employs a dual-colony cooperative mechanism to effectively de­couple the adversarial resource coupling between piling crews and grouting crews. Specifically, a novel look-ahead heuristic strategy is introduced, guiding crews to maximize spatial sparsity, which is analogous to solving the Maximum Independent Set problem and avoiding topological deadlocks. Computational experiments demonstrate that TA-ACO effectively mitigates spatial fragmentation and reduces the project makespan by 21.5% to 28.3% across different large-scale instances, compared to the industry-standard greedy strategy. The engineering application results of large airports show that the proposed algo­rithm compressed the construction period of a critical zone, which includes 97 pile foundations, from 47 days to 34 days, se­curing a valuable 13-day lead time for subsequent superstructure assembly.

candidates.title: Can large language models complement tourism surveys?
candidates.abstract: Tourism research relies heavily on surveys, yet declining response rates challenge data collection. Large language models offer a potential alternative for approximating human responses. This study compares four prompting techniques using ChatGPT-4o. At the mean level, chain-of-thought and role-based prompting showed limited alignment with human data, while bias mitigation yielded slight improvement. N-shot learning achieved the strongest mean-level alignment, although performance varied across measures. Analyses of variance, skewness, and kurtosis showed that no prompting technique consistently reproduced human response distributions. These findings identify important boundary conditions: large language models may approximate the “average respondent” on specific measures but fail to capture broader distributional properties, supporting their potential use for early-stage pretesting and screening rather than inference-driven research.

candidates.title: Recent advances in electrohydraulic actuation from structural design to emerging applications
candidates.abstract: Electrohydraulic actuators (EHAs) have emerged as versatile soft transducers that couple electrostatic attraction with fluid redistribution to generate diverse mechanical outputs. Their performance is governed not only by electrostatic loading but also by how actuator architecture directs the enclosed dielectric fluid and converts its motion into deformation. This review examines EHAs from this architecture-centered perspective. The fundamental mechanisms of electrostatic zipping and hydraulic redistribution are first introduced together with key design parameters and performance metrics. Representative structural architectures are then classified into planar pouch and zipping structures, localized protrusion and hydraulically amplified electrostatic taxel configurations, stacked and multilayer systems, and segmented or multidirectional designs. Their mechanical characteristics are discussed in terms of force, displacement, dynamic response, geometry-dependent fluid transport, and trade-offs among voltage, stroke, force, and bandwidth. Emerging applications in wearable haptics, soft robotics, reconfigurable surfaces, and soft pumping are subsequently surveyed. Finally, challenges associated with high-voltage operation, material durability, scalability, system integration, sensing, control, and standardized performance evaluation are discussed. This review highlights fluid-redistribution pathways as a central design variable linking actuator architecture to mechanical function and application-specific performance.

candidates.title: Towards Human-Centered Safety in Vision-Language-Action Robot Control: A Survey and Outlook
candidates.abstract: As Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models couple perception and language understanding with physical action in human-shared environments, safety depends on whether they capture relevant information about people, environments, and social context and use it to shape robot behavior. We therefore center this survey on semantic-to-action causality towards human-centered robot safety, examining how safety-relevant semantics remain consequential for actions that preserve human well-being, environmental integrity, and social compliance. To trace this relationship from learning through execution to validation, we organize the literature across design-time methods that shape how safety-relevant features are learned, deployment-time mechanisms that govern their influence on behavior, and validation-time approaches that assess their effectiveness under safety-critical conditions. Across these stages, we identify four linked requirements, safety boundary coverage, semantic-to-action fidelity, contextual intervention and recovery, and incident-path validation, which describe how safety-relevant information must be captured, preserved, enforced, and evidenced. These requirements expose corresponding open challenges in sparse boundary examples, limited causal verifiability, gaps in intervention timing and recovery, and incomplete incident attribution.

candidates.title: Sanitizing the stain: a critical integrative review of sportswashing discourse
candidates.abstract: Purpose This paper aims to develop a marketing-oriented understanding of sportswashing by synthesizing its burgeoning, fragmented and cross-disciplinary scholarship through Mary Douglas’s anthropology of purity and pollution, explaining how sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a critical integrative review of 45 peer-reviewed articles, identified through systematic searches of major academic databases. After two-stage screening, the corpus was analyzed qualitatively from an interpretive stance, using thematic synthesis followed by abductive theorization. Findings This study first maps the sportswashing ecosystem − stains, actors, motivations, mechanisms, phases and outcomes − revealing complexity and tensions pervading the literature. Building on this synthesis, it identifies five cleansing logics through which sportswashing operates as a symbolic purification process: separation, dilution, displacement, containment and sanctification. Each logic illuminates how sportswashing operates as a contest over cultural classification through association without explicit claims. Research limitations/implications This synthesis advances a research agenda for interpretive marketing and consumer research, highlighting what qualitative inquiry could reveal about sportswashing across consumer resistance, platformization of consumer culture, CSR-washing, macromarketing, branding and reputation, marketing communications, market systems and critical and postcolonial marketing. Originality/value This paper theorizes sportswashing as a symbolic purification process, extending the CSR-washing literature from deception to associative classificatory work. Its five cleansing logics connect marketing scholarship on sponsorship, reputation, meaning transfer and brand activism; show how fan meaning-making and consumer resistance become embroiled in cultural-political reputation management; and reframe sportswashing as a contest over cultural classification, resolving persistent conceptual tensions.

candidates.title: Autonomous Quantum Measurement with Agentic AI
candidates.abstract: Quantum materials exhibit diverse electronic and functional phenomena, but their characterization requires extensive experimental expertise, iterative decision-making and accumulated laboratory knowledge that is difficult to document and transfer. Here we introduce Quantum Agent (QUANTA), an agentic artificial intelligence (AI) framework for autonomous quantum-materials characterization. Using a widely adopted Physical Property Measurement System (PPMS) as an experimental platform, QUANTA combines retrieval augmentation using scientific literature, experimental protocols and prior measurements with specialized agents for experimental planning, troubleshooting, and data interpretation. A separate deterministic control layer validates instrument actions. Guided by incoming data, QUANTA evaluates measurement quality, revises experimental plans and selects subsequent measurements. We demonstrate these capabilities through transport measurements of the topological Weyl semimetal TaP, as well as investigations of nonlinear responses in magnetic material Co2MnGa. These results establish QUANTA as a generalizable framework for evidence-driven, safeguarded and closed-loop quantum-materials characterization.

candidates.title: Beyond a Name: The CAPE Framework for Names, Nicknames, and (Nick)Naming in Marketing
Do We Conform to Machines? Social Influence in the Age of AI
candidates.abstract: People now take advice, drafts and judgments from AI systems many times a day, and classic social influence theory predicts they will sometimes yield to them. This article reviews how the work of Sherif, Asch, Deutsch and Gerard, and Cialdini on informational and normative influence applies to human–AI interaction. It synthesizes evidence on computers as social actors, algorithm appreciation and aversion, automation bias, robot-induced peer pressure, and the influence of large language models (LLMs) on opinions and moral judgments. Four mechanisms are proposed: perceived competence, authority cues, social presence, and cognitive effort reduction. Task ambiguity, self-efficacy, domain expertise, and culture are discussed as moderators. A qualitative study of ten adults, analysed with reflexive thematic analysis, is presented as a framework of eight superordinate themes. The article ends with design implications and a research agenda aimed at separating rational reliance from conformity.

candidates.title: OpenJaws: An Open Hardware UMI Framework with Stereo Localization for Generalist Manipulation
candidates.abstract: Handheld data-collection interfaces such as the Universal Manipulation Interface (UMI) allow manipulation demonstrations to be gathered in the wild without a robot in the loop, but the quality of the resulting action labels is bounded by the accuracy of vision-based localization. Existing systems recover end-effector pose from monocular visual-inertial odometry, which is subject to scale ambiguity and drift, or delegate tracking to closed-source modules and external infrastructure that reintroduce cost and setup burden. We present OpenJaws, a fully open hardware and software framework for sensorized UMI that improves localization and simplifies deployment across robot platforms. OpenJaws pairs a modular, 3D-printed gripper exposing a standardized ISO adapter with a low-cost stereo camera to recover metric camera trajectories. We further introduce UMI-Loc-Bench-v1, a benchmark quantifying real-world localization accuracy for handheld data-collection devices, and show that stereo localization substantially outperforms monocular alternatives. Finally, we demonstrate that policies trained on data collected with OpenJaws can be deployed on a real robot across multiple tasks. Hardware, software, and data are released under a commercially permissive license. Code, data, and videos are available at https://open-jaws.github.io/

candidates.title: Embodied timing turns a robotic tug-of-war into cooperative transport
candidates.abstract: Living systems move loads with agents that pull against one another. Kinesin and dynein pull one vesicle, ants haul a dead insect, and antagonist muscles move a joint. Whether the timing of the forces can by itself determine which side moves the load is not well understood. Here, combining experiments, theory, and simulations of a tug-of-war between two matched teams of spring-coupled robots, we show that the relative timing of the pull forces breaks the symmetry and decides the contest. Teams pulling in unison or in strict alternation tie. Between these, the lagging team wins, most strongly near a quarter cycle, because the springs unload while the leading team coasts and the lagging team still pulls. In the model and in robot simulations, braking rather than coasting between pulls, once strong enough, shifts the advantage to the leading team. Winning and losing leave distinct signatures in each robot’s motor current. Using these local signals, we formulate an embodied decentralized phase-adaptation rule that enables transient leadership to switch between teams, allowing the collective to transport high-friction cargo and to navigate around obstacles towards a prescribed target without explicit communication.

candidates.title: Evolving Agent Teams
candidates.abstract: The rapid progress of software engineering agents drives interest in applying them to open-ended problems such as GPU kernel optimization. However, we find that existing coding agents converge to local optima on real-world, expert-written kernels (e.g., FlashInfer). We introduce Evolving Agent Teams, a multi-agent framework that escapes such local optima. It features (1) a central supervisor that diagnoses each local optimum and restructures a team of agents; and (2) a persistent file system that comprises a learning document, an evolution history, and per-team artifacts, grounding restructuring with accumulated experience. Under a matched token budget, Evolving Agent Teams consistently outperforms strong coding-agent baselines. With an extended token budget, Evolving Agent Teams generates a CUDA kernel that reaches 1.2x mean speedup over the production FlashInfer MLA paged decode kernel from scratch and wins on 36 of 47 production workloads from FlashInfer-Bench (0.86-0.99x on the remaining 11). It also demonstrates superior performance on tasks such as KDA prefill on AMD MI350X (3.01x over vLLM) and NVIDIA B200 (3.44x over FlashKDA), MoE expert-offload serving on Apple silicon (30.3 tokens/s decode for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next in MLX 4-bit on a 48 GB M4 Pro), and RoboDojo robot manipulation (62.1 on held-out seeds vs. 55.3 for the best leaderboard entry). Code is available at https://github.com/caoshiyi/EAT.

candidates.title: EgoThumb: A Vision-Driven Supernumerary Robotic Thumb for Autonomous Grasp and Holding Assistance
candidates.abstract: Supernumerary robotic fingers augment human dexterity by enabling a single hand to perform complex "hold-and-manipulate" tasks that typically require bimanual coordination. However, existing devices are often hindered by bulky hardware that limits interaction to large objects and rely on explicit hand motion triggers that lack environmental context. To address these challenges, we present EgoThumb, a fully open-source, vision-driven supernumerary robotic thumb. EgoThumb features a compact, dual tendon-driven finger whose actuation is relocated to the forearm, reducing distal weight while enabling precise active joint control. The system utilizes a visual imitation learning policy that maps egocentric images from a palm-facing camera directly to continuous joint positions. By implicitly decoding human intent from visual cues capturing both the hand and the object of interest, EgoThumb achieves robust autonomous manipulation and strong generalization across diverse users and environments. All hardware designs and software implementations are fully open-sourced at https://ego-thumb.github.io.

candidates.title: AI-Assisted Design Optimization of Modular Robotic Arm Structures Using Genetic- Algorithm-Trained Neural Surrogates
candidates.abstract: Abstract Modular robotic arms are increasingly adopted in manufacturing and service robotics because interchangeable link and joint modules shorten redesign cycles and improve part commonality across product families. Sizing each module, however, still normally requires repeated finite-element analysis (FEA), which becomes computationally prohibitive once it is embedded inside a population-based search such as a genetic algorithm (GA). This paper presents a genetic-algorithm-trained neural-surrogate framework that replaces the great majority of these expensive structural evaluations with a fast, learned approximation. A two-module shoulder-to-elbow and elbow-to-wrist link chain is parameterized by six design variables covering outer diameter, wall thickness, and material selection per module. A Latin-Hypercube-sampled dataset of 1,500 configurations is labelled using a one-dimensional Euler-Bernoulli finite-element beam model that returns structural mass, tip deflection, root and step-section von Mises stress, and first natural frequency. A feed-forward neural network trained on this dataset attains coefficients of determination between 0.984 and 0.997 on an independent test set. The trained surrogate is then embedded as the fitness evaluator inside a constrained non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) that searches for Pareto-optimal trade-offs between mass and tip deflection subject to stress, frequency, and buckling constraints. The surrogate-assisted optimizer converges to the same optimum as a direct finite-element-in-the-loop genetic algorithm while consuming roughly one-eighth of the high-fidelity structural evaluations, and 98.8% of its Pareto-optimal candidates remain feasible under independent re-validation. The best surrogate-optimized configuration reduces structural mass by 19.9% relative to a representative baseline while satisfying every specified constraint, demonstrating a reproducible and computationally economical route to modular robotic-arm structural design.

candidates.title: RAVEN: A Unified Active SLAM System for Rapid Autonomous Visual Exploration with Aerial Robots under Localization Uncertainty
candidates.abstract: Active simultaneous localization and mapping (SLAM) addresses the problem of planning robot motion to build complete and accurate maps of unknown environments through efficient exploration while maintaining high localization accuracy. This raises a dilemma between exploring unknown spaces to expand coverage and exploiting visited regions to perform active loop closures. Despite numerous prior works on ground robots, aerial robots with high agility and constrained sensor suites face more significant localization drift and thereby demand dedicated active SLAM planning. Moreover, a unified strategy that adapts performance based on task-specific priorities remains an open question. In this article, we introduce RAVEN, a unified active SLAM framework for Rapid Autonomous Visual ExploratioN using quadrotors, which systematically accounts for localization uncertainty. The framework starts with identifying frontiers and active loop closure candidates, from which global tour candidates are generated. These candidates are evaluated using a utility vector that separately quantifies exploration efficiency and localization accuracy, and the final tour is selected according to a prioritization parameter ranging from $[0,1]$. Finally, a perception-aware navigation planner generates smooth execution trajectories that minimize visual state estimation error based on the online Fisher information field that provides visual localization information in real-time. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate that RAVEN outperforms state-of-the-art active SLAM methods, highlighting its advantages in producing a spectrum of performance across prioritizations. Fully onboard field experiments with a customized stereo-inertial quadrotor further validate its practical applicability in challenging environments. The source code will be released to benefit the community.

candidates.title: Perspective on AI and quantum open-source software
candidates.abstract: Quantum open-source software provides essential infrastructure for quantum science, and artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping its capabilities and transforming its development. However, verifying quantum software at scale remains difficult, and AI-generated contributions can increase the workload of maintainers. In this Perspective, we examine verification as a central requirement for reliable AI-assisted quantum software development and research. We analyze public repositories, records covering 110 repositories from five annual quantum open-source hackathons that we organize, and responses from more than 1600 participants in a community survey. Our analysis connects limitations in automated verification with the review burden on quantum software maintainers. We propose verification practices and contribution standards that require contributors to support their changes with reproducible evidence for maintainer review. We also examine how quantum open-source software can provide infrastructure for AI-driven research whose results the community can independently verify and build upon. We maintain an open-source companion repository to support reproducibility and help projects adopt and refine these proposals. Together, these contributions help the quantum open-source software community translate advances in AI into reliable quantum research through reproducible verification.

candidates.title: The Generation of Willingness to Pay in Cross-Platform Fan Communities: A Comparative Study of the Mutual Constitution of Platform Policies and Community Behavioral Dynamics
candidates.abstract: The proliferation of platform-based fan communities has transformed how cultural content is produced, consumed, and monetized, yet the relationship between platform payment architectures and the cultural norms that emerge within fan communities remains poorly understood. As platforms increasingly shape not only what fans can pay for but also how payment itself is understood, understanding how payment cultures are generated across different platform environments has become urgent. This study examines how platform monetization policies and fan community norms interact across four platforms—Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, Lofter, and AO3—to generate distinct and self-reinforcing payment cultures. Through a comparative case study design incorporating community observation, textual analysis, and semi-structured interviews with 16 active members, we identify four consumption models arrayed along two axes: consumption drive (commercial vs. affective) and linkage mode (collective vs. atomistic). A self-constructed commercialization index reveals a negative correlation between platform commercialization intensity and perceived community agency, suggesting that less intensive platform governance may paradoxically foster deeper community loyalty on members' own terms. Content creators emerge as pivotal mediators in this bidirectional feedback loop.

candidates.title: Integrated Design and Reproducible Feasibility Analysis of a Four-Wheel Rover with Packet-Commanded Imaging, LiDAR Ranging, and Learning-Assisted Target Recognition
candidates.abstract: This study develops an integrated, reproducible design assessment for a four-wheel educational rover intended for the high-school remote-control division of the 2027 NASA Human Exploration Rover Challenge. The architecture combines commercial differential drive control, independently sprung wheel carriers, separate drive and task batteries, and a Raspberry Pi-based subsystem that executes received imaging and ranging commands. The analysis reconciles component lists with dimensioned computer-aided design views, derives mobility and electrical constraints, and connects sensor geometry to command execution. At the estimated mass of 10.919 kg, a 215 mm wheel rotating at 200 RPM produces a theoretical rolling speed of 8.105 km/h; consequently, the nominal motor label does not establish compliance with an 8 km/h design ceiling. A steady 20-degree climb requires at least 1.255 newton-meters per wheel under an assumed rolling-resistance coefficient of 0.10 and equal torque sharing. At 50 ft, an ideal 12-inch feature spans approximately 71 pixels across a full-resolution Camera Module 3 Standard image, while a 1-degree pointing error displaces the ranging ray by approximately 266 mm. An executed synthetic benchmark compares color-geometry rules and two linear support-vector classifiers on 2,400 generated board crops with scene-disjoint evaluation. A separate reference command executor is checked using mocked hardware. These software results and analytical sensitivities support a testable development plan; the study does not report physical rover trials. The principal contribution is a traceable connection between component choices, failure mechanisms, quantitative design limits, and reproducible verification tasks.

candidates.title: Allocating cognitive work across people, language models and deterministic tools: A task-analytic method
candidates.abstract: Abstract People supervising language-model agents need to know what the agents decided and when to intervene. Reading every response becomes impractical as more work is delegated. We extend a task-analysis method to allocate decisions among deterministic tools, small language models, reasoning models and people, with each task represented as an observe, orient, decide and act cycle. Analysts specify its inputs, decision and output, and derive the information supervisors need from their goals. Allocation depends on how formally the decision can be specified, the cognitive control it demands, its Cynefin domain and whether it establishes facts or makes a normative choice. A machine tier withholds a decision when it declines, fails the output checks or falls below its confidence threshold. The decision then passes to the next tier. People retain normative choices and may store them as scoped policies. In a computational comparison with two open-weight models on 64 synthetic tanker-join instances, the allocated system was correct on 89.6% of required epistemic decisions, against 67.2% for a reasoning model given the whole task. It used about a third of the input tokens and an eighth of the output tokens. A scripted supervisor supplied 13% of its scored decisions. The small-model tier withheld 97% of its wrong candidates and the reasoning-model tier 93%, counting refusals, output checks and confidence thresholds together. The prototype failed to keep one training choice with people. Effects on supervisors' situation awareness and workload require a study with practitioners.

candidates.title: Augmentation or Attrition? Task Redistribution After a Generative AI HR Deployment
candidates.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) is widely expected to reshape human resource management (HRM), yet organization-level evidence on how it redistributes work between people and machines is scarce, and debate is split between optimistic augmentation and pessimistic attrition narratives. This paper asks a narrower, answerable question: after an enterprise generative AI platform is deployed in HR, which tasks move to the machine, which remain human, and how do practitioners experience the change? We report an exploratory pre–post study of a single platform deployed across ten organizations over six months, combining anonymized operational data (more than 6,000 requisitions) with thirty-two practitioner interviews. The design is observational, with no control group, so results are reported as associations rather than causal effects. Time-to-hire fell by a median of 23% across sites (95% CI 20-26%; from about 42 to 32 days), and the volume of routine queries reaching human advisers fell by 72% (95% CI 69-75%); every site moved in the same direction (Wilcoxon signed-rank p = 0.002, matched-pairs rank-biserial r = 1.00), though with only ten sites this is indicative. Both varied across sites and accrued gradually over the six months rather than at switch-on. The platform absorbed high-volume, rule-bound tasks such as screening, scheduling, and policy queries, while judgment- and relationship-based tasks remained human. Practitioners reported reallocating time towards that relational work, alongside concerns about transparency, surveillance, and new supervisory demands. We do not observe long-run employment outcomes: no participating organization reduced HR headcount during the window. Six months is shorter than a typical restructuring cycle, and we cannot establish that augmentation, rather than attrition, is the lasting result. We therefore treat the optimistic reading as a conditional leadership choice, not a finding. Because the platform is a commercial product connected to the authors and the data are vendor-context, we disclose this relationship in full and report the study as early, transparency-qualified evidence. The contribution is empirical: a rare multi-site, mixed-methods account of task redistribution after a generative AI HR deployment, offered with explicit attention to its limits and to the governance obligations, including high-risk AI rules, that such deployments now entail.

candidates.title: TrySee: Modular Perception-Enhanced VLM Grounding for Closed-Loop Robot Task Planning in Specialized Domains
candidates.abstract: Vision Language Models (VLMs) have shown impressive capabilities in high-level reasoning and task planning for robots. However, specialized domains remain a challenge for VLMs' image interpretation and grounding abilities. We introduce TrySee, a modular closed-loop robot task planning pipeline integrating general-purpose VLM reasoning with domain-specific perception and established robotics components. The system consists of an inherently reactive cyclic planning pipeline, augmented with domain-specific modular vision preprocessing, to provide online grounding. Finally, a dynamic preprocessing selection mechanism contributes to the scalability of the pipeline. The system requires neither VLM fine-tuning nor end-to-end demonstrations and adapts through replaceable perception modules and motion planning. The approach is evaluated on planning tasks across 5 widely different domains, including a real-world robot disassembly task. The field tests in a brownfield environment demonstrate the approach's practicality in integrating VLM planning into specialized robotic systems with limited domain-specific training data.

candidates.title: Liability for rogue behaviors of agentic AI
candidates.abstract: This article addresses liability for harm caused by rogue behaviors in agentic AI systems (AAI), such as specification gaming and deliberate deception. These harms stem from inherent AI vices-intrinsic, inevitable, and unpredictable rogue behaviors of AAI which cannot be fully eliminated with the current state of technological development. Current regulatory frameworks mainly focus on risk prevention but fail to address how liability should be allocated when harms do occur. In response, we conducted a game-theoretic analysis to study the optimal design of legal liability for unpredictable AAI harm caused by rogue behaviors under imperfect information. Our analysis shows that the optimal liability regime dynamically hinges on the explainability of the AAI system in question. Under this regime, courts can leverage industry-led explainability benchmarks to differentiate damages based on whether the developer can satisfactorily prove that the harm in question was caused by inherent vices. Under this arrangement, developers are incentivized to invest in explainability techniques to reduce both the risk of their AAI and their own liability exposure. Through this analysis, we demonstrate how a liability framework grounded in explainability can create economic incentives for developers to prioritize transparency and accountability of commercially available AAI.

candidates.title: Learning Interaction-Aware Path Corrections from Unlabeled Trajectories: A LiDAR-Based Sim-to-Real GNN Framework for Construction Robots
candidates.abstract: Construction robots operating near workers require navigation that can anticipate human motion while remaining robust to dynamic and unstructured site conditions. However, existing social navigation methods depend on hand-crafted interaction rules, labeled demonstrations, or robot-specific control policies, limiting their scalability and transferability in construction environments. We propose a real-time, LiDAR-only framework that learns interaction-aware path corrections from unlabeled demonstrations. Constant-velocity extrapolation generates residual learning targets, while a GNN models relationships among the robot, pedestrians, and goal context. During deployment, an extended Kalman filter tracks LiDAR detections to construct dynamic graphs, and the GNN offsets planner-generated waypoints through a planner-agnostic interface. Within the bricklaying trial, the GNN reduced path irregularity by 39.2\% and increased minimum TTC. Across Dynablox sequences, it increased minimum TTC by 38.3\% while producing shorter, smoother paths than the baselines. Ablation studies supported a 1.0-s prediction interval and confirmed the benefits of target context, reflection augmentation, and feature normalization.

candidates.title: Robust design of air chamber to enhance impact connection strength of magnetic connectors on modular truss robots
candidates.abstract: The connection mechanisms between neighboring modules are crucial subsystems in modular reconfigurable robot (MRR) systems. Magnetic connectors have been widely used for docking and undocking because of their mechanical simplicity and ease of use. However, they suffer from lower maximum tensile strength compared with mechanical docking mechanisms. This limitation is critical when modular truss robots are subjected to impact forces during locomotion, reconfiguration, docking, and undocking. To address this challenge, this paper presents a comprehensive parametric study and establishes design guidelines to maximize the impact resistance of magnetic connectors. As a core component of this approach, we investigate a mode-switching silicone air chamber designed to enhance impact absorption while mitigating the degradation of undocking capabilities. To evaluate the performance of the air chamber, we introduce an experimental evaluation method inspired by the Charpy impact test. Because the transient response of the soft structure is highly complex, the Taguchi and full factorial design method were employed to optimize the design parameters and derive the design guidelines. In the case of parameters, four factors were selected that could be judged to have an impact on the pneumatic stiffness, structural flexibility, and fluid damping of the air chamber. Also, each design parameter was divided into three levels, and five replicate experiments were conducted for each combination using an \(L_9(3^4)\) orthogonal array. The performance metrics consist of the sum of weighted values of \(M_1\) , which indicates the air chamber’s resistance to impact, and \(M_2\) , which reflects the indicator of mode switching between opening and closing the air chamber’s bottom hole. To explore the vicinity of the optimal value identified in the first experiment, a second experiment was conducted to pinpoint the final optimal parameter configuration, achieving a metric improvement of 0.051969 over the worst-case scenario. Finally, the practical feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed design guidelines were demonstrated through a hardware model using a prototype connector within a configured MRR system, demonstrating connection retention under selected impact conditions.

candidates.title: Fast and Robust Actuation of Continuum Robots via Antagonistic Tendons
candidates.abstract: Tendon driven continuum robots (TDCRs) exhibit extraordinary dexterity and navigability in highly constrained workspaces, for example, in minimally invasive surgery or industrial inspection and repair tasks. The curvilinear nature of these robots, with their extreme diameter-to-length ratios, enables them to dexterously navigate around obstacles in their environment to reach their goals. However, the dynamic properties of these highly deformable mechanisms make them challenging to operate autonomously at high speeds, and the presence of external loads can significantly impact the accuracy of kinematic models. In this work, we present a compact, low-cost, modular tendon robot actuation platform with fast and stable open-loop dynamics. We explore how pretensioned antagonistic pairs can enable repeatable actuation at high bandwidths using our low-cost hardware setup. Secondly, we show how intrinsic sensing using only motor currents and displacement can be used to improve the shape estimate of the robot when manipulating unknown objects at its tip, without any additional sensors. In this work, we show how high-performance continuum robots can be achieved with relatively low-cost components through the mechanical design of the actuation structure and by leveraging existing information available from the actuators in the computational modeling of these systems.

candidates.title: RoboJev: An Open Vision-Language Judge for Robot Success Detection
candidates.abstract: Many robot manipulation videos do not indicate whether the task was successfully completed. RoboJev-27B is an open-weight vision-language model that takes a task instruction, 10 frames of a manipulation attempt, and (if available) final frames from auxiliary cameras and predicts whether the robot accomplished the task. RoboJev-27B is a variant of JEV-27B-VL, trained with a rank-32 LoRA adapter on the language model only (keeping the vision encoder frozen) using 52,598 episode records. It also uses a source-specific KL penalty that applies only to research data, anchoring predictions closer to the original model on those sources. It uses a calibrated two-token readout that outputs success/failure probabilities in a single forward pass. On 268 held-out episodes of the same robot model (SO-101), RoboJev-27B attains 95.2% balanced accuracy and 0.993 AUROC. It also generalises to episodes collected by unseen labs/robots (AUROC = 0.890 over 459 episodes) as well as to clearly labelled community-collected episodes (accuracy = 93.3% over 135 episodes), where the base model attains an AUROC = 0.900 on the unseen-lab/robot subset with the same inputs. It takes 0.26 seconds per episode (median, serial) to infer on a single H100, which is about \$0.19 per 1,000 success predictions at \$2.69 per GPU-hour (not including media processing and serving costs). RoboJev-27B is released together with its inference code, along with a transparent evaluation: 20,628 predictions organized into 29 model/protocol entries are made available to facilitate browsing and to enable reproducible benchmarking of success detection. We also compare against strong API-based frontier VLMs, which take in fewer input frames (4 images from the primary camera only); note that this comparison is not strictly like-for-like because RoboJev-27B is given more frames at inference.

candidates.title: Memory-Aware Keyframe Management for Dense Maps on Memory-Constrained Robots
candidates.abstract: Running a language model and a dense 3D map on one device means the two share one memory, and exceeding its limit is an out-of-memory failure. Map systems that keep a bounded working set bound it by a count of keyframes, but the memory one keyframe occupies varies widely with what it carries, so a count does not control what the working set occupies. The unit of admission is as poorly matched, since a radius around the pose, a fixed cell, or the graph neighbors of the last matched keyframe all move parts of the map that are not needed. We therefore propose two decisions. First, the memory the resident map uses is bounded directly, and the cost of every admission is known before any data is read, from per-keyframe resident sizes computed offline and carried with the map. Second, keyframes are admitted and released at a semantic spatial unit, the rooms and corridors of the building, so that the robot holds the zone it occupies together with the zone it is about to enter while the zones it has passed are released. Every admission measures the resident total, makes room, and only then reads, so the budget is never overshot. On two NVIDIA Jetson boards the budget holds in every run and the model gives up at most 0.8 percent of its throughput, whereas without it the operating system kills the model or the map. Under that budget, and over the environments evaluated, admission by semantic zone localizes 6-9 points more of the query frames than a geometric partition of matched zone count and about twice as much as the retrieval of RTAB-Map, at a lower ATE. Bounding memory lets the map and the model coexist, and moving the map in semantic zones makes the bounded map usable.

candidates.title: An open-source, 3D-printable droplet microfluidics platform with strobe-enhanced microscopy
candidates.abstract: Droplet microfluidics underpins many single-cell, precision biomedical, and nanomaterial techniques. However, implementing these methods reproducibly remains challenging outside specialised laboratories due to high equipment costs, operational inflexibility, mechanical impracticality at the microscope stage, as well as open-source pumping solutions that are inadequately validated for low-flow stability. We present an accessible, research-grade, open-source droplet microfluidics platform integrating a compact, microfluidics-optimised microscopy stage with networked syringe-pump control. Designed for local digital fabrication, primarily 3D printing, and widely available components, the platform supports reproducible builds across diverse settings. This setup enables stable droplet generation, observation of rapid droplet dynamics, and automation-ready networked workflows. The microscopy module uses a Raspberry Pi camera and microsecond stroboscopic illumination to capture sharp images of fast-moving droplets without the need for a high-speed camera. A modular hardware interface and extensible, web-accessible software stack provide a path to integrate additional modules and laboratory automation beyond the configuration evaluated here. For infusion, we introduce an open-source syringe pump optimised for low reliable flow rather than maximum rates, combining gearbox-assisted stepper mechanics with workflow-centric control that enables manual intervention (keypad control) and remote operation (web interface and automation hooks). We benchmark droplet regimes, size tuning, and time-stability under low-flow conditions (between 25 and 2500 µL/h) relevant to advanced assays and demonstrate biomedical readiness through the encapsulation and incubation of cells, beads, and bacteria in monodisperse droplets. The platform has been replicated across laboratories in Latin America and globally, including independent builds, supporting reproducibility. All design files, firmware/software, analysis notebooks, and benchmark datasets are openly released.
