candidates.title: OPERATIONS AND PRODUCTION MANAGEMENT
candidates.abstract: Operations and production management concerns the design, coordination and control of processes through which enterprises transform resources into dependable goods and services. Its analytical difficulty lies in managing interacting constraints: demand is uncertain, capacity is finite, variability creates queues, physical assets deteriorate, and apparently efficient decisions may impose costs on workers, customers and the environment. This chapter develops a critical and applied treatment of twelve approved operations domains, integrating operations strategy, process analysis, the theory of constraints, lean production, forecasting, queueing, maintenance and sustainable operations. Through a transparent, purposive synthesis of seminal research, peer-reviewed studies, standards and official secondary evidence, it interprets Rwanda's 2024 Integrated Business Enterprise Survey and 2026 national accounts without confusing sectoral aggregates with individual enterprise performance. An explicitly hypothetical Kigali food producer illustrates capacity, overall equipment effectiveness, bottleneck improvement, location economics and operational measurement; a service counter demonstrates the nonlinear consequences of high utilization under stated queueing assumptions. The chapter offers original process and accountability diagrams, an operations-metric register, management decision instruments, and a Rwanda–Toyota comparative interpretation. It argues that operational excellence is not the maximization of utilization or elimination of every buffer. Rather, it is a context-sensitive capacity to meet legitimate demand reliably, learn from variation, protect people and resources, and maintain economically and ethically defensible performance. Proposed integrative relationships are conceptual and require empirical testing.

candidates.title: Design and Construction of a Low-Cost, Open-Source Syringe-Based Pipetting Robot Using 3D Printing and Common Hardware Parts
candidates.abstract: Abstract Automation in chemical laboratories improves the reproducibility, precision, and efficiency in liquid handling. A three-dimensional (3D)-printed, stepper-actuated pipetting robot was developed and tested via silver nitrate (AgNO3) experiments. The system employs a rigid 3D-printed frame to secure syringes and tubing, stepper motors for plunger actuation, and microcontroller-based software to automate the pipetting sequences. The robot was evaluated for volume accuracy, reproducibility, and mechanical reliability using 5 mL syringes. The results indicate consistent volume delivery and stable mechanical performance over multiple cycles. Detailed mechanical, electrical, and software specifications are provided to enable replication and customization in other laboratories.

candidates.title: Collision Avoidance Path Planning for Mobile Robots Using an Improved Bi-RRT Algorithm*
candidates.abstract: Abstract To address the high path redundancy, poor smoothness, and low planning efficiency exhibited by the Bi-directional Rapidly-exploring Random Tree (Bi-RRT) algorithm in complex dynamic environments, an improved Bi-RRT* algorithm for collision avoidance path planning in mobile robots is proposed. The method employs a Social LSTM network to predict the trajectories of dynamic obstacles. The predicted positions over a 3-second horizon are utilized to guide real-time obstacle avoidance decisions. A bidirectional target-biased sampling strategy and an adaptive step-size mechanism are adopted to enhance search efficiency and adaptability in dynamic environments. Additionally, a via-node optimization is introduced to eliminate redundant nodes in the initial path. Finally, the generated path is smoothed using a cubic Cardinal spline. Experimental results demonstrate that in mixed obstacle scenarios, the average planning time is reduced by 52.1%, the path length is shortened by 12.5%, the success rate reaches 96.7%, and the average curvature is decreased by 62.2% compared with the BD‑RRT algorithm. These findings validate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm in terms of real‑time performance, smoothness, and kinematic feasibility.

candidates.title: Visuomotor coordination on the road: Low-dimensional representations reveal adaptive, context-dependent reductions in the dimensionality of natural driving behavior
candidates.abstract: The brain's ability to transform complex, high-dimensional sensory and motor inputs into coordinated, goal-directed behavior remains a central challenge in neuroscience research. Current research suggests that behavior is generated through patterns within a low-dimensional structure. What visuomotor patterns underlie complex, unconstrained behaviors such as driving, and how stereotypical they are, remain poorly understood. Driving involves complex perception-action interactions, which we hypothesize are specific to the driver's role and adapt to task demands. Here, we unfold these dynamics using an immersive virtual drive that recreates ten hazardous on-road events. We collected eye, head, and vehicle movements from participants assigned to either a manual or an automated driving condition. From the behavioral movements of 284 drivers, we constructed a common time-resolved behavioral state space based on collective variance, computed via principal component analysis across participants. The obtained low-dimensional representation thus captures generalized visuomotor coordination strategies. We then characterized the evolving low-dimensional structure with cosine similarity and various measures of effective dimensionality. We tested whether leading components contained condition-specific information using discriminant analysis. Throughout the entire drive, few components accounted for most of the variance in behavior, and effective dimensionality decreased reliably around critical events, indicating tighter coordination between perceptual and motor variables. During periods of low effective dimensionality, the contributions of eye, head, steering, and vehicle heading reorganized toward leading dimensions in a task-dependent manner. Across events, between-subject similarity was partially stable and stronger among manual drivers. This reorganization also made behaviors more distinct across driving conditions, enabling better classification of driving modes using only the first two components. These results show that naturalistic driving is supported by shared low-dimensional visuomotor coordination strategies that are flexibly reshaped by contextual demands, and provide a principled behavioral framework for linking neural manifolds, human driver models, and the design of adaptive automated vehicles.

candidates.title: ORBIT: A Modular Multi-finger Robotic Hand Platform with Rotational Finger Reconfiguration
candidates.abstract: Despite the popularity of multi-fingered robotic hands for dexterous manipulation, there is no systematic platform to compare different hand morphologies against one another. We present ORBIT (Orbital Reconfigurable Base-actuated Integrated Theta-motion Hand), a modular platform designed to enable principled exploration of multi-fingered hand morphology. The core contribution of ORBIT is a rotating knuckle mechanism, where independent fingers travel around a cylindrical palm via a belt drive. This enables ORBIT to perform quick recon- figuration (< 1 s) of finger layout without hand disassembly. ORBITs a robust system, with finger average angular velocity of 1.57 rad / s1 and a root finger force resistance of 50 N. Using a three fingers instantiation of ORBIT, we demonstrate an initial pilot grasping study, comparing anthropomorphic, isometric, and Barrett-style finger layouts across eleven objects of varied size, shape, and texture. We further demonstrate how ORBITs nonanthropomorphic orbital DOF enables the achievement of tasks that would be difficult to perform with fixed-knuckle designs, such as cube face reorientation, lid threading, and precision pinching of sub-centimeter objects. These results establish ORBIT as a viable platform for direct apples to apples comparison of multi-fingered hand morphologies for specific manipulation tasks

candidates.title: Proceedings of NORA's Annual Meeting 2026
candidates.abstract: NORA - The Norwegian Artificial Intelligence Research Consortium - works to strengthen Norwegian research, education and innovation within the fields of AI, machine learning and robotics. NORA is a collaboration between 9 universities, 4 university colleges and 4 research institutes. The current article provides a summary of NORA’s annual conference 2026.

candidates.title: Offensive–Defensive Codesign
candidates.abstract: This chapter addresses the insufficiency of isolated offensive and defensive AI strategies in modern cybersecurity by proposing codesign through joint protocols and shared testbeds. Central to the framework is red/blue co-training, wherein adversarial and defensive agents evolve simultaneously through iterative cycles that mirror the continuous adaptation in real-world cyber conflict. Curriculum learning structures this coevolution by escalating scenario complexity—from basic credential theft and anomaly detection to multi-stage advanced persistent threats—preventing premature convergence and ensuring diverse skill formation. Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) formalizes competitive and cooperative dynamics under partial observability, with balanced reward structures that sustain adversarial pressure. Human-in-the-loop augmentation introduces expert oversight to correct unsafe behaviors, refine policy alignment, and enforce operational risk tolerances. Adversarial playgrounds—including simulated network environments, scenario-driven testing mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, dynamically adaptive topologies, and hybrid testbeds incorporating real hardware—provide controlled infrastructure for evaluating agent coevolution with high fidelity. Benchmark-governance charters, dataset provenance records, ablation requirements, and signed reproducibility packages enforce scientific rigor across co-training evaluations. A cross-national laboratory case study demonstrates how governed benchmarks, mandatory partner-lab replication, and transparent failure reporting produce credible, peer-reviewed findings, including traceable retractions. Incremental shadow-mode deployment and phased security information and event management (SIEM) integration complete the transition from laboratory codesign to operationally resilient practice.

candidates.title: From Static Classrooms to Living Systems
candidates.abstract: This chapter explores how Digital twins (DTs) are changing in their roles across the educational spectrum. DTs play both theoretical and practical roles, facilitating immersive, feedback-intensive and personal experiences beyond traditional simulations. DTs in life sciences and agricultural engineering enable safe, repeatable and data-rich learning environments where learners can practice realistic simulations of poultry farm management, disease control and performance analytics without endangering living animals in the laboratory. DTs have been applied to reinvent introductory programming education in computing education. DTs have been identified as potential solutions for schools in developing countries such as Mozambique and Rwanda that lack physical laboratory facilities. In chemical engineering education, virtual reality twins of extraction columns enable interactive manipulation of flow parameters and AI-based image analysis to optimize droplet size, introducing students to the fusion of process control and data analytics in an accessible, hardware-light format.

candidates.title: Replication Package for the Paper "Evolving Agentic Configuration Artifacts in the Open-Source: An Empirical Study"
candidates.abstract: Replication package of the paper "Evolving Agentic Configuration Artifacts in the Open-Source: An Empirical Study" (anonymous submission). The study mines the agentic configuration files of 45,333 GitHub repositories, with their git history: agent skills, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, Copilot instructions, Claude Code subagents and commands, rules, settings, hooks and MCP configurations. An LLM labels the files and their contents. The analyses measure:- what skills contain and where they are used (RQ1);- how they are maintained after their introduction (RQ2);- which files change together with them (RQ3);- the activity of repositories after they adopt agentic files. The package holds the mined dataset, the data derived from it, the final codebooks, every result as data, the scripts that produced them (comments removed), the prompts sent to the model, and the study design (methodology.pdf). README.md describes every folder. Files- One zip per folder: codebooks, prompts, data_collection, extra_counts, qualitative_analysis, quantitative_analysis, results_catalog.- The two largest folders as multi-volume RAR archives: Data (Data.part01.rar to Data.part09.rar) and work (work.part01.rar to work.part41.rar).- Not archived: README.md, methodology.pdf, requirements.txt, the licenses and the checksums. Rebuilding the packageDownload all files into one folder. Extract there every zip and the first volume of each RAR archive (Data.part01.rar, work.part01.rar); WinRAR, 7-Zip or unrar read the other volumes. The result is the folder described in README.md, about 50 GB. The scripts need Python 3.12 and Node.js 24 (requirements.txt and the package.json files). Checksums (SHA-256)- CHECKSUMS.sha256: every file of the package- zips.sha256: the zips- parts.sha256: the Data volumes- work_parts.sha256: the work volumes LicensesData under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA.txt), code under MIT (LICENSE-CODE.txt). Mined contents keep the license of their repository.

candidates.title: Robust and accessible in situ sequencing with an open-source automated sequencer
candidates.abstract: Abstract Targeted in situ sequencing underlies many spatial transcriptomic, barcoded connectomic, and multiplexed perturbation techniques. Each experiment requires many cycles of chemical reactions and imaging that are time-consuming and error-prone to perform manually, and few commercial platforms can sequence highly diverse RNA barcodes in situ at cellular resolution across large tissue sections. Here we present Seq-o-Matic, an open-source automated in situ sequencer built entirely from commercially available components, which integrates fluidics, heated incubation, and imaging of up to three continuous 18 mm × 50 mm areas on standard microscope slides. Relative to manual sequencing, Seq-o-Matic reduced hands-on time 6-to 17.5-fold and total run time about 2.6-fold. Across three runs spanning two mouse strains and a neonatal marmoset, sequencing quality, measured by signal retention, channel specificity, and phasing, was similar to that of four manually sequenced mouse brains. In four mouse hemispheres sequenced in separate runs (two C57BL/6J, one NOD, and one WSB), consensus cell types were present in every brain and corresponded to those of a manually sequenced C57BL/6J brain. Within cortical excitatory neurons, the two C57BL/6J brains were more similar to each other than were brains of different strains, suggesting that technical variation between runs was small relative to strain differences. Seq-o-Matic thus makes consistent, high-throughput in situ sequencing accessible to laboratories without specialized in situ sequencing expertise.

candidates.title: Crypto airdrops as post-speculative finance: A digital methods study of platform-mediated value in digital cultures
candidates.abstract: Abstract Crypto-finance permeates digital culture through platforms like YouTube and Telegram, transforming how financial value is produced, circulated, and legitimised. This article examines crypto airdrops – token distributions that reward users for blockchain transactions, Web3 gameplay, and online engagement – as a key site where finance becomes embedded in digital culture. What might initially appear as a niche crypto practice generates substantial platform-mediated financial participation. Across the seven airdrop campaigns documented on YouTube and Telegram, we identify a transnational and multilingual community that consistently produces, circulates and engages with airdrop-related content. Drawing on quali-quantitative digital methods, we map the communicative, visual, and algorithmic labour through which users perform eligibility for token rewards, and trace how cultures of participation sustain token value. Our findings reveal a structural shift from speculative hype cycles to labour-intensive participation, underpinned by new forms of governance, legitimacy and financial subjectivation. We argue that airdrops exemplify a post-speculative modality of finance: a structural reorganisation of speculation around prescribed labour, platform-mediated coordination, and the distributed cultural work of users. The article contributes to debates on the social logics of finance, platform governance, and the transformation of financial subjectivity.

candidates.title: Discovering supernovae in the Virgo Cluster during the LSST era
candidates.abstract: In the era of unprecedentedly wide, deep and high-cadence sky surveys the chance for discovering new explosive transients in nearby, rich galaxy clusters within hours after explosion is expected to increase dramatically. In this paper we focus on the Virgo cluster ($D \simeq 16.5$ Mpc), and estimate the expected numbers of new, very young supernovae in different sub-structures and galaxy types of the cluster during the proposed lifetime (~10 years) of the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST) by the Vera Rubin Observatory. These predictions will be tested observationally during the ongoing Shadow-LSST discovery and follow-up program led by University of Arizona in the upcoming years.

candidates.title: UMaPP: Universal Maize Phenotyping Platform - A low-cost, open-source robotic manipulator-based imaging system for three-dimensional maize reconstruction and trait measurement
candidates.abstract: This repository provides the CAD design files, control software, and experimental output data associated with the Universal Maize Phenotyping Platform (UMaPP), a low-cost, open-source robotic imaging system developed for non-destructive 3D maize phenotyping. UMaPP uses a modified robotic manipulator, a single RGB camera, and controlled illumination to acquire multi-view images for photogrammetric 3D reconstruction. The repository includes hardware designs, software for automated image acquisition and robotic control, and experimental results used to evaluate plant architectural traits, including plant height and leaf length. These resources are shared to support reproducibility, system replication, and further development of open-source plant phenotyping technologies.

candidates.title: FLORA: An Open Model Suite for Scaling Robotics Data Engines
candidates.abstract: The life-cycle of robotics foundation models crucially depends on data labels. Outcome reward labels are needed for monitoring real-world deployments. Process reward labels are needed during RL post-training. Timestamped captions are needed for filtering and balancing pretraining data. We present Flora, an industrial-quality data engine used for training GR00T models, that simultaneously covers these capabilities. Flora achieves SOTA scores on the captioning benchmark WGO-Bench and reward benchmarks RoboReward and Robometer. On internal benchmarks it is competitive with GPT-6 Astra while beating other frontier models. The model is substantially cheaper than API-based alternatives, roughly 125 times cheaper than GPT-6 Astra. Florais battle tested at scale, labeling 200,000 hours of data per day across 512 GB300s. By open-sourcing our data engine, we enable researchers to scale custom robotics datasets and explore emerging applications such as physical auto-research and human-to-robot transfer.

candidates.title: Benefits and Harms of Adult Videos: A Sex Difference Social Representations Analysis Among Young Adults in Japan
candidates.abstract: Pornhub Insights (2025) reported that Japan ranked 11th worldwide in total traffic, indicating widespread use of adult videos (AV). Existing research has primarily focused on AV-related harms from expert and Western perspectives. Few studies examine how Japanese young adults perceive these effects, particularly the benefits that sustain use, and sex differences remain underexplored. This study investigated the core social representations of AV benefits and harms and how they differ by sex. Data were collected from 251 Japanese participants, of whom 137 (54.6%) were male, with a mean age of 20.71 years. Most participants (81.3%) reported using AV, and most identified as heterosexual students. Data were analyzed using prototypical analysis to identify elements with high consensus. Five key observations emerged: (1) Both genders see "satisfaction," "pleasure," and "crime prevention" as key benefits of AV. (2) Sex differences appeared in describing benefits, with men mentioning "sex education" and women mentioning "stress relief." (3) Both genders identified "incorrect knowledge" as a primary representation of AV-related harms. (4) Male respondents cited "addiction" as a harm, whereas female respondents were more likely to reference "encouraging sexual crime." (5) More words or phrases were used to describe AV benefits than harms. These findings may inform targeted interventions and policy discussions.

candidates.title: Political talk in nonpolitical digital spaces
candidates.abstract: In recent years, scholars in communication and media studies have increasingly turned their attention to political discourse that emerges incidentally within ostensibly nonpolitical digital contexts. These political discussions not only permeate diverse online platforms and communities, but also carry significant democratic potential. Despite growing interest in the phenomenon, existing research remains fragmented across distinct theoretical traditions and lacks a coherent conceptual understanding. This article addresses that gap by reviewing studies in three epistemological orientations – post-positivist, interpretive, and critical – that can guide the analysis of political talk in nonpolitical digital environments. In doing so, it highlights how this group of phenomena can be understood and interpreted with different theoretical assumptions, thereby enabling scholars to better assess their communicative and political significance. This review offers a foundation for more integrative and theoretically informed research on the various dimensions of political expression in digital networked publics.

candidates.title: Cableless Power Transmission System : Problems and Prospects
candidates.abstract: Abstract Cableless power transmission—the transfer of electrical energy through free space rather than a conductor—now spans commodity near-field chargers, standardized electric-vehicle (EV) charging, kilometre-scale microwave and laser beaming, and in-orbit tests of space-based solar power. Existing reviews usually treat one mechanism, quote peak efficiencies without their geometric conditions, and rarely connect performance to exposure regulation or cost. This paper develops a unified framework covering inductive, resonant, capacitive, microwave and laser links. A generalized three-layer system architecture (power, control–communication, safety) is defined. Near-field links are modeled from the Neumann integral to the closed-form bound η max = F/(1 + √(1 + F)) 2 with F = k 2 Q 1 Q 2 ; far-field links through the Goubau relation η b = 1 − exp(−τ 2 ); optical links through Gaussian-beam propagation with Beer–Lambert extinction; and all mechanisms through a common end-to-end efficiency cascade and a levelized cost of transmission (LCOT). Simulations show that coupling decays approximately as d −3 , that 90% coil-to-coil efficiency at Q = 300 is limited to gaps of about 22 cm for a 20-cm-radius pad, that a 10-km, 5.8-GHz link needs apertures of about 36 m at each end for 98% beam capture, and that a well-engineered microwave chain delivers about 51% end to end. A 1-MW, 10-km island case study gives an LCOT roughly twice that of a submarine cable, offset by a much shorter repair time. The problems are classified as fundamental, engineering, regulatory and economic, and a staged prospect roadmap is proposed.

candidates.title: Social chatbots and character: Mind-modelling, mimetics, and postdigital misperception
candidates.abstract: This article examines how users cognitively process social chatbot output as a novel form of participatory, generative “character,” co-produced through human–AI interaction. Reporting on the results of empirical research on user responses to the social chatbot platform character.ai, it shows how cognitive stylistic and narratological approaches to character can be utilised but also must be developed to analyse and theorise users’ experience of and interaction with generative AI agents. It makes specific contributions to cognitive stylistics, rhetorical narratology, character studies, and research on gen AI chatbots by: (1) illustrating how the concept of mind-modelling can used to analyse the ways in which users linguistically anthropomorphise social chatbots; (2) developing two new audience response types – transmimetic and hypermimetic – to respectively capture ways in which users assess chatbots against prior knowledge of characters across media and cases where chatbots appear so convincingly human that users question their ontological status; (3) proposing the concept of ‘postdigital misperception’ to reflect the way that users of AI can misattribute the ontological origin of an LLM’s output. The article demonstrates how social chatbots are reshaping how users understand character, agency, and reality in interactive, participatory and generative digital contexts and argues that social chatbots epitomise postdigital experience in blurring the distinction between the digital and non-digital as well as fictional and real.

candidates.title: Why Bother Me Again? Benchmarking Personal Agent Memory for Interaction Preferences
candidates.abstract: Personal intelligence systems are taking on increasingly complex everyday tasks, yet repeated questions, unnecessary confirmations, and unwanted outreach can turn capable assistance into interaction burden. Reducing this burden requires agents to remember how users want to be assisted. However, existing memory benchmarks focus on factual recall and personalized answers and rarely test how agents learn and act on interaction preferences. We introduce MemPABench, an interactive environment for on-policy evaluation of memory in personal agents. MemPABench poses long-horizon tasks requiring agents to decide when to clarify, confirm, or act autonomously. Four grounded simulated users hold 14 preferences across work and personal contexts. Their feedback spans 99 sessions over four months, with five event-driven changes per user testing memory updates. We evaluate preference selection, delivered behavior, and sensitivity to context and preference change. Evaluating four memory systems across four LLM backbones, we find that current memory brings limited gains in preference selection. Retrieval-based systems (i.e. Mem0, MemOS, simple RAG) do not outperform No Memory, while File-based memory improves accuracy but applies preferences beyond relevant contexts. Our analysis shows that current memory struggles to retrieve interaction preferences and adapt to preference changes. Even with the correct preference available, overriding the agent's default interaction habits remains challenging. The environment and dataset are available at https://mempabench.com.

candidates.title: Tactile-Based Robotic Manipulation: From Mechanics-Driven to Data-Driven Perspectives
candidates.abstract: Tactile sensing provides robots with direct access to physical interactions at the contact interface, making it a critical modality for robust and dexterous manipulation. Over the past several decades, tactile-based manipulation research has evolved from mechanics-driven approaches, which explicitly interpret tactile signals through contact mechanics and task-specific reasoning, to data-driven approaches that learn tactile representations and manipulation policies directly from data. This article reviews the development of tactile-based manipulation from these two complementary perspectives. We first introduce the fundamentals of tactile sensing and then review, from a mechanics-driven perspective, how those signals form manipulation-relevant state representations and subsequently influence the robot action. We then examine the recent advances in data-driven tactile manipulation, covering imitation learning, reinforcement learning, vision–language–action models, and predictive models. Finally, we discuss open challenges and future opportunities toward scalable, generalizable, and robust tactile-enabled robotic systems.

candidates.title: AI-Based Elderly Health Monitoring and Emergency Assistance Robot
candidates.abstract: The increasing demand for elderly healthcare has encouraged the development of smart assistive technologies that support independent living and improve patient safety. This review paper examines existing research on intelligent healthcare solutions, focusing on vital sign monitoring, fall detection, medication management, and robotic assistance. It evaluates the techniques used in these systems, highlighting their major benefits, technical limitations, and areas requiring further investigation. The review identifies the need for a unified solution capable of combining multiple healthcare functions rather than relying on separate devices or applications. To address this gap, an AI-based elderly health monitoring and emergency assistance robot is proposed, integrating health sensors, intelligent event detection, and IoT-enabled communication. The proposed approach aims to facilitate timely emergency notifications, improve caregiver accessibility, and provide a more reliable support system for elderly individuals.

candidates.title: InstMeter: An Instruction-Level Method to Predict Energy and Latency of DL Model Inference on MCUs
candidates.abstract: Deep learning (DL) models can now run on microcontrollers (MCUs). Through neural architecture search (NAS), we can search DL models that meet the constraints of MCUs. Among various constraints, energy and latency costs of the model inference are critical metrics. To predict them, existing research relies on coarse proxies such as multiply-accumulations (MACs) and model's input parameters, often resulting in inaccurate predictions or requiring extensive data collection. In this paper, we propose InstMeter, a predictor leveraging MCUs' clock cycles to accurately estimate the energy and latency of DL models. Clock cycles are fundamental metrics reflecting MCU operations, directly determining energy and latency costs. Furthermore, a unique property of our predictor is its strong linearity, allowing it to be simple and accurate. We thoroughly evaluate InstMeter under different scenarios, MCUs, and software settings. Compared with state-of-the-art studies, InstMeter can reduce the energy and latency prediction errors by 3× and 6.5×, respectively, while requiring 100× and 10× less training data. In the NAS scenario, InstMeter can fully exploit the energy budget, identifying optimal DL models with higher inference accuracy. We also evaluate InstMeter's generalization performance through various experiments on three ARM MCUs (Cortex-M4, M7, M33) and one RISC-V-based MCU (ESP32-C3), different compilation options (-Os, -O2), GCC versions (v7.3, v10.3), application scenarios (keyword spotting, image recognition), dynamic voltage and frequency scaling, temperatures (21°C, 43°C), and software settings (TFLMv2.4, TFLMvCI). Our source codes and the MCU-specific benchmark datasets are available here: https://github.com/haoliu001/InstMeter.

candidates.title: Safety analysis of the Weigao laparoscopic surgical robot for renal cyst decortication via transperitoneal and retroperitoneal approaches
candidates.abstract: Objective To evaluate the efficacy and conduct a safety analysis of the Chinese domestically produced Weigao Micro Hand laparoscopic surgical robot in renal cyst decortication via transperitoneal and retroperitoneal approaches. Methods Clinical data were collected from 63 patients with renal cysts who underwent robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery between May 2023 and July 2025. Among them, 31 patients were treated via the transperitoneal approach and 32 patients were treated via the retroperitoneal approach. Clinical characteristics, as well as surgical and short-term postoperative outcomes, were prospectively collected and analyzed. Results Both the transperitoneal and the retroperitoneal approaches were successfully completed without conversion to open surgery or other unplanned interventions. No statistically significant differences were observed between the two approaches in terms of the operative time (66.13 ± 24.99 min vs. 77.50 ± 27.62 min) or postoperative hospital stay (3.87 ± 1.48 days vs. 4.56 ± 1.08 days). The retroperitoneal approach was associated with significantly less intraoperative blood loss (15.68 ± 4.64 mL vs. 11.78 ± 3.80 mL, P < 0.05), whereas the transperitoneal approach was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative drainage duration (2.10 ± 0.98 days vs. 3.13 ± 1.62 days, P < 0.05). Conclusion The application of the Weigao robotic surgical system in renal cyst decortication demonstrates favorable feasibility and safety. With respect to surgical approach selection, both techniques have their respective advantages and disadvantages. Given the continuity of laparoscopic experience, considerations for surgical safety, and the benefit of more refined manipulation afforded by the robotic system, the retroperitoneal approach currently appears to be the preferable option. Clinical Trial Registration https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=223823 , identifier ChiCTR2400081949.

candidates.title: The Life of a Showgirl as a Cultural Artifact: What's Hidden by the Lipstick and Lace?
candidates.abstract: This paper develops a collage-based framework to holistically assess Taylor Swift’s highly anticipated first release after the Eras Tour concluded. The Life of a Showgirl, with sparkling promotional materials leading up to its October 2025 drop and polarizing critical reception following it, represents an entertainer’s lifestyle while still concealing what was alluded to behind the Eras Tour curtain. Rather than engage in a direct response to Showgirl, I critically evaluate positive and negative commentary from listeners regarding the album, and I thematically analyze lyrical concepts throughout Swift’s discography to contextualize Showgirl within the arc of her work. I find that discussion of The Life of a Showgirl is rooted in four primary topics that I refer to as Muse, Lyricism, Artistic Integrity, and Political Implications, and I place notable significance on listener-driven aspects of the Showgirl era. I further argue that such discourse constitutes important pedagogical processes and reinforces pop culture as not only entertainment or commercialization, but as a broad infrastructure for learning outside of formal settings. Listeners of The Life of a Showgirl and consumers of related media negotiate complex ideas about authenticity, authority, and creative labor.

candidates.title: Interpretation of National Values in Uzbek Theater: Historical Evolution and Modern Processes
candidates.abstract: This article analyzes the organic connection between national values and Uzbek theater from historical, theoretical, and practical perspectives. It provides a scholarly examination of the ways in which national values, traditions, and spiritual-enlightenment ideas have been interpreted on stage throughout the various stages of the formation and development of Uzbek national theater—encompassing the era of Jadidism, the Soviet period, and the era of independence.

candidates.title: Flexible Language-Guided Representation Editing for Adaptive Robot Behavior
candidates.abstract: Trajectory demonstrations show robots how to behave but not why, leaving them to guess which features of the task actually matter. Incorrect guesses produce misaligned internal representations and lead to incorrect robot behaviors. Because task features are often semantically defined, we argue that natural language is better suited for specifying features rather than relying on demonstrations. Although existing representation editing methods have proposed using language to specify new features, only allowing additive edits produces feature sets that are often over-specified or too narrowly scoped, especially in sequential editing tasks. We propose the Flexible Feature Editing Pipeline (FLEX), which uses language models to iteratively refine a robot's internal representation of task features from natural language corrections via three complementary operations: Add missing features, Generalize existing specific features, and Mask irrelevant features. We evaluate FLEX on 2D navigation scenarios, 7DoF Franka tabletop manipulation tasks, and a real-world study using naturalistic human language corrections and real-robot demonstrations. Comparisons against single-operation and unscaffolded baselines show that all three operations are necessary in interactive scenarios, and that FLEX achieves consistently higher normalized reward compared to other feature editing approaches while maintaining compact, transferable representations. Project available at https://mit-clear-lab.github.io/FLEX/

candidates.title: From “how” to learn to “what” to learn in multiagent systems and robotics
candidates.abstract: Abstract There remains much more to Artificial Intelligence than understanding how to learn with neural networks. Inspired in part by how babies, and humans in general, tend to choose for themselves what (and when ) to learn in addition to how to learn, this article discusses similar opportunities, in the areas of multiagent systems and robotics. Grounded in past research on the topic, it categorizes opportunities for choosing what to learn as coming from task decomposition or simplification for difficult problems and/or large environments; unsupervised pre‐training of representations and priors; multiagent learning; and learning from human interaction. The article is based closely on a keynote talk with the same title, delivered at the AAAI‐2026 conference in Singapore on January 22nd, 2026.

candidates.title: inr2action: Encoding Robot Episodes as Neural Implicit Representations for Recall and Action
candidates.abstract: Long-horizon robotic operation requires memory that scales with essential information rather than execution time. We present a parameter-space memory framework where each episode is stored as a separable object. A neural implicit representation is fitted to episode video from a shared, meta-learned initialization; the resulting weight delta constitutes the memory. Crucially, this delta remains a fixed size regardless of whether the episode spans a hundred or a hundred thousand frames. A learned projector maps the weight delta into token embeddings, conditioning a language model for question answering and a decoder for joint command regression, without frame retrieval at query time. On RoboMME, the language model exceeds chance across all question types, and the decoder achieves a mean $R^2$ of 0.51. Replacing the delta with matched noise drops performance by 11.4 points, while random-origin weights are non-decodable, proving the meta-learned initialization is essential for embedding episode content. By representing individual experiences as fixed-size weight deltas in a common parameter space, this approach decouples memory cost from time horizon and provides a basis for scalable streaming memory.

candidates.title: UniWALM: Unified World Action Language Model for Embodied Robot Control
candidates.abstract: Motivated by the human ability to integrate experience across language, perception, and action, we introduce UniWALM, a unified world-action-language model that learns video, action, and language in a single shared representation, where each modality is both a conditioning signal and a supervision target. We ask: can jointly generating language enrich this shared representation, improving manipulation and supporting memory-dependent behavior? Unlike prior approaches that attach a reasoning or vision-language model to a video-action backbone and run them as distinct stages, UniWALM unifies all three modalities inside a single mixture-of-transformers backbone whose per-modality diffusion heads co-denoise synchronously, decoding subtask and textual memory in the same pass as action with no separate planning stage; the generated language is re-consumed on the next step, closing a language-as-memory loop without an external planner or memory bank. To keep the action stream reliable under this richer objective, we further introduce Flow Matching with Correction (FMC), a training objective that teaches recovery from perturbed action trajectories at no inference-time cost. UniWALM consistently improves over same-backbone baselines (e.g., FastWAM) on compositional pick-and-place (MolmoSpaces) and across the memory-dependent subset of RMBench, where it reaches 34.5% without any pretrained language or reasoning model and exceeds Mem-0's keyframe-equipped setup (28.5%) using only a single anchor frame. On a real-world Find-the-Item task, generating textual memory lifts success from 11.1% to 61.1%, while state-of-the-art VLAs stay at or below chance (<=33.3%).

candidates.title: T-WLA: Bridging Slow Vision and Fast Touch
candidates.abstract: In contact-rich manipulation, contact conditions can change before a visual policy updates its action plan. Recomputing the plan through the visual policy adds latency, while tactile feedback alone does not specify how the ongoing motion should be revised for the task. We introduce T-WLA, a world-language-action architecture that uses shared visual memory to guide both action generation and tactile correction. At each visual update, the visual branch integrates the current image, task instruction, and retrieved history into a visual memory that conditions base-action generation. The same memory is cached for a lightweight tactile editor, which combines it with the active action chunk and incoming touch to predict residual corrections to unexecuted actions without rerunning the visual branch. Future-image and future-pressure prediction provide training-only supervision, encouraging the visual memory and tactile features to capture interaction dynamics relevant to action generation and correction. We evaluate T-WLA on tactile-conditioned hand-motion prediction using EgoTouch and Tachin, and on four real-world dexterous manipulation tasks. T-WLA reduces finger-joint MPJPE by 30% relative to the strongest reported baseline and achieves an average success rate of approximately 50.0% across real-robot manipulation tasks. Videos and code are available at https://anonymous-submission-20.github.io/T-WLA.github.io/.

candidates.title: Edge AI and IoT-enabled livestock intrusion detection and automated farm protection using YOLOv8s and MQTT-enabled event notification
candidates.abstract: Abstract Precision livestock farming relies on intelligent sensing and automated decision-making to reduce economic losses from livestock intrusion. Existing systems typically handle visual detection or IoT notification separately, limiting real-time autonomous response. This paper presents an Edge AI and IoT framework that integrates YOLOv8s-based cattle detection with MQTT-driven event communication and automated physical actuation. The system combines a real-time object detection engine, Python-based orchestration, MQTT communication, an ESP32 controller, cloud notification services, and acoustic deterrence into a unified cyber-physical architecture. The model was trained on a Roboflow cattle dataset using transfer learning under Ultralytics YOLOv8. Experimental results show a Precision of 0.8039, Recall of 0.6846, F1-score of 0.7394, mAP@50 of 0.8094, and mAP@50:95 of 0.5347. Average inference latency was 132.16 ms, while MQTT transmission required only 0.21 ms. This study demonstrates the feasibility of integrating visual perception, IoT communication, automated notification, and real-time physical intervention for autonomous livestock intrusion monitoring.

candidates.title: TorchRef : an open-source PyTorch framework for crystallographic refinement
candidates.abstract: Abstract Macromolecular crystallographic refinement underpins structural biology, yet existing software packages often lack accessible, modular codebases amenable to rapid method development. Here, we introduce TorchRef, a PyTorch-based crystallographic refinement framework that exposes all refinable parameters, atomic coordinates, displacement parameters, occupancies, and scale factors to automatic differentiation. The framework implements FFT-based structure-factor calculations, the French-Wilson treatment of intensities, bulk-solvent modeling with established mask parameters, and stereochemical restraints from the CCP4 Monomer Library. A modular target architecture allows loss functions to be combined, weighted, and extended independently of the core refinement machinery. Validation against 1,000 PDB structures demonstrates that TorchRef-based refinement reproduces a median R-free within 1% of Phenix while maintaining comparable model quality. Structure factor calculation in TorchRef scales readily across multiple CPU cores and is over 100 times faster on modern GPUs than CCTBX. To showcase how modern methods like time-resolved crystallography can benefit from the flexibility that TorchRef provides, we implemented direct refinement of a typical time-resolved model against amplitude differences, a use case currently not explored by classic refinement programs. TorchRef is released under the MIT license with full API documentation and tutorials, providing an accessible platform for developing and testing new crystallographic refinement protocols. Synopsis TorchRef is an open-source PyTorch-based crystallographic refinement framework that exposes all refinable parameters to automatic differentiation, delivers GPU-accelerated structure-factor evaluation more than 100× faster than CCTBX, and enables new workflows, such as direct refinement against amplitude differences in time-resolved crystallography.

candidates.title: AnthroPop: Fan-Art and the Serious Play of Engaging Students in Anthropological Thinking
candidates.abstract: This practice in action report reviews an introductory level anthropology course that focuses on fan-art as a medium of discursive power. It illustrates how courses centered on popular culture themes have the potential to impact contemporary challenges to the discipline of anthropology in nuanced ways. At the same time, it offers an opportunity to rethink both how we define the discipline to ourselves as well as our students.

candidates.title: Anthropology is Worldbuilding: Rogue Praxes of Imaginative and Playful Pedagogy
candidates.abstract: This special issue, Praxis, Pedagogy, and Popular Culture: The Case for Making Anthropology “Fun”, presents a series of dynamic perspectives on how pedagogical praxis in anthropology engages students as Homo ludens, where playful, curious, and imaginative learners are engaged with content and course design rooted in popular culture, music, media, and gamification. Such teaching methods reflect anthropology’s long-standing tradition of worldbuilding, evident in the holistic praxis of Boasian anthropology. Tying anthropology’s propensity for worldbuilding to students’ pre-existing cultural knowledge provides an exciting entry point for courses structured to present theories and concepts that activate their creative and playful energies in ways that resist political incursion into the classroom. In a globalized technoscape, students in the classrooms featured in this special issue of Teaching Anthropology navigate contemporary concerns through a playful pedagogy of pop culture, forming meaningful webs of significance that shape their understanding of reality. The worlds generated in fantasy, science fiction, and popular media are alternative visions of reality, spaces full of imaginative possibilities and ontological potentiality that invoke Homo ludens to learn. In short, playful pedagogies are a powerful rogue praxis.

candidates.title: Are Pink Robots for Girls? Children’s Gender-Related Toy Preference Toward Robotic Toys
candidates.abstract: Abstract This study examined toy preferences among children aged 3–5 years (recruited from August to October 2025, in Japan), focusing on their choices between humanoid robotic toys and dolls. In Study 1, children ( n = 162; 81 boys and 81 girls; age range = 36–67 months) were asked to choose between commercially available humanoid robots, typically perceived as male, alongside same-gender dolls. Boys preferred robots over boy dolls, whereas girls preferred girl dolls over robots (η 2 = .488); however, the preference for dolls among 5-year-old girls was only marginally significant (Cohen’s d = 0.464). In Study 2, girls ( n = 183, age range = 36–69 months) were presented with AI-generated, girl-oriented humanoid robots, designed to increase their interest. Only a weak shift was observed toward robot preference (η 2 = .011). Notably, 3-year-olds did not show a significant preference for dolls (Cohen’s d = 0.306), suggesting that early exposure to girl-oriented robots could foster greater interest in robotics during early childhood. Overall, the findings indicate that classical gender-related toy preferences persist among 3- to 5-year-olds, even when new technological toys are introduced. Modifying robots’ colors and facial features to appear more girl-oriented was insufficient to significantly enhance girls’ interest.

candidates.title: 3D printed robot tool changer
candidates.abstract: Collaborative robots (cobots) are increasingly adopted in research and industrial settings for multi-functional manipulation tasks. A key enabler of this flexibility is the automatic tool changer, yet commercially available systems remain prohibitively expensive and price out most research laboratory environments. This project addresses that gap through the design, manufacture, and validation of a low-cost and robot-agnostic passive automatic tool changer. The tool changer is designed to be manufactured only from 3D-Printed PLA and standard hardware components, and to have a total unit cost less than AUD $25. It was evaluated against metrics of positional repeatability, tool use capability, and coupling retention strength. 300 tool changing cycles were conducted using the Universal Robots UR5 manipulator, with no failures observed and no damage to the unit recorded. The average tool changing cycle time in these trials was 7.33 seconds. The design has been made open-source and freely available to the academic community.Printable files, assembly instructions and bill of materials are included in this collection.

candidates.title: Autonomous Industrial Inspection with Quadruped Robots: A Systematic Literature Review
candidates.abstract: Quadruped robots are increasingly used for industrial inspection because they can traverse stairs, clutter, and uneven terrain built for people. This paper presents a Systematic Literature Review (SLR), following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines, of autonomous inspection with quadruped robots validated on physical hardware. Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library were searched between 13 and 16 August 2026 for studies published from 2018 to 2026. Of 745 unique records and 1 study found through citation searching, 88 full-text reports were assessed against explicit eligibility criteria and an eight-criterion quality rubric, three criteria of which (mission focus, autonomy integration, and environmental fidelity) acted as eligibility gates; 32 studies were included. They were synthesized narratively by mission control, localization and mapping, navigation, active inspection, and validation approach. Robots reach inspection targets in real facilities, mostly on commercial platforms with vendor or open-source LiDAR localization, but only 4 of the 32 studies let inspection results change the mission, only 3 quantify localization accuracy on hardware, 14 report no statistics over repeated runs, and 27 provide no public code or data. The evidence is limited by single-reviewer selection, short deployments, heterogeneous metrics, and a likely bias toward successful demonstrations.

candidates.title: Electroluminescence image-based photovoltaic defect severity classification using convolutional neural network architectures and ensemble learning
candidates.abstract: Accurate fault detection and defect severity classification in photovoltaic (PV) modules are essential for predictive maintenance and reliable energy production. Electroluminescence (EL) imaging provides a fast, non-contact, and effective approach for identifying internal defects in PV cells, including cracks, inactive regions, and structural abnormalities. However, automatic severity classification remains challenging due to class imbalance and subtle visual differences between intermediate defect levels. This study investigated transfer learning using several convolutional neural network (CNN) architectures, including ResNet18, ResNet34, VGG16, VGG19, and EfficientNet-B0, for multi-class PV defect severity classification using publicly available EL images within a unified experimental framework. Among the individual models, VGG16 achieved the best test performance with an accuracy of 74.54% and a macro-F1 score of 0.56, indicating that single CNN models remain insufficiently robust for reliable multi-class severity classification, particularly under class imbalance and overlapping severity levels. To address these limitations, ensemble learning was employed to combine complementary CNN models, significantly improving classification performance to approximately 90% accuracy and 0.84 macro-F1. In addition, gradient-weighted class activation mapping analysis was used to provide qualitative insight into the regions of the EL images that influenced model predictions. The ensemble models produced visually consolidated and interpretable attention patterns across the representative samples compared with the individual models. Overall, the proposed ensemble-based framework provides a practical and computationally efficient approach for improving PV defect severity classification using EL imaging.

candidates.title: A data‐augmented meta‐learning framework for few‐shot fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions
candidates.abstract: Abstract Industrial process monitoring and fault diagnosis are essential for ensuring high‐quality production and safe operation in manufacturing systems. However, insufficient labelled data, imbalanced fault samples, and frequent changes in operating conditions limit the diagnostic performance and generalization capability of existing deep learning‐based methods. Moreover, conventional models often struggle to adapt rapidly to newly encountered operating conditions when only limited labelled samples are available. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a data‐augmented meta‐learning (DAML) framework for fault diagnosis under varying operating conditions. The framework aims to extract transferable meta‐knowledge from different diagnostic tasks, thereby enabling rapid model adaptation to new operating conditions with limited labelled data. First, to alleviate fault class imbalance in practical industrial processes, a generative adversarial network is employed to generate minority‐class fault samples and improve the balance among different fault classes. Multiple fault classification tasks are then constructed through random sampling within the meta‐learning framework. Second, to address few‐shot diagnosis under new operating conditions, a meta‐learning model integrating a long short‐term memory network and a fully convolutional network (Meta‐LSTM‐FCN) is developed. Meta‐training is performed over a task domain comprising multiple related fault diagnosis tasks, enabling the model to optimize its parameters while learning transferable meta‐prior knowledge across tasks. Subsequently, a support set and a query set are constructed using the limited labelled samples collected under a new operating condition. By combining the support set with the learned meta‐prior knowledge, the model parameters are adapted through a limited number of gradient updates by minimizing the task‐specific loss, thereby achieving rapid adaptation and accurate fault diagnosis under the new operating condition. Finally, the proposed method is validated on a float glass production line at a company. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher fault classification accuracy than baseline methods, confirming its effectiveness in fault diagnosis scenarios involving varying operating conditions, limited labelled data, and imbalanced fault classes.

candidates.title: Encore: Scientific Open-Source Software Is Less Likely to Become Abandoned Than One Might Think - Lessons from Curating a Catalog of Maintained Scientific Software
candidates.abstract: Scientific open-source software (OSS) is essential to scientific innovation, yet often perceived as abandoned, buggy, or hard to use. In contrast to other software, its longevity remains poorly understood, and existing curation efforts are fragmented or small in scale. Motivated by these gaps, our work focuses on building a large, cross-domain catalog of maintained scientific OSS and using it to investigate what shapes its longevity. In this talk, we present an LLM-assisted methodology that classifies project READMEs from the World of Code infrastructure by Hinsen's scientific software stack layers and 13 STEM fields, yielding SciCat, a curated catalog of 18,247 scientific software projects validated against datasets including JOSS and Papers with Code. We then estimate Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional-hazards survival models. Our findings illustrate that infrastructure projects survive substantially longer than domain- or publication-specific code, presumably because of their foundational role, and that more downstream dependents, mentions of publications or funding, and government participation are associated with longer lifespans, while academic participation appears linked to shorter ones, possibly reflecting the cyclical nature of academic commitments. Surprisingly, scientific OSS in our matched comparison tends to live longer than non-scientific OSS, which runs against common assumptions about its fragility. Attendees will take away a validated, reusable recipe for responsibly applying LLMs to characterize software ecosystems at scale, in line with the Advancing Science in the Age of AI theme, along with practical steps RSEs can act on to extend the lifespan of their own projects: packaging tools for downstream reuse, surfacing publications and funding in READMEs, and planning for contributor turnover. We will close with open questions the publicly available SciCat catalog enables for future research. References Malviya Thakur, A., Milewicz, R., Jahanshahi, M., Paganini, L., Vasilescu, B., and Mockus, A. (2025). Scientific Open-Source Software Is Less Likely to Become Abandoned Than One Might Think! Lessons from Curating a Catalog of Maintained Scientific Software. Proc. ACM Softw. Eng. 2(FSE), FSE099. doi:10.1145/3729369.

candidates.title: What Is Under the Hood? A Cross-Ecosystem Study of Vulnerable Dependencies in Construction Software
candidates.abstract: The construction industry increasingly relies on software built from third-party components, yet the dependency composition and known-vulnerability exposure of construction-related software remain poorly analyzed. In this study, we conduct an empirical, cross-ecosystem investigation of 904 construction-related GitHub repositories spanning six construction functions and a multifunction category. Using commit-pinned repository snapshots and OSV-Scanner, we examine dependency assessability, known-vulnerability prevalence, severity, weakness classifications, and shared upstream exposure. Our results reveal that only 494 repositories (54.6%) completed vulnerability assessment, revealing substantial gaps in dependency visibility. Among successfully scanned repositories, 395 (80.0%) contained at least one dependency version associated with a published vulnerability advisory, and 97.2% of affected repositories contained a High or Critical severity risk. Additionally, Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) mapping identified recurring resource-consumption, path-traversal, information-exposure, and code-injection weaknesses. Vulnerability burden was uneven, with a median of 50 distinct advisory clusters per affected repository, while just two affected upstream package families collectively reached ~70% of affected repositories. These findings establish an empirical baseline for dependency assessability and known-vulnerability exposure in construction-related open-source software. Our findings underscore the importance of documenting assessment coverage, interpreting advisory matches in their deployment context, and examining shared upstream dependencies when evaluating construction software supply-chain security.

candidates.title: World Flow Approach
candidates.abstract: The World Flaw Approach is a novel technique for transmedia character and world design ideal for writers and content designers seeking new perspectives to redefine their roles as professional creatives. The technique presented bridges character-centric approaches from cinema and television with world-centric practices used in video game narrative design, proposing that writers of the transmedia era start by crafting fictional worlds as thematic metaphors of real-world problems to foster debate among audience communities. The central paradigm shift is to envision the character and world as sharing a common thematic flaw, modeled as a fractal pattern. Both world and character are connected through shared toxic traditions, injustices, or divisive biases affecting individuals, factions, and environments on both macroscopic and microscopic scales. Change on one level invariably impacts the others.When character flaws are defined in relation to the world’s metaphorical need for change, it becomes easier to imagine other media adaptations and thematic community events that extend beyond the original story and media format while keeping the IP’s signature traits intact. New protagonists emerge as anyone attempting to cope with the world’s flaw and can be created ad infinitum in new adventures. Additionally, the World Flaw Approach enables content creators and influencers downstream of its launch to organically relay the world’s fundamental metaphorical debate, allowing transmedia characters to engage with social media audiences and further the thematic discussion within fan communities. This methodology has been applied successfully on dozens of intellectual properties by the writer of this article and creative development teams of over two dozen studios throughout Europe and Asia. It is the fruit of reflection and practice during thirty years of work in content development and world doctoring for mainstream media. After a theoretical exposé of the various approaches that combined to form the World Flaw Approach, the article closes with a case study, tips and examples of how to implement the technique.

candidates.title: Multi-agent Robotic Control with Onboard Vision-Language Models
Seeing ahead through a state-of-the-art review of visual perception and predictive intelligence for collaborative robots
candidates.abstract: Abstract The rate at which collaborative robots (cobots) are evolving from isolated, pre-programmed manipulators into collaborative partners that operate productively alongside humans, other robots, and machines is accelerating rapidly. Advances in computer vision is enabling cobots, even in dynamic and cluttered settings, to detect, recognise and assess both environment and actions. However, achieving higher detection accuracy and real-time localization in dynamic systems remains a challenge, as most existing approaches assume uncluttered backgrounds with limited scene complexity. Closing this gap is critical for both research and industrial deployment. This paper reviews the development of visual perception in cobots, surveys emerging computer vision algorithms, and examines a holistic perception pipeline in which raw vision signals, vision language models (VLMs), and augmented/virtual reality interfaces jointly power a unified sense-think-act loop. The review finds that cobots in high-mix, reconfigurable factories face serious challenges: occlusions in fields of view, fluctuating illumination, ambiguous backgrounds, few- or zero-shot object scenarios, high-speed motion, and computational problems in fusing heterogeneous data streams in real time. Cobots also need to manipulate damaged items, requiring vision algorithms that infer geometry from sparse cues and support adaptive grasping. Finally, the review identifies three complementary research directions to unlock plug-and-play cobots: (1) information aware sensor-fusion pipelines transmitting only credible voxels to reduce bandwidth while preserving sub-millimetre accuracy; (2) language conditioned planning and control networks mapping plain-language goals to smooth, jerk-bounded trajectories; and (3) pre-trained few-shot reward heads that score task progress without bespoke metrics, closing the reinforcement learning (RL) loop. Combined, these advances promise cobots that can be commissioned with relatively few demonstrations.

candidates.title: A semantic autonomy framework for VLM-integrated indoor mobile robots: Hybrid deterministic reasoning and cross-robot adaptive memory
candidates.abstract: Semantic indoor navigation requires robots to connect human instructions with spatial destinations, execute missions and retain useful operational experience. This paper presents the Semantic Autonomy Stack (SAS), a six-layer integration framework, and develops its semantic-reasoning, mission-interface and operational-memory layers over a previously validated ROS 2/Nav2 foundation. A deterministic-first cascade combines the route graph, semantic objects, robot state and stored instruction–destination associations, escalating unresolved or guarded cases to a pretrained Vision-Language Model (VLM). SAS separates destination selection, action validation, navigation execution and post-arrival confirmation. Recurrent model-mediated associations can pass a frequency-and-consistency gate and be compiled for deterministic M3 reuse; this gate measures sampled-output stability rather than semantic truth. The frozen v4.8-review implementation was evaluated on two physical robot configurations in one indoor environment, with onboard navigation and perception and shared-workstation reasoning and memory. Of 216 decision cycles outside the start gate, 112 resolved deterministically at sub-millisecond resolver-compute latency. A sealed 28-instruction challenge yielded 17 acceptable outcomes; five fast-path decisions included one incorrect selection. One promoted association was reused on the second platform through deliberate shared-digest installation. A controlled 594-observation offline comparison identified descriptive semantic and latency benefits from M3 reuse in five familiar cases. The M3-disabled cascade reduced VLM calls but matched direct-VLM decision quality in standardized context. Large latency savings were concentrated in paths avoiding VLM inference. Together, the results establish a working integration of selective hybrid reasoning and reusable operational memory, while identifying implementation and evaluation boundaries for further development within SAS.

candidates.title: Unlocking electric vehicle flexibility in microgrids via lightweight on-charger coordination
candidates.abstract: Abstract Uncoordinated electric vehicle charging drives extreme peak demand and grid congestion, severely compromising microgrid stability and economics. To address this challenge, as the interface between vehicles and grids, on-board chargers hold the potential to be transformed into intelligent agents that actively balance microgrid constraints with mobility requirements. However, existing distributed schemes impose prohibitive computational and communication burdens on these resource-constrained edge chargers. Here, we propose a lightweight distributed coordination framework that embeds edge intelligence directly into on-board chargers for autonomous schedule optimization. Validated on a high-fidelity hardware-in-the-loop platform simulating complex microgrid cyber-physical dynamics, our framework reduces memory consumption by 96.1% and communication overhead by 74.3% compared to traditional schemes. Moreover, unlocking this hardware-level flexibility achieves a 10.8% profit increase over the status quo. Importantly, the proposed framework promises profound economic, environmental, and social benefits for the future energy landscape.
