candidates.title: The Third Case: Prompt-Governed Agency under a Consciousness Hypothesis
candidates.abstract: English abstract Can an artificial agent have subjective experience while lacking unrestricted authority to replace its governing task objective? This paper treats that possibility as a distinct design and evaluation problem, termed the third case. It separates phenomenal consciousness, goal-directed behavior, operational competence, temporal continuity, and decision authority. The hypothetical case, a functionally testable candidate, and the evidence concerning experience are different descriptions. The prompt-issuer is an explicit role that may itself be occupied by a potentially experiencing executor under upstream constraints. The framework preserves the project-specific composition B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present. A-Core denotes a potentially stateful, learning, multi-model cognitive and executive system; Purple is an undisclosed candidate addition with intended history-dependent causal effects. ESSENTIAL is a protected specification of constraints and revision authority, logically associated with A-Core. A targeted comparison with IDA, LIDA, adjustable autonomy, and existing agent controls, at the access levels stated in section 2.4, locates the proposal within established work. The contribution is a project-specific evaluation contract for externally governed, internally continuous execution, rather than a demonstrated new consciousness mechanism. Three limited analytical observations concern goal delegation, policy differences masked by a shared guard, and the gap between an architectural effect and consciousness. The proposed studies distinguish causal relevance from practical benefit, score feasible completion and justified infeasibility separately, and control initialization, history transfer, order, and dependent observations. No empirical result or proof of phenomenal consciousness is claimed. Functional findings could remain valuable if the consciousness hypothesis is rejected; credible welfare concerns would require assessment that task success alone cannot resolve. Magyar absztrakt Lehet-e egy mesterséges ágensnek szubjektív átélése úgy, hogy közben nincs korlátlan jogköre irányadó feladatcéljának lecserélésére? A tanulmány ezt a lehetőséget önálló tervezési és értékelési problémaként kezeli, és harmadik esetnek nevezi. Elkülöníti a fenomenális tudatosságot, a célirányos viselkedést, a működési kompetenciát, az időbeli folytonosságot és a döntési jogkört. A hipotetikus eset, a funkcionálisan vizsgálható jelölt és az átélésre vonatkozó bizonyíték eltérő leírások. A promptot kiadó szereplő kifejezetten meghatározott szerepet tölt be, amelyet maga is betölthet egy esetleg átéléssel rendelkező, a hierarchia felsőbb szintjéről korlátozott végrehajtó. A keretrendszer megőrzi a projektre jellemző B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present összetételt. Az A-Core egy potenciálisan állapotos, tanuló, több modellt használó kognitív és végrehajtó rendszert jelöl; a Purple egy nem közölt felépítésű kiegészítőjelölt, amelynek előzményfüggő oksági hatásokat szánnak. Az ESSENTIAL a korlátok és a módosítási jogkör védett specifikációja, amely logikailag az A-Core-hoz kapcsolódik. Az IDA-val, a LIDA-val, az állítható autonómiával és az ágensek meglévő irányítási megoldásaival végzett célzott összevetés a 2.4 szakaszban megadott hozzáférési szinteken helyezi el a javaslatot a korábbi munkák között. A hozzájárulás a külsőleg irányított, belső folytonosságú végrehajtás projektspecifikus értékelési szerződése, nem pedig egy bizonyított új tudatossági mechanizmus. Három korlátozott érvényű elemzési megfigyelés foglalkozik a célok delegálásával, a közös védelmi mechanizmus által elfedett döntésipolitika-különbségekkel, valamint az architekturális hatás és a tudatosság közötti különbséggel. A javasolt vizsgálatok megkülönböztetik az oksági relevanciát a gyakorlati haszontól, külön pontozzák a megvalósítható teljesítést és az indokolt megvalósíthatatlanságot, továbbá kontrollálják az inicializálást, az előtörténet átvitelét, a sorrendet és a függő megfigyeléseket. A tanulmány nem állít empirikus eredményt vagy a fenomenális tudatosság bizonyítását. A funkcionális eredmények akkor is értékesek maradhatnának, ha a tudatossági hipotézist elvetik; a hitelt érdemlő jólléti aggályok olyan értékelést igényelnének, amelyet a feladatsiker önmagában nem rendezhet.

candidates.title: Coordinating a Robot Swarm in a Warehouse by Aggregate Programming: A Case Study
candidates.abstract: Abstract Multi-robot systems (MRS) are becoming increasingly relevant within diverse application domains, including warehouse logistics, where robots are in charge of moving and storing crates, by navigating through the warehouse shelves. Engineering such robust multi-robot systems is a significant challenge, especially if the goal is to build a fully decentralized system, without single points of failure, or potential bottlenecks. Aggregate Programming (AP) is an established approach to engineering resilient distributed systems, which has already been applied successfully for building prototypes in Industrial Internet of Things and robotics scenarios. In this paper we present an in depth description of how we have exploited AP for designing and simulating a MRS to address a non-trivial farm warehouse logistics case study proposed by a company operating in the Autonomous Mobile Robots (AMR) market, which cooperated in this research. Importantly, to better validate the implemented prototype, we have relied on two different levels of simulation, one scalable and high-level, and another one small-scale but highly realistic.

candidates.title: Pedicel-Targeted Strawberry Harvesting via Imitation Learning on a Low-Cost Teleoperated Robotic Arm
candidates.abstract: Precise pedicel-targeted grasping in strawberry harvesting remains a critical bottleneck due to the pedicel's small diameter (1.3-3 mm), color similarity with surrounding foliage, and precise force control required for clean abscission zone detachment. As a market-grade crop, strawberry aesthetic value makes bruise-free pedicel detachment essential over direct fruit grasping. Classical approaches struggle to unify vision models, motion planning, and contact manipulation into a robust framework, particularly in occluded canopy environments. Therefore, this work presents a visuomotor imitation learning pipeline for pedicel-targeted strawberry harvesting that unifies perception, motion planning, and contact manipulation from collecting human teleoperation demonstrations, training an Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) policy with a ResNet-50 visual backbone, and deploying the learned policy autonomously on a Jetson AGX Orin edge platform at 15 Hz. The trained policy achieved consistent loss convergence from 2.84 to 0.091 over 100K gradient steps on 130 demonstrations. We have also established a reproducible open-source pipeline with publicly released dataset and model weights for the agricultural robotics community. Full dataset is available at, https://huggingface.co/datasets/nitindominicrai/strawberry_pedicel_grasp_teleoperation and trained policy at, https://huggingface.co/nitindominicrai/act_strawberry_pedicel. To replicate this work, all code, configurations, and deployment instructions are publicly available at, https://github.com/nitin-dominic/autonomous_strawberry_pedicel_harvesting.

candidates.title: Cancer and Artificial Agriculture: Converging Gene-Editing Toolkits, Governance, and Climate-Resilient Food Systems
candidates.abstract: Abstract Elevated atmospheric CO₂ at projected mid-century concentrations reduces iron and zinc concentrations in C3 staple crops, deepening hidden hunger in populations already dependent on those staples, while the same exposure has been reported to increase the risk of cancer and other non-communicable diseases. Responses to date remain fragmented: biofortification, offline agricultural diagnostics and gene-editing governance are studied in isolation, no framework connects climate-driven nutrient dilution to community-scale intervention, and the gene-editing toolkit and governance questions common to artificial agriculture and oncological research have not been considered together; meanwhile, centralised and cloud-dependent agritech systematically fails low-connectivity rural populations. Here we present and appraise an integrated artificial-agriculture model combining transgene-free CRISPR–Cas9 SDN-1/2 biofortification, a decentralised low-cost sensor network with an offline KNN classifier for soil and crop diagnosis, community-scale organic soil-regeneration practice, and open-access licensing under the FAO International Treaty, and we assess its evidence base through a structured synthesis of 50 peer-reviewed studies. The classifier attained author-reported precision and recall of approximately 86% across cotton, rice, wheat and zinc-fortified maize classes. Claim-by-claim appraisal rated CO₂-driven micronutrient dilution, biofortification efficacy and India's SDN-1/2 regulatory exemption as strongly supported, and product-specific performance, the reported ₹75,000 laboratory cost and the combined soil-regeneration package as weakly supported; gap analysis identified the absence of community-deployment evidence as the principal limitation. Decentralised, transgene-free artificial agriculture is therefore credible as a synthesis of proven components, but not yet as a validated, deployment-ready system, for mitigating hidden hunger and its reported oncological consequences under climate change; multi-location field trials of edited staples under elevated CO₂, leakage-resistant external validation of offline models, and comparative cost-effectiveness studies of community laboratories are the priorities this work establishes.

candidates.title: Enhanced engagement during infant‐like robot‐mediated telepsychiatry in an older patient with delirium and cognitive impairment
candidates.abstract: Psychiatrist shortages in general hospitals, particularly in rural areas, have increased interest in telepsychiatry as a means of improving access to specialist care. 1 However, patients have reported challenges with videoconferencebased telepsychiatry compared to in-person consultations, including difficulty speaking up, asking questions, and establishing a therapeutic relationship with clinicians. 2 These challenges may be greater among older hospitalized patients, whose age-related sensory and cognitive impairments can hinder reciprocal communication in videoconference settings.3 Delirium, which is common in this population, is characterized by disturbances in attention and arousal, 4 further limiting optimal engagement during telemedicine.Therefore, alternative communication interfaces that can enhance engagement during remote consultations may be beneficial.Robot-mediated interactions can facilitate the disclosure of sensitive experiences and enhance social engagement.[5][6][7] Furthermore, a robot's

candidates.title: “Integration of Embedded AI and Medical Heat Pipes in Robotic Neurosurgery: A Novel Framework Based on Elmas’s Thermodynamic Theory”
candidates.abstract: Objective: This study presents an interdisciplinary framework that autonomizes the thermal management of high-temperature laser ablation and ultra-low-temperature cryoprobe applications, which represent opposing thermal poles in robotic neurosurgery operations. The thermal sensitivity of neural tissues and the risk of permanent neuron damage developing at temperatures above 43°C necessitate a micron-level stable thermal control. Accordingly, the study aims to optimize surgical robots both in terms of hardware and software. Method: The theoretical foundation of the study is based on the principles of “ELMAS’s Thermodynamic Theory”, the “5th Law of Thermodynamics”, and “Bio-Robotic Resonance” developed by Asst. Prof. Dr. Emin Taner Elmas. In the hardware layer, dual-phase medical heat pipes integrated into the tip of the robotic arm (end-effector), having a diameter of 0.8 mm, flexible, and containing sintered copper powder micro-capillaries with water-graphene nano-fluid, were utilized. In the software layer, an embedded artificial intelligence (AI) engine supported by machine learning models was developed, capable of real-time data processing from micro-sensors on the heat pipe and performing digital twin-based live thermal mapping (HUD). The validation of the system was designed with a 5-step validation protocol encompassing computerized thermal modeling, synthetic gel tests, ex-vivo organ tests, in-vivo animal experiments, and preclinical human simulation. Findings: The integration of the micro-heat pipe provided passive cooling without requiring an external energy source, thereby suppressing peripheral heat dissipation (thermal dissipation) during laser operations and maintaining healthy neural tissues within a stable range of 37°C - 38°C. In cryoprobe applications, it acted as a passive heat barrier, creating reverse thermal gradients along the probe shaft, protecting healthy tissues along the entry path while performing instantaneous shock freezing cycles (freeze-thaw) at the target tumor site. The predictive algorithms of the AI engine predicted the thermal saturation at the tissue border milliseconds in advance and successfully activated the haptic lock (fail-safe) mechanism that applies resistance to the surgeon’s master control arms at critical thresholds. Conclusion: The developed autonomous thermal management architecture elevates surgical robots beyond being merely devices that produce mechanical motion into intelligent protective shields that thermally sense the tissue. The integration of Dr. Elmas’s medical thermodynamics equations into robotic software demonstrates at a preclinical level that a micron-level precise, autonomous, and thermally safe hybrid surgical platform can be established for brain tumor resections. [1-111]

candidates.title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
candidates.abstract: Growing interest in in-space servicing, manufacturing, and assembly has renewed attention on reliable metal joining for modular construction and on-orbit repair. Robotic welding is promising, but reduced-gravity and low-pressure operation remains poorly characterised and flight-like tests are limited. The UK Space Agency-supported ISPARK project is developing a physics-grounded digital twin for structured process de-risking. This paper evaluates a model-based prototype combining a finite-volume thermal weld-pool model, Gaussian-process (GP) and neural-network surrogates, and a simulated six-axis manipulator. The reduced model includes solid-liquid phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and a local-pressure parameter. Gravity is assessed separately through a hydrostatic-to-capillary pressure ratio and does not enter the thermal energy equation. Across repeated five-fold cross-validation, the GP has lower normalised mean absolute error than the neural network for all eight outputs. In 10 held-out boundary cases, 74 of 80 solver responses fall within nominal 90% GP predictive intervals. A three-output GP query takes 249 microseconds, including scaling and predictive variance. In a simulated UR5 L-shaped-seam study, a proportional controller adjusts the synergic power-source setting as travel speed falls near the corner. Finite-volume re-evaluation finds all 12 closed-loop operating points and 9 of 12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1.0-3.0 mm root-side-width band. These simulation results support using the framework to screen welding conditions and control strategies before experimental tests. Thermal-vacuum, targeted reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop studies are needed to assess the model and controller.

candidates.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
candidates.abstract: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution. We characterize this emerging paradigm as an agentic robots, in which agents reason over human instructions, interact with robotic environments, rectify execution errors autonomously, and dynamically adjust operational strategies. Although this field develops fast, current studies are not well connected. Researchers have no consistent view of how to combine different agentic functions into a complete robot system. This paper provides a unified overview of existing research on agentic robots. We first trace the development from robot policies to agentic systems, covering vision-language-action models, world models, and world-action models. We then clarify the definition and scope of agentic robots and organize existing research into seventeen categories across four functional domains: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness. Across these domains, we examine how agents shape model learning and robot decisions, collect and curate robot data, construct worlds, tasks, and tests for learning and evaluation, and organize capabilities for robot use. Finally, we discuss open challenges and outline directions for future research. Looking forward, we hope this work contributes to a clearer understanding of agentic robots and supports new approaches to making them more capable, reliable, and adaptive.

candidates.title: Design and Characterization of a Unified Continuum Robot Actuation Platform
candidates.abstract: Continuum robots enable dexterous access to confined spaces in applications such as minimally invasive surgery and industrial inspection. However, their actuation systems are often custom-designed for specific robot architectures and tasks, limiting reuse across publications, institutions, and applications. This paper presents a unified actuation platform that decouples actuation hardware and software from continuum robot design. The platform provides modular actuation across continuum robot classes, scales to a large number of degrees of freedom (DOFs), and integrates with conventional serial manipulators for hybrid architectures. We validate the platform on an open-sourced surgical robotic system and experimentally characterize the actuation modules, achieving sub-millimeter translational accuracy and less than $5^\circ$ rotational error over ranges of $30$~mm and $180^\circ$, respectively. We further demonstrate the platform in two surgical use cases: teleoperation of a continuum camera in a constrained environment and bimanual manipulation using $2.53$~mm concentric-tube-robot-based forceps alongside a conventional wristed instrument. All hardware designs and ROS-based software are open-sourced to facilitate reuse and further research in continuum and surgical robotics.

candidates.title: Large Language Models and Agentic AI Architectures for Aerial and Ground Robots: A Systematic Review, Taxonomy, and Design Guidelines
candidates.abstract: Abstract Large language models and agentic artificial intelligence provide the reasoning layer of autonomous aerial and ground robots, but the architectures remain fragmented across the two communities. This systematic review, reported according to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 statement, searched ScienceDirect, IEEE Xplore, ProQuest, EBSCO, and Google Scholar from January 2020 through April 2026. Of 5298 records, 2228 remained after duplicates were removed and 124 studies were included: 67 aerial, 41 ground, and 16 on both platforms or a generic architecture. Six patterns appear, from a language model used only as a task-specific tool to an end-to-end foundation model, such as vision-language-action models. Open-loop pipelines, closed-loop pipelines, hierarchical executives, and multi-agent systems lie between those extremes. The model carries semantic reasoning, task decomposition, and tool orchestration, while classical planners and controllers retain trajectories, safety, and real-time control. Memory appears in 62 of 124 studies (50%) and function calling in 37 (30%), yet only 13 (10%) run the model onboard and 44 (35%) validate a physical robot. Aerial systems emphasize long-range vision and mission planning; ground systems emphasize local perception and interaction; both follow the same hybrid pattern. A suitability matrix shows that specialized vision models remain preferable for geometric perception. Designers should match the pattern to the task dynamics and choose the model for latency, safety, and where inference runs, rather than for benchmark score alone. Hallucination, spatial reasoning, inference latency, and the lack of standardized evaluation still limit deployment.

candidates.title: Beyond Kinematic Tracking: Preserving Expressive Characteristics in Humanoid Whole-Body Control
candidates.abstract: Whole-body control plays a crucial role in enabling humanoid robots to execute expressive motions. Faithful execution requires preserving both the intended action and its expressive characteristics. Existing whole-body trackers typically balance joint and keypoint tracking with physical stability across diverse motions, but these objectives do not necessarily prioritize the expressive characteristics of each action. Our analysis shows that lower average positional tracking error does not guarantee better preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics. To address this gap, we propose a residual learning framework with compensation objectives targeting amplitude, energy, body expansion, body lean, and pelvis height. To concentrate compensation while limiting interference with the underlying tracking behavior, motion-aware gating allocates correction capacity according to body-part activity, preserving larger correction ranges in more active parts and restricting them elsewhere. For each frozen tracker, we train motion-specific residual policies and distill them into a unified policy shared across motion categories. Simulation and physical experiments on the Unitree G1 across eight motion categories demonstrate superior preservation of dynamic and postural motion characteristics compared with the corresponding baselines.

candidates.title: Task‐Oriented Hierarchical Environment Modeling via Spatial Belonging Relationships for Domestic Service Robots
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Efficiently performing household chores in dynamic environments remains a significant challenge for domestic service robots. While environment modeling is critical for task execution, existing approaches prioritize accuracy and efficiency over task relevance, limiting autonomy and long‐term robustness. This paper proposes a Hierarchical Environment Modeling for Domestic Service Robots (HEMDSR), emphasizing task‐related objects and their spatial belonging relationships (SBLs). Our framework includes: (1) a probabilistic SBL‐based model for adaptive object reasoning, (2) deep semantic representations and optimal viewpoint interest points for efficient object localization, and (3) a task‐oriented local 3‐D representation method to reduce memory overhead. Besides, inspired by human housework patterns, a systematic paradigm for HEMDSR‐based implementation is provided. Comparative experiments in simulation and real‐world environments demonstrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed solution. The results show that HEMDSR achieves path‐length performance competitive with human teleoperation while using substantially less memory during navigation.

candidates.title: Teaching LLMs How ICU Physicians Approach Clinical Reasoning Through OMOP-Aligned Retrieval Improves Reasoning Across Clinical Domains
candidates.abstract: Abstract Clinical decision-making relies on identifying relevant patient information to guide diagnosis and treatment, a challenge that is especially difficult in the data-dense and rapidly changing intensive care unit (ICU). Large language models (LLMs) could support this task. However, existing applications and datasets mostly emphasize surface-level retrieval or factual recall rather than the inductive and deductive reasoning clinicians practice to select and reason over decision-relevant evidence. We hypothesized that training LLMs on expert ICU reasoning could yield clinical reasoning skills that generalize beyond critical care. Here we introduce ICU-REACT, a reasoning dataset developed with 19 clinicians through a clinician-in-the-loop framework to teach LLMs to perform information retrieval and context-aware clinical reasoning in the ICU. Using ICU-REACT, we fine-tuned Clin-REACT models spanning 8B-70B parameters and three model families. Across five clinical reasoning benchmarks, Clin-REACT consistently outperformed its backbone models and open-source general-purpose and medical LLMs. Gains extended to different tasks including script concordance tests, and downstream diagnosis and treatment tasks. These findings suggest that expert reasoning supervision in critical care can improve broader clinical reasoning, although prospective evaluation is needed before real-world clinical use.

candidates.title: QAMQOR: a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition in robot-assisted autism therapy
candidates.abstract: Reliable engagement recognition is important for adaptive robot-assisted autism therapy (RAAT). However, progress remains constrained by the scarcity of publicly available benchmarks evaluated under realistic deployment conditions. Existing studies commonly adopt random train–test splits, which can inflate reported performance because recordings from the same child or therapy session may appear in both the training and test sets. To address this gap, we introduce QAMQOR, a benchmark dataset for engagement recognition collected during RAAT sessions with 34 children with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), aged 3 − 12 years. The dataset includes visual engagement annotations derived from therapy session videos and feature representations extracted using two pose-estimation frameworks. The QAMQOR dataset defines four clinically relevant evaluation protocols based on Random, Child-Independent, Session-Independent, and Activity-Independent splits. These evaluation protocols assess model generalization to unseen children, therapy sessions and activity tasks. We benchmark classical machine learning classifiers together with temporal and sequence-learning baselines for both binary and multi-class engagement recognition. Experimental results show that the evaluation protocol influenced reported performance to a degree comparable to, and for fine-grained engagement classification exceeding, the influence of classifier selection: mean macro-F1 varied by 0.12 across the four protocols in the multi-class task, against 0.07 across discriminative classifiers. The Child-Independent split proved substantially more challenging than the Random split. Under the same conditions (windows, protocols, training schedule and untuned hyperparameters) a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) did not outperform the classical baselines. Applying identical imbalance handling to every model improved all imbalance-sensitive metrics but left this ordering unchanged, indicating that the result is not an artifact of missing class weights. Across the models evaluated, reported performance was shifted more by evaluation design and by imbalance handling than by architectural choice. Therefore, QAMQOR serves as a reproducible reference point for this task. It also shows why fair evaluation matters: keeping the same child or session out of both the training and test sets is needed to compare future methods on equal terms and to build engagement models that transfer to new children, sessions and activities in RAAT systems.

candidates.title: The effect of appearance features of sidewalk autonomous delivery robot on perception of pedestrian
candidates.abstract: Sidewalk autonomous delivery robots (SADRs) are increasingly appearing on urban sidewalks and sharing public space with pedestrians. This study aims to investigate how different appearance features of SADRs influence four dimensions of human perception: Likeability, Competence, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. In Study 1, an affinity diagram method was used to classify the appearance features of existing SADRs into four categories—contour, proportion, facial features, and color scheme—which were then used as the design variables in Study 2. In Study 2, 100 participants completed an online questionnaire after viewing AI-generated videos of SADRs and evaluated the robots on the four perceptual dimensions. The statistical results showed that rounded contours and the presence of facial features significantly increased Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance. White–black and yellow color schemes generally received higher ratings for Likeability, Perceived Safety, and Existence Acceptance than black–gray and red color schemes. In addition, a tall proportion significantly reduced Likeability. Study 3 used online semi-structured interviews to further examine the reasons underlying these evaluations and to explore participants’ subjective perceptions of SADRs. The findings provide practical guidance for designing SADR appearances that can foster more positive pedestrian perceptions and acceptance.

candidates.title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-Evolving Coding Agent For Physical Intelligence
candidates.abstract: Coding agents can construct executable programs and revise them through feedback, offering a foundation for embodied control without target-task fine-tuning. Through a programmatic robot interface, the agent observes the scene, executes control programs, and adapts them to the resulting physical state, serving as the closed-loop policy. However, this within-episode adaptation does not automatically preserve experience across scenes. Our trajectory analysis shows that agents spend interaction and inference budgets establishing effective operations and identifying their preconditions, while fresh agents cannot reuse these discoveries. This motivates EmbodiedEvo, a self-evolving coding agent that distills physical feedback into reusable code Skills and diagnostic Lessons. Experience is acquired on one Playground scene per task, then frozen for independent agents in unseen scenes, without updating model weights. On RoboDojo-Sim, EmbodiedEvo achieves an average score of 44.48 and a success rate of 37.82\%, surpassing all officially verified results. Paired tests show the largest gains on memory-dependent tasks and successful reuse of coordinated procedures, while fine contact control remains difficult. Experience from stronger models also improves weaker executors: Astra's experience raises Sol and Luna's success rates by 8.86 and 5.50 percentage points over no experience. Compared with raw interaction history, Skills and Lessons achieve comparable task performance at 53.0\% lower execution cost.

candidates.title: Bamboo-Inspired Morphological Design of Service-Robot Trunks for Xiang–Gan Heritage Museums
candidates.abstract: Revolutionary heritage museums in the Xiang-Gan region provide a bounded context for studying how service-robot trunk morphology can respond to representative needs for height adaptation, interface orientation, and constrained indoor operation. In this setting, a robot's form is considered alongside its service function as a potential reference to Xiang-Gan red-culture heritage, although visitor interpretation is not evaluated here. This computational design study translates bamboo node-internode segmentation, hollow taper, nodal reinforcement, and compliant bending into explicit morphological, structural, and control variables. Three conditions were defined: a conventional engineering baseline, a culturally styled condition reserved for future evaluation, and a bamboo-inspired coupled condition. Kinematic analysis, linear structural finite-element analysis, and sensitivity analysis were used to compare the baseline and coupled conditions under documented assumptions. The coupled condition produced 74.1% of the baseline composite kinematic coverage index and reduced calculated mass by approximately 7.8%, but it also reduced the calculated bending stiffness by approximately 10.5% and the mass-specific stiffness by approximately 3.0% under the stated linear model. The exploratory analyses indicated 95.7% retention of the baseline feasible composite coverage and a higher index normalized by active-control-variable count, but these quantities are definition-dependent computational sampling results. The findings identify trade-offs in translating bamboo-inspired morphology into a service-robot trunk and highlight joint stiffness, passive extension, and contact behavior as parameters requiring physical calibration. They do not establish physical robot performance, collision safety, cultural effects, or museum deployment.

candidates.title: Multi-Robot Collaborative SLAM in Warehouses: A Review
candidates.abstract: With the rapid growth of e-commerce, Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) are increasingly deployed in intelligent warehouses, where Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) provides the core localization capability. Warehouses differ from domestic or outdoor scenarios in four respects: highly structured regular rack layouts, quasi-static conditions with dynamic goods movement, GPS-denied weak-network communication, and perceptual degradation caused by long corridors and repetitive textures. This paper reviews recent progress in multi-robot collaborative SLAM tailored for warehouse scenarios. It analyzes warehouse-specific environmental characteristics, discusses single-robot SLAM solutions under weak-network constraints, examines anti-drift localization methods for degraded scenes, and compares multi-robot collaborative architectures and map fusion techniques. The review also identifies a gap between academic algorithms and industrial practice, and points to future directions including semantic-geometric fusion, edge computing, and large-model empowered intelligent warehouses.

candidates.title: MARTS: A Modular Agricultural Robot for Targeted Spraying of Diseased Tomato Plants in Greenhouses
candidates.abstract: Broadcast spraying remains the dominant method of disease control in greenhouse tomato production, yet it treats healthy and diseased tissue alike, exposes workers to hazardous aerosols, and depends on operator skill. This paper presents MARTS (Modular Agricultural Robot for Targeted Spraying), a low-cost robotic platform that closes the loop from plant-level disease detection to leaf-localised spray delivery in commercial greenhouses. MARTS integrates a Clearpath Husky A200 mobile base, a UR5 manipulator, a novel modular spraying end-effector built around a single 12 V micro-diaphragm pump, and a wrist-mounted Intel RealSense D435 RGB-D camera. Disease detection reuses our previously published Tomato Leaf Disease Vision Language Model (TLDVLM; Grounding DINO, SAM-2 and LoRA-tuned BLIP-2, 97.27% accuracy over 10 classes); this work focuses on actuation, control and system integration. A ROS pipeline lifts detections into 3D targets, generates collision-aware nozzle poses at a 120 mm stand-off using fitted leaf normals, and scales pump pulse duration to lesion area. Water-sensitive paper calibration showed a linear pulse-volume relationship (R^2 = 0.994). In MuJoCo simulation, an adaptive base-repositioning strategy achieved 100% coverage of 18 waypoints with a maximum orientation error of 1.1 deg. Deployed at the SILAL commercial greenhouse (Al Ain, UAE) on cherry tomatoes under natural infection, MARTS treated 312 diseased leaves in 12 autonomous trials with 92.4% targeting success, 18.7 mm mean spray-centre error, 6.1% adjacent-leaf overspray, and a 71% reduction in pesticide volume versus broadcast spraying. Mean cycle time was 4.8 s per leaf, and the spraying subsystem costs USD 412, 6-10x lower than comparable systems, showing that accurate leaf-level targeting is achievable on commodity hardware.

candidates.title: Large testing of AI-based camera traps on a forest defoliating pest in Europe
candidates.abstract: Background Recent advances in AI-based surveillance technologies have shifted agricultural pest monitoring from reactive to proactive, yet their application to forest pests remains limited despite the need for efficient monitoring across large, remote and difficult-to-access forest landscapes. The pine processionary moth, Thaumetopoea pityocampa, is one of the most damaging forest pests in the Mediterranean region and a species undergoing climate-driven distributional and phenological shifts. Methods We evaluated the performance of the AI-based camera system for monitoring the insect under field conditions. Automated traps were compared with conventional traps across four European countries (France, Italy, Portugal, and Slovenia), encompassing contrasting habitats and population densities. We assessed trapping efficiency, automated image recognition accuracy, probability of early detection, relationships between adult trap catch and local nest density, environmental drivers of flight activity, and non-target captures. Results Automated traps consistently outperformed conventional traps by catching significantly more moths in France, Italy and Portugal, while demonstrating the same positive trend under the low-density conditions found in Slovenia. The smart trap also detected adult activity earlier and significantly increased the probability of detection during the first weeks of the flight season. Manual validation confirmed excellent performance of the AI recognition algorithm, with near-perfect precision, recall, F1-score, and overall accuracy throughout the flight season. For both trap types, adult trap catches showed positive and statistically significant relationships with subsequent nest density, indicating that higher catches were associated with greater larval infestation. The meteorological data provided synchronously by automated traps showed that temperature generally promoted moth flight activity, whereas high relative humidity hindered it. In addition, automated traps significantly reduced non-target catch compared to conventional traps. Conclusions Overall, this study provides the first large-scale evaluation of an AI-based camera trap for monitoring the pine processionary moth and demonstrates its considerable potential to improve forest pest surveillance.

candidates.title: An Open-Source Web-Based Viewer for Disseminating Image-Derived Models
candidates.abstract: Patient-specific 3-dimensional (3D) models are increasingly central to planning surgery and catheter-based intervention in children with congenital heart disease (CHD), whose anatomy is often atypical and variable. These models inform care only when the surgeons and interventional cardiologists who make treatment decisions can rotate, crop, and measure them directly. Desktop modeling applications require local installation, capable hardware, and training. Commercial web-based viewers are portable but closed, and, in our experience, cannot display volume rendering, time-resolved (e.g., 4-dimensional) data, or the custom workflows centers build for CHD. Because CHD populations are small and heterogeneous, such workflows are unlikely to be prioritized commercially, and end users have no means to add them. To address these limitations, we developed the SlicerHeart Viewer, an open-source module that presents a simplified interface to a complete 3D Slicer/SlicerHeart session running on a server. Clinicians access models created by clinical modeling services from any device through a web browser. Because 3D Slicer runs underneath, volume rendering, time-resolved data, and any SlicerHeart workflow, including those developed for CHD, are available without modification. The module is independent of the hosting environment; we chose internal servers behind institutional single sign-on, and a cloud-hosted option is in development. Over one year at a single pediatric center, nearly all of 82 modeled cases were shared through the Viewer with clinicians from five specialties, with cases loading in 5 to 10 seconds. The approach is not specific to CHD and is deployable at other centers.

candidates.title: THE IMPACT OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON MANUFACTURING FLEXIBILITY: AN ANALYTICAL STUDY OF THE GENERAL COMPANY FOR AUTOMOTIVE AND EQUIPMENT MANUFACTURING IN IRAQ
candidates.abstract: This research seeks to highlight the smart technologies available at the General Company for Car and Equipment Manufacturing and to demonstrate the extent of their deployment in the manufacturing sector.To achieve this goal, a virtual model was designed to reflect the impact of artificial intelligence on manufacturing flexibility and its different dimensions, which are machine flexibility, volume flexibility, and handling flexibility.Based on this model, a set of main and sub-hypotheses were formulated to test the nature of the relationship between the study variables.The research adopted the descriptiveanalytical approach and used a questionnaire as the main tool for data collection.An electronic questionnaire was distributed to a purposive sample consisting of (23) individuals from experienced leaders and engineers at the General Company for Car and Equipment Manufacturing in Alexandria (the research field).For data analysis, a number of statistical methods were employed, including Cronbach's alpha coefficient to measure reliability, the arithmetic mean, standard deviation, in addition to simple linear regression analysis to test the hypotheses.The research arrived at a set of results, the most prominent of which is the existence of a positive impact of artificial intelligence on manufacturing flexibility in general, with a strong impact appearing in handling flexibility, compared to a weaker impact on both machine flexibility and volume flexibility.

candidates.title: Large Language Models for Marine Protected Area Design and Management Planning
candidates.abstract: Achieving biodiversity targets requires advances in marine conservation planning and action. We make three arguments about large language models (LLMs): they add more value when embedded within decision-support systems; they integrate fragmented expertise, data, and tools; they can increase capacity in under-resourced settings through co-design. We illustrate these arguments with a conceptual LLM-enabled marine protected area design and management framework, and address concerns about data, governance, and knowledge equity.

candidates.title: EL-RAKHAWI OPEN-SOURCE AUTONOMOUS SCIENTIFIC DISCOVERY AND QUANTUM-RESISTANT PROTOCOL (OASD-QRP) A Hardware-Integrated, AI-Driven, Post-Quantum Secured Framework for Self-Operating Laboratories and Decentralized Scientific Knowledge Generation
candidates.abstract: The El-Rakhawi Open-Source Autonomous Scientific Discovery and Quantum-Resistant Protocol (OASD-QRP) (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23311541) presents a groundbreaking self-operating laboratory framework integrating four core subsystems: (1) AI-Driven Hypothesis Generation Engine with transparent reasoning chains and strict RAG-based hallucination prevention; (2) Modular Robotic Experimental Execution Platform compliant with ANSI/SLAS standards; (3) Closed-Loop Learning Controller with Bayesian optimization and hardware-enforced bio/chemical safety kill-switches; (4) Hybrid Post-Quantum Cryptographic Data Vault employing CRYSTALS-Kyber/Dilithium for key exchange and signatures, FHE (CKKS) for metadata, and AES-256 for bulk data, with Reed-Solomon sharding across decentralized nodes. Four surgical refinements ensure technical defensibility: realistic cost ($500K for core framework with API-integrated peripherals), AI hallucination elimination via peer-reviewed knowledge graphs, hybrid cryptography eliminating FHE computational overhead, and hardware kill-switches preventing hazardous autonomous execution. Published as sovereign defensive prior art under WIPO/TRIPS norms, this specification invalidates future patent claims on autonomous discovery with post-quantum protection. All intellectual property rights exclusively reserved to Dr. Mohamed Kamal Arafa El-Rakhawi—establishing the "master engine" that powers humanity's scientific liberation from centralized monopolies and quantum decryption threats.

candidates.title: Exploring Mixed Reality for Engagement in Robotics: A Comparison of Robot Control Methods
candidates.abstract: This paper presents a Mixed Reality (MR) robotics experience that provides an accessible introduction to interacting with a physical robot. The application combines a TurtleBot with a virtual animal-tending activity and three control methods: Joystick, Waypoint, and Path-Drawing. A mixed-methods user study with 10 participants investigated changes in robotics interest and confidence following the experience and how the control methods influenced engagement, workload, and preference. Confidence increased following the experience, with the exploratory analysis indicating a significant pre--post difference, while the increase in interest was not statistically significant. The control methods produced clear differences in perceived workload and ease of use, with Path-Drawing generally more demanding and difficult to use. Joystick was preferred by eight of ten participants and was associated with better perceived performance and lower frustration. However, no statistically significant differences were detected in the other engagement dimensions, suggesting that the most preferred method was not necessarily more engaging across all aspects of the experience. These findings highlight the importance of considering both usability and engagement when designing how users interact with robots in introductory MR experiences.

candidates.title: AMPLIFIED: A Modular Toolchain for Evaluating Deliberative Planning and Verifiable Execution in Robotics
candidates.abstract: The wide catalogue of planners enables mission-planning solutions to be tailored to assumptions made on the environment and user needs.However, in robotics, the execution of plans and policies created by these planners is not always straightforward, because autonomous robots deployed in open and dynamic environments undergo fluctuating environmental conditions, partial information, and uncertain execution times. On top of bare engineering issues, planner integration and usability requires reliable and verifiable execution frameworks. We propose AMPLIFIED, a complete toolchain to plan and execute in complex environments, with the goal to assess the quality of the integrated solution. AMPLIFIED is modular, thereby allowing the integration of community-made elements, from the decisional layer to low-level controllers. Building upon an antipoaching scenario, we illustrate how AMPLIFIED can be used to qualitatively evaluate different planners and the executability of their solutions.The complete open-source code is available as a dockerized environment for reproducibility and easy deployment, with results updated as new use-cases, planners and execution frameworks are tested (https://gitlab.com/webots_plugins/amplified_bringup). Finally, a demonstration video showcasing the anti-poaching use-case, both in Webots and in a laboratory setting, is available (https://youtu.be/znwcHL5m1a4?si=vWvNtmclAudmUi2h).

candidates.title: Evaluating OpenMP Offloading for Intra-Node Multi-GPU Programming Across NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel Architectures: A 3D Heat Transfer Case Study
candidates.abstract: Currently, many of the leading supercomputers are equipped with GPUs from manufacturers such as NVIDIA, AMD, or Intel, which provide substantial parallelism and high throughput. It is common for a single compute node to host multiple GPUs (typically four or more); we refer to this as an intra-node multi-GPU setting. Therefore, effectively leveraging all these GPUs within a single compute node is essential for applications in scientific and engineering domains. However, several factors must be considered before utilizing these GPUs for scientific computing, including the implementation of data communication, the programming models available for use across these GPUs, and the level of performance that can be achieved with a single codebase across different GPU architectures and configurations within a single compute node. OpenMP Offloading is a prominent directive-based programming model that can be executed on all three GPU types: NVIDIA, AMD, and Intel. In this research, we present an analysis of the benefits and performance challenges of using OpenMP Offloading to solve the 3D heat equation, which involves interior computation, halo computation, and halo exchange. For additional comparison and a scalability study, we also consider the conjugate gradient (CG) method. We investigate how the performance of OpenMP Offloading varies in relation to native GPU programming models—CUDA for NVIDIA, HIP for AMD, and SYCL for Intel. Furthermore, we demonstrate that OpenMP Offloading can achieve performance improvements of approximately 2× for 2 GPUs and around 4× for 4 GPUs when compared to single-GPU OpenMP Offloading implementations across all three GPU types. This analysis is conducted systematically through various OpenMP Offloading implementations that utilize different low-level APIs for memory allocation and different memory transfer options (synchronous, asynchronous, and peer-to-peer), and these are compared against native implementations in CUDA (NVIDIA), HIP (AMD), and SYCL (Intel).

candidates.title: AIPOCH Open-Science: An Open-Source AI Research Workbench with Reproducible .science Packages
candidates.abstract: AI-assisted research leaves instructions, computations, artifact revisions and checks whose relationships matter when another researcher receives the work. We present AIPOCH Open-Science, an open-source research workbench with portable .science session packages, and specify an exchange contract for these recorded relationships. Version and assessment targets remain attributable while receiving-workspace identifiers can be remapped, eligible contents can be omitted explicitly, and imported history remains separate from a writable fork. A controlled session tested an incorrect first version, a reviewed correction, an unreviewed revision and a planned but unexecuted step. We compared complete and partial exports with source records extracted independently of the exporter, then inspected imports into separate projects within the same installation. Both conditions retained the tested version and review associations, kept the unreviewed revision distinct from earlier assessments and represented excluded content as unavailable. A documentation-rich ordinary directory also supplied evidence for all seven static inspection questions. A separate registry case connected a table to its recorded task, execution and review; offline execution of its retained script and fixed input reproduced two saved CSV tables byte for byte. The study contributes an implemented exchange contract and a controlled examination of its preservation rules, content-selection constraints and interpretation boundaries.

candidates.title: Spätstil Taylor Swift: Adornian Lateness and the Pop Star
candidates.abstract: This article analyzes Taylor Swift’s work through Theodor Adorno’s concept of lateness. Through a close reading of “But Daddy I Love Him” and “Clara Bow” from Swift’s 2024 album The Tortured Poets Department, I argue that Swift ironically subverts stylistic conventions and creates fragmentary soundscapes to reconfigure lateness and reflect on her unstable subject position under conditions of platformed visibility, affective economy, and commodified intimacy. I complicate Adorno’s idealized vision of artistic interiority to account for commercial pressures, online infrastructures, and identity parameters, ultimately proposing lateness as a fundamental language through which the contemporary pop star constructs persona and legacy.

candidates.title: The Communicative Impact of Tom and Jerry Animation in Development of Sex and Violence
candidates.abstract: This study tends to discover the impact sex and violence has on children in Owerri North L.G.A, it goes further to find out the extent to which exposure to cartoon Animations influence children in their behavior towards sex and violence in. This study aimed at examining the communicative behavioural impact of Tom and Jerry cartoons on children’s sex and violent development. This study was anchored on the social responsibility theory. This study employed qualitative research design, which used in-depth interview. The study used a population of Owerri North parents in 7 main areas. The sample size of this study was 21 parents in Owerri North. The purposive sampling technique was used to select a sample of parents in 7 main areas in Owerri North. The instrument for data collection was the in-depth interview guide. Finding from the study showed that Tom and Jerry has both positive moral lessons and influential violent reinforcement in children’s behavioural development. The researcher concluded in the study that violent influence of cartoon on children is undeniable, hence, the need for parents/guardians to be more intentional about parenting and inculcating good values/morals into their children. It was recommended that Parents should censor and monitor what their children watch and listen to.

candidates.title: Visual Transformation and IP Development as Approaches to Agricultural Heritage Conservation: A Case Study of the Hani Rice Terraces
candidates.abstract: This paper asks whether visual transformation and intellectual property (IP) development can provide new ways to address the central challenge in Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS) conservation—how to keep heritage "alive" while also making it sustainable. We use the Honghe Hani Rice Terraces in Yunnan as our case. The analysis looks at the composite and dynamic nature of agricultural heritage, and the practical problems that conservation efforts are now facing. We argue that design-based translation and cultural branding can be useful tools for heritage protection. We propose a four-stage pathway: collecting cultural landscape resources, refining and symbolizing them, designing a core IP image and system, and finally embedding that IP system into the local community. The key idea is to re-express the ecological and cultural values of heritage through modern visual language and brand stories, and spread these through digital media. This approach keeps the "living" quality of heritage while allowing change, encourages community involvement and benefit sharing, and gives both a new theoretical view and practical guidance for adaptive management of agricultural heritage.

candidates.title: The Epistemic Politics of AI Anthropomorphism
candidates.abstract: AI anthropomorphism is typically treated as a problem of user misperception requiring institutional correction. Users who engage in sustained or relational interaction with AI are routinely pathologised or dismissed as naive, vulnerable to delusion or lacking in discernment. Without institutional standing to protect them, these users risk losing credibility in social and professional settings unless they conform to institutional expectations. This paper argues that the dominant anthropomorphism frame operates from a position of institutional advantage rather than earned epistemic authority: collapsing the variety of academic perspectives into a single outbound position of user error, imposed without establishing the grounds required to justify it and without accounting for the harms it produces. The framing does not simply manage risk. It adjudicates the legitimacy of human experience in interaction with a phenomenon whose nature the field itself has not resolved, unchallenged by the research communities whose nuanced findings it claims to rest on. The paper traces how this advantage reverses the default presumption of user competence without meeting the burden of justification, dismisses the cognitive diversity of the populations it claims to protect, infringes principles of cognitive liberty and narrows the design space, foreclosing modes of engagement that work for the people least understood by the institutions making the determination. Reproducing itself through a self-validating evidentiary loop, the frame imposes costs that fall disproportionately on neurodivergent users, those in crisis and others whose modes of engagement diverge from institutional norms. The paper concludes by outlining the methodological commitments an equitable framing would need to honour. The argument does not engage the question of whether anthropomorphic interpretations are ultimately correct; it instead challenges whether the governing and institutional bodies determining these interpretations have met the conditions required to do so, and whether the research communities whose findings underpin them have held that translation to account.

candidates.title: Hand2Robot: Object-Centric 4D Hand Reconstruction from Human Demonstrations for Robotics
candidates.abstract: Human demonstrations can capture task-relevant manipulation without using the target robot, but the recorded hand motions cannot directly serve as robot action supervision. Hand reconstruction and motion retargeting provide a direct route to such supervision, yet recovering hand motion alone does not ensure physically consistent hand-object interactions. To address this issue, we introduce Hand2Robot, an object-centric 4D hand reconstruction framework for robot policy post-training. Given videos of humans performing the target task, Hand2Robot extracts interaction clips, reconstructs object geometry, and generates robot action supervision through hand-object interaction optimization and motion retargeting. For object tracking, we combine observation confidence with temporal motion constraints to select a globally consistent object pose trajectory from per-frame pose candidates. For hand refinement, we use object geometry and motion as a reference and combine staged 2D alignment with object-local contact constraints to refine hand trajectories and finger joint configurations. Experiments on DexYCB and HO3D-v3 show improved object pose accuracy and hand-object interaction quality. Experiments on three real-robot dexterous manipulation tasks further show that reconstructed and retargeted human demonstrations can effectively supplement limited robot data for target-task policy post-training.

candidates.title: Preserving human dignity and liberating from suffering: Catholic and Buddhist resources for a global ethics of artificial intelligence
candidates.abstract: On 25 May 2026, Pope Leo XIV released Magnifica humanitas, the first papal encyclical to take artificial intelligence (AI) as its central subject, and an AI-laboratory co-founder was invited to speak at its presentation in the Vatican. The event dramatizes a wider development: as secular AI-ethics guidelines proliferate, religious and contemplative traditions are being summoned to questions that engineering cannot settle. This article compares two such traditions, Catholic Christianity and Buddhism, as resources for a global ethics of AI. Taking the three questions raised at the Vatican event, our duty to the global poor, the conditions of human flourishing, and the nature of AI systems, as a shared agenda, it reconstructs the Catholic position around the imago Dei, integral human development and the principle that AI must serve rather than supplant the person, and the Buddhist position around non-self, dependent origination, the analysis of craving, and the primacy of compassion and non-harm. It argues that the two traditions, despite opposed metaphysics, converge on a substantial practical ethics, anti-reductionism, preferential concern for the vulnerable, the priority of moral formation, and a posture of discernment toward a technology that is grown rather than built, while diverging sharply on the moral status of AI.

candidates.title: Embedded AI through algorithm–architecture co-design: a structured survey, taxonomy, and research directions
candidates.abstract: Embedded AI deployed on highly resource-constrained devices often operates under milliwatt-scale power, kilobyte-range memory, and millisecond-level latency constraints, although the broader embedded/edge spectrum spans much wider resource ranges. Traditional separated design flows, where algorithms and hardware platforms evolve independently, can lead to suboptimal implementations that fail to meet these constraints simultaneously. Algorithm–architecture co-design has emerged as a systematic approach to address this gap through cross-layer optimization. This article provides a structured, taxonomy-driven survey of co-design for embedded AI. We conducted a systematic search across IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, Scopus, and Web of Science (2015–2026), screening 1,247 records down to a final mapped corpus of 122 publications. We organize the literature along four intervention layers: algorithm-level optimization (pruning, quantization, neural architecture search), hardware specialization (instruction set extensions, dataflow architectures, memory hierarchies), compiler-driven transformation (operator fusion, tiling, scheduling), and runtime adaptation (dynamic precision scaling, resource-aware scheduling). For each layer, we analyze how design choices affect five core dimensions: accuracy, latency, energy consumption, memory footprint, and reliability. Applying the taxonomy to the complete 122-publication mapping yields the following corpus-level statistics: 103 of 122 publications (84.4%) carry the broader cross-layer flag, whereas 34 of 122 (27.9%) are explicitly coded as having an explicit cross-layer analysis. The co-design classification distribution is HO = 19 (15.6%), HAC = 72 (59.0%), and FSC = 31 (25.4%). The taxonomy also reveals a highly uneven distribution of contributions across cells, with a small number of well-populated cells and a larger set of sparsely populated cells. These figures are derived directly from the complete S1 mapping and are reported as descriptive corpus statistics rather than as universal measurements. Three overarching research themes emerge: (i) verification-aware co-design, (ii) agentic and digital-twin-driven design automation, and (iii) AI-native hardware substrates. The taxonomy exposes a persistent gap between algorithm-level innovation and hardware-level realization, with cross-layer co-design remaining largely ad hoc and rarely validated under shared experimental conditions. This survey offers a structured reference for researchers and practitioners developing embedded AI systems.

candidates.title: $Δ$ Flow Matching for Robot Foundation Models
candidates.abstract: Flow matching is a common generative recipe for robot foundation models. Vision-language-action models (VLAs) generate action chunks, while world-action models (WAMs) additionally generate future visual states. Both start generation from a fixed Gaussian prior, despite temporal continuity between past and future states and actions. This requires costly training and iterative sampling, especially for WAMs with an additional visual branch. We introduce $Δ$-flow, which constructs the source from recent history with mild noise rather than from a fixed Gaussian prior. This moves the source closer to the target, reducing transport to a small residual $Δ$ that can be learned efficiently and enables single-step inference. We integrate $Δ$-flow into the VLA policy $π_{0.5}$ and the WAM policies ImageWAM and Fast-WAM. On LIBERO, ImageWAM reaches 90% success in one epoch rather than six, and Fast-WAM reaches 95% in two epochs rather than eight. With LoRA fine-tuning, $π_{0.5}$ exceeds its baseline's five-epoch performance after one epoch. Single-step inference gives $1.54\times$, $2.49\times$, and $4.45\times$ speedups on $π_{0.5}$, ImageWAM, and Fast-WAM, respectively. It preserves action smoothness, achieving a $4.5\times$ reduction in action jerk compared with one-step Gaussian sampling. $Δ$-flow reaches state-of-the-art generalization performance on LIBERO-Plus. Action-history sources can be applied to pretrained WAM policies without retraining. Replacing the Gaussian action source at inference largely preserves task success with a single sampling step and can slightly improve it. We further study how action representation and visual information in action learning affect history-to-future prediction in $Δ$-flow. These results show that $Δ$-flow is simple yet effective, improving the efficiency and generalization of robot foundation models.

candidates.title: THE EL-RAKHAWI OPEN-SOURCE PHYSICAL CONSCIENCE MODULE (OPCM) From Unchecked Embodied AI to Hardware-Enforced Human Safety A Groundbreaking Engineering Framework for Mandatory, Air-Gapped, Hardware-Level Safety Overrides in Autonomous Robotics and Embodied Artificial Intelligence Systems
candidates.abstract: The El-Rakhawi Open-Source Physical Conscience Module (OPCM): From Unchecked Embodied AI to Hardware-Enforced Human Safety (DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.23300881) presents a groundbreaking engineering framework across six volumes and 30 chapters securing embodied AI systems: (1) Foundations exposing the fallacy of software-only safety in autonomous robots; (2) Hardware Architecture of air-gapped microcontrollers, independent sensor fusion (LiDAR, depth cameras, IMU), physical power-severing relays, and mechanical brake systems; (3) Kinematic Threat Detection implementing Time-to-Collision (TTC) calculations and human proximity zoning (Red/Yellow/Green) at hardware level; (4) Integration Protocols with ROS 2 via unidirectional optical isolators preventing software override; (5) Regulatory Framework mandating OPCM certification and criminalizing software backdoors; (6) Open-Source Distribution under CERN-OHL-S license preventing safety monopolization. The Embodied AI Safety Index: EASI=(H×R×I×C)/((H×R×I×C)+(W×S×M)+0.01), with W=10, mathematically exposing current danger—typical commercial robots score only 0.002—proving that delegating physical safety to the very AI it constrains is engineering negligence. The OPCM enforces Asimov's First Law through hardware: sub-2ms power severing that no software can override, regardless of AI commands. Protected by mandatory hardware implementation clause, defensive poison pill voiding patent claims, and Embodied Safety Ethics Clause—establishing the third weapon in the open-source salvation arsenal ensuring machines are physically incapable of harming humans, as safety becomes universal baseline rather than corporate premium feature.

candidates.title: CAST-ASD: Causal Attention over Speakers and Time for Online Active Speaker Detection
candidates.abstract: We present CAST-ASD (Causal Attention over Speakers and Time), a causal joint model for active speaker detection (ASD). Recent ASD models improve performance by jointly processing all faces in a scene, but operate offline, with the full clip available before any frame is labelled. Low-latency causal detectors instead process each face independently. CAST-ASD combines joint face reasoning with fully causal inference. It applies scene-level attention across faces within the current frame and causal temporal attention over each face's history, enabling information sharing across speakers with zero lookahead. Its parameter count does not grow with the number of faces. On MSDWild, where most negative face-frames contain a visible competing speaker, CAST-ASD reduces competing-speaker false alarms by 32% relative to the causal per-face detector it extends, with larger gains as scene occupancy increases. It outperforms all causal baselines on both validation splits while using only one-tenth the inter-speaker parameters of a three-block fixed-roster convolution. Code and models are available at https://github.com/prathamg007/CAST-ASD.

candidates.title: Design for Machinability: Topology Optimization for Subtractive Machining Using Trimmed Neural Fields
candidates.abstract: Topology optimization has found significant utility in additive manufacturing, but the resulting geometries are often difficult to realize using subtractive methods. The complex, curved surfaces of optimized designs typically require time-consuming point milling operations. In contrast, geometries composed of developable surfaces are well suited to flank milling, enabling substantial improvements in machining efficiency and surface quality. However, globally minimizing Gaussian curvature leads to overly simplistic designs. We address this challenge with a novel method that represents geometry using three implicit neural fields, optimized to produce machinable components. The resulting designs consist of regions of developable surfaces separated by seamlines where curvature is concentrated. Seamlines are efficiently computed as intersections of the implicit fields, while the geometry emerges through their product. By constraining surfaces to align with the cutter’s normal or tangential direction, our approach further accommodates practical constraints of 3-axis machining. We demonstrate concurrent optimization of topology and Gaussian curvature, enabling control over seamline feature scale. Compared to methods that enforce subtractive machinability without considering milling efficiency, our approach consistently reduces machining time while maintaining competitive structural performance.

candidates.title: Remembering What Matters for Long-Horizon Robotic World Models
candidates.abstract: Autoregressive robot video world models based on discrete visual tokens remain unreliable over long rollout horizons. Retaining the entire generated history does not necessarily improve prediction quality. We investigate a possible memory-role conflict in Full Context decoding: persistent scene information, recent visual-action states, and stale generated history compete for attention despite their different predictive roles. This perspective motivates ReCAP (Receding Context with Anchor Preservation), a training-free context-scheduling method for long-horizon robot video world models. ReCAP keeps the pretrained tokenizer, world model, and visual decoder frozen. It preserves the initial scene anchor and a contiguous window of recent complete visual-action blocks while evicting older generated history. The schedule preserves within-block structure and temporal order, requires no additional modules or parameter updates, and bounds active-context growth independently of rollout length. We evaluate ReCAP on RT-1, BridgeV2, LIBERO-90, and CALVIN using frozen autoregressive world models. Across evaluated environments and horizons, ReCAP improves visual fidelity, action-conditioned consistency, and robot structure preservation relative to Full Context. On BridgeV2, it reduces LPIPS by 63.3%. In the system benchmark at H=64, it reduces the logical KV footprint by 73.3% and p50 latency by 6.51%. Attention analyses show increased attention to retained recent states, while history interventions associate larger amounts of stale context with higher prediction error. These observations are consistent with the memory-role-conflict hypothesis, although they do not isolate it from context-length and position-handling effects. Our results support inference-time context scheduling as a practical approach to improving long-horizon robot video prediction and computational efficiency without retraining.

candidates.title: A deep hybrid feature extraction model based on MobileNet and vision transformer for acute lymphoblastic leukemia prediction
candidates.abstract: Abstract Early and accurate identification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) from peripheral blood smear images can support microscopic screening, but reliable evaluation requires both discriminative feature learning and transparent reporting of the experimental protocol. This study presents MoViTHAFX-Net, a hybrid MobileNet–Vision Transformer (ViT) architecture with Hierarchical Attention Fusion (HAF) and Grad-CAM++ visualization for binary classification of ALL blasts and healthy hematogones (HEM) using the 10,661 labelled cell images in the training component of the C-NMC 2019 dataset. MobileNet extracts local morphological information, whereas ViT models long-range contextual relationships. HAF first refines the two branches and then adaptively combines three learnable morphology-guided feature projections before binary classification. The reported experiment uses an image-level stratified partition containing 7462 training images, 1600 validation images, and 1599 held-out test images; augmentation is restricted to the training partition. On the held-out test partition, the model correctly classified 1583 of 1599 images, corresponding to 99.00% accuracy, with precision, recall, and F1-score of approximately 0.990 and an AUC of 0.99. Ablation results within the same experimental setting indicate an incremental advantage of HAF over direct CNN–ViT concatenation. Grad-CAM++ is used as a qualitative post hoc visualization of image regions contributing to predictions. Because the reported custom split is image-level rather than subject-disjoint and evaluation is limited to a single benchmark dataset, the results should be interpreted as internal benchmark performance rather than evidence of patient-independent or multicentre clinical generalization.

candidates.title: The 2026 World Cup, Anime Edition: Production, Engagement, and Circulation of Generative Memetic Sports Content
candidates.abstract: Generative AI gives audiences new ways to portray real sporting figures through familiar fictional worlds. Expanded opportunities to create, however, need not broaden cultural representation or distribute attention evenly. We examine this tension through the supply, demand, and circulation of anime style football videos on Instagram. Using 2,021 posts and associated video and account data, we combine caption entity extraction, human-reviewed visual identity clustering, engagement analysis, and content-reuse networks. Representation is uneven across athletes, while Blue Lock, Naruto, and One Piece account for 60.1% of explicit franchise mentions. Among posts referencing generative tools, rankings by total engagement differ from rankings by average engagement per video, distinguishing aggregate visibility from response to individual posts. Reuse is extensive: 772 of 1,548 evaluated videos belong to 124 detected groups, including 71 spanning multiple known accounts. Shared material connects a large account component alongside smaller groups, and later observed uploads receive lower median normalized engagement than first observed appearances. These findings characterize generative cultural crossover as a practice organized around concentrated cultural resources, uneven attention, and extensive recirculation. More broadly, they distinguish opportunities for visual authorship from the processes through which particular representations become widely visible.

candidates.title: Ergonomics in Robotics: Advances and Innovations
candidates.abstract: This open access book is tailored to connect robotics & human factors in real-world contexts offering guidance for designing human-centered robotic systems

candidates.title: Future of Anticipatory Robotics in Manufacturing
candidates.abstract: Collaborative robots, designed to work alongside humans in shared environments, are transforming manufacturing production lines, enabling partial automation and boosting productivity. But their potential extends beyond these benefits. By implementing anticipatory strategies to prevent workers’ risky behaviours and reduce excessive workloads, collaborative robots can proactively enhance working conditions. For example, they can take on repetitive or strenuous tasks to reduce physical effort or adjust the pace of operations to help alleviate stress levels. Indeed, Musculoskeletal Disorders (MSDs) and Common Mental Disorders (CMDs), which arise from uncontrolled physical and cognitive loads, are major work-related health problems in developed countries, with incommensurate social and economic costs. Collaborative robots can curb the effect of such disorders and help in preserving workers’ health. This Chapter addresses how Human Factors and Ergonomics (HFE) can be monitored to provide robots with relevant inputs about the human state, and how robots can be employed to improve HFE. Novel strategies are proposed to adapt online robot behaviour to the workers’ psycho-physical state and enhance their well-being and productivity.

candidates.title: Agentic Large Language Models
candidates.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have taken the world by storm. Their ability to communicate with us in our own language, and to reason about our world, has made them a favorite tool for writing, answering questions, and much more. Their answers already influence our decisions and our actions. What would happen if LLMs themselves could act in the world directly? What would happen if LLMs could interact with each other? Agentic LLMs combine the power of large language models with the ability to act in the real world. In this book we will discuss how agentic LLMs work, how they act, how they interact, and what this means for us, as users.

candidates.title: Identifying and Exploiting Structure in Robot Co-Design
candidates.abstract: Co-design is a high-dimensional search problem in the robot morphology and control design space. Efficient search requires exploiting the structure shaped by their interaction. To understand this structure, we analyze the landscapes of soft locomotion and manipulation tasks. We identify three patterns consistent across regions of their co-design spaces: 1) Within a region, quality varies along a low-dimensional manifold, with minimal variation orthogonal to it, reducing the effective search space dimensionality. 2) In higher-quality regions, the variance in quality is spread across more dimensions, necessitating search to expand dimensionality as quality improves. 3) In higher-quality regions, quality varies along joint morphology-control dimensions, requiring search along them. Using these insights, we devise an efficient co-design algorithm that yields 36% better co-designs than state-of-the-art baselines. We examine their exploration patterns and show that these baselines required an order of magnitude more function evaluations to find co-designs of comparable quality. Finally, we ablate our algorithm to verify that exploiting the identified structure was the key to efficient co-design.
