candidates.title: Design and development of IoT based solar power agriculture robot
candidates.abstract: Agriculture in developing economies such as Pakistan remains heavily dependent on manual labor and single-purpose, grid or fuel-powered machinery that is often unaffordable for smallholder farmers. This paper presents the design, fabrication, and experimental evaluation of a multifunctional, solar-powered, Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled agricultural robot capable of performing soil cultivation, seed placement, irrigation, and crop cutting within a single integrated platform. The system architecture is built around an ESP32 microcontroller that interfaces with a DHT11 temperature/humidity sensor, an HC-SR04 ultrasonic obstacle sensor, an ESP32-CAM module for visual field monitoring, an L298N dual H-bridge motor driver, and relay-controlled actuators, with energy supplied by a 20 W photovoltaic panel, a 12 V/7.2 Ah battery, and a battery management system (BMS). Mechanical subsystems comprising a tooth-type cultivator, a soil-leveling roller, a servo-actuated seed dispenser, a DC pump-based irrigation unit, and a blade-type cutter were designed in CAD, fabricated, and integrated onto a four-wheel-drive chassis. Engineering calculations were used to size the power budget, battery backup, drive-motor torque, structural factor of safety, seeding rate, and irrigation flow. Field trials show a typical operating power demand of 24.4 W against an average usable solar output of 11–12 W, a battery backup of approximately 3.5 h, The experimental results demonstrated satisfactory performance of the proposed agricultural robot, achieving an average seed-placement accuracy of 74.45% over 11 experimental trials. The developed system also successfully performed soil digging, irrigation, crop cutting, obstacle detection, and real-time IoT-based remote monitoring, demonstrating its suitability for sustainable precision agriculture.

candidates.title: SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices
candidates.abstract: World-action models (WAMs) predict a robot's actions together with the observations those actions will produce. However, the strongest models rely on video diffusion transformers that are far too computationally expensive for resource-constrained edge devices. We present SmolWAM, a latent WAM that we derive from the 2B-parameter Cosmos Policy by keeping its pretrained trunk and rebuilding its inference interface: single-frame visual latents, cached text features that preserve the trunk's attention sinks, 12 of 28 transformer blocks, and 1,008 tokens from which actions and future visual latents are read out in one rectified-flow step. Trained in 3.6 GPU-hours, SmolWAM succeeds in 95.5% of 400 LIBERO episodes at 57 ms and 2.3 TFLOP per 16-action chunk with 2.4 GiB of GPU memory, 11x faster than its teacher with 18.5x fewer FLOPs and 3.2x less memory, and its world head still forecasts scene motion.

candidates.title: NÁYU UNIVERSAL LANGUAGE RESEARCH CONCEPT
candidates.abstract: NÁYU — Global Validation Challenge: A 10-Page Open Research Protocol NÁYU is an early-stage universal scratch language concept exploring whether a deliberately designed language can support simple human communication and predictable processing by AI systems, software, edge devices, IoT systems, and robotics interfaces. This document introduces the proposed sound inventory, core syllable combinations, prototype grammar, and a global research challenge inviting independent evaluation. It outlines experimental methods for assessing human learnability, multilingual accessibility, AI model interpretation, deterministic parsing, computational resource usage, edge-device performance, and robotics safety. It also proposes benchmark metrics, comparison methods, visualization ideas, reproducibility requirements, and a staged validation roadmap. Research status: Conceptual proposal requiring further specification, implementation, testing, and independent validation. The document does not claim that NÁYU is a proven universal language or that its performance advantages have been experimentally established. The objective is to encourage transparent, reproducible research and collaboration among AI researchers, universities, linguists, software engineers, embedded-systems developers, and robotics teams. Central research question: Can we design a language humans can learn, software can validate, AI can reason over, and future devices can process efficiently? Author: Chigateri RajeshaVersion: 1.0Date: October 2026

candidates.title: Field Notes from a Low-Cost Robot Learning Lab: Hardware Churn, Software Whiplash, and What Actually Went Wrong
candidates.abstract: This is the informal companion to two more rigorous papers from the same project. Over roughly seven weeks we trained imitation-learning policies on a self-built SO-101 robot arm, and along the way we moved the work between machines more often than planned, rebuilt the camera setup, fought a fast-moving open-source framework, and lost an embarrassing amount of time to causes that turned out to be a loose power cable, a swapped port, or a missing audio package. The quantified findings are reported elsewhere. Here we tell the rest: what the hardware and software path actually looked like, which incidents cost us the most time and why, what we would warn a newcomer about, and which threads we deliberately left unfinished. We write for people building something similar on a hobbyist budget, not for reviewers, and we try to be as candid about our mistakes as about our results.

candidates.title: Occupational Wearable Robotics
candidates.abstract: Injuries and occupational diseases represent an important economic factor in different industrial sectors. In Italy alone, there have been over 60000 confirmed cases of occupational diseases in 2022, where musculoskeletal disorders (MSD) represent 70% of the total. This fact highlights the importance of protecting workers against physical efforts. While current ergonomic tools can mitigate most of the risk factors, there is still a non-negligible number of tasks that cannot be completely compensated for. This is due to the high complexity and costs of the workplace reorganization, or simply strict requirements of the target task. In some of these cases, exoskeletons are a viable solution. This chapter introduces different kinds of existing exoskeletons, with particular focus on occupational exoskeletons, considering commercial systems already deployed in industry, and some of the most promising technologies which will arrive in the next years. The deployment of occupational exoskeletons is conditioned by the regulatory frameworks and by the required reorganization of the workplace. Both concepts and the latest developments are discussed in this chapter, including their integration into Industry 4.0. Finally, this chapter describes the most common evaluation methods and discusses current efforts toward standardized benchmarking methods which will allow evaluating the benefit of using exoskeletons in real applications.

candidates.title: Blockchain Security: An Empirical Evaluation of High‐Impact Exploits and Detection Tools
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT Blockchain introduced secure, peer‐to‐peer transactions in decentralized environments without reliance on central authorities. However, attackers continue to exploit blockchain projects. Over the past decade, reported blockchain exploit losses have exceeded $24 billion. Although existing research analyzes blockchain vulnerabilities and real‐world incidents, many studies focus on specific vulnerability classes or smart contract issues only. Therefore, we present an empirical study of major blockchain exploits from 2020 to 2025. Based on detailed analysis of these exploits, we introduce a practitioner‐oriented taxonomy that organizes the dominant root causes observed in the analyzed exploits across four domains: Human Risks, Off‐Chain Infrastructure Vulnerabilities, Private Key Compromises, and Smart Contract Vulnerabilities. Across these categories, we present case studies, code illustrations where applicable, and mitigation strategies. Moreover, we evaluate five vulnerability‐detection tools spanning four paradigms, namely static analysis ( Slither , 4naly3er ), symbolic execution ( Mythril ), bounded/formal verification ( SMTChecker ), and LLM‐assisted analysis ( GPTScan ), on a curated test suite of vulnerable and secure contracts. Our results show detection gaps under the evaluated setting: Slither, Mythril, and 4naly3er all scored recall below 40%. SMTChecker and GPTScan were evaluated separately because of their narrower target scopes. SMTChecker detected only arithmetic issues, while GPTScan produced no benchmark‐relevant detections. The study highlights the high average loss associated with smart contract access‐control failures, the need for post‐deployment monitoring beyond one‐time audits, and risks related to Off‐Chain Infrastructure Vulnerabilities. By analyzing exploits and offering mitigations, we provide a structured reference for identifying, prioritizing, and mitigating major blockchain security risks.

candidates.title: Between Journalism and Justice: Disciplinary Humility in Open-Source Investigations
candidates.abstract: Open-source investigations (OSI) have become an increasingly influential method for reporting on conflict, documenting human rights violations, and supporting justice and accountability efforts. As the field has matured, OSI practitioners have increasingly operated across journalistic, legal, human rights, and technical domains, creating innovation and collaboration opportunities, but also disciplinary tensions. Despite growing scholarship on the institutionalization of OSI, less attention has been paid to how practitioners navigate overlapping disciplinary mandates. Drawing on interviews with 35 practitioners involved in OSI across journalism, human rights, law enforcement and specialized investigative organizations, this article examines how disciplinary boundaries are experienced and responded to within justice and accountability contexts. The findings show that practitioners respond to tensions between journalistic and legal norms through forms of boundary recalibration, including recognizing disciplinary limitations and restructuring investigative work. To explain these dynamics, this article introduces disciplinary humility, defined as the recognition of the limits of one’s disciplinary expertise and mandate when operating across overlapping professional jurisdictions. The article contributes to digital journalism scholarship by showing that the OSI institutionalization is shaped not only by hybridity and boundary crossing, but also by boundary recalibration through which practitioners re-examine expertise and mandates across journalistic and legal contexts.

candidates.title: USE OF DATABASE NARRATIVE IN MULTIMIDIA IPs AND VISUAL NOVELS
candidates.abstract: This article aims to present the theoretical concepts and practical effects of the process of creating multimedia Intellectual Property (IP), as a franchise solidified in the market, through the use of database narrative in the creation of a game genre called visual novel. Through an exploratory study on concepts such as otaku subculture, database narrative, visual novel, and multimedia IPs, using the narrative review method, two case studies were structured. The results demonstrated that the capacity of visual novels to generate new successful multimedia IPs requires relatively small investments compared to other media in this cultural field, both in specific niches and throughout the otaku subculture in general, and even surpassing this subculture, with successful Western visual novels already circulating in the market, feeding back into this highly engaged subculture. This confirmed the hypothesis that the use of visual novels in the construction of a multimedia IP is a strategy successfully adopted since the 1990s, allowing cultural product companies to ensure, with little investment, a constant generation of original or adapted content, just as the creation of content by fan communities after the release of a title. Therefore, it can be concluded that this strategy is ideal for experimenting with narrative elements and for launching products on the market with low cost and high reach among the public.
authors: Vitor Pedro da Silva Castelo Tavares

candidates.title: QSLA Application to Agentic AI-Mediated Robots and Robotic Design
candidates.abstract: Robots directed by agentic artificial intelligence can translate natural-language objectives into sequences of perception, planning, tool use and physical action. Their engineering challenge extends beyond generating a feasible plan: a particular action must have valid authority, adequate evidence, an acceptable transition envelope and enforceable execution conditions. This paper proposes a robotics application of Quantum-Safe Ledger Architecture (QSLA), integrating those obligations through a non-compensatory admission rule. The architecture separates an agent that proposes tasks, an independent governance plane that admits bounded skills, a local controller that maintains immediate physical safety, and an evidence service that records decisions and observed consequences. Heuristic Admissibility and Lineage Logic (HALL) evaluates material claims; the Stochastic Control Barrier Function (SCBF) evaluates uncertain transitions; a theta intervention mechanism selects operational responses; capability security binds permissions to specific robot configurations; and resource reservations coordinate concurrent robots. A hybrid model connects discrete task admission to continuous plant dynamics, with explicit inter-sample obligations and a conditional finite-horizon risk bound. Four worked cases cover warehouse navigation, collaborative manipulation, hospital logistics and AI-assisted robotic design. Proposed information models, failure responses, standards-support mappings and an independent evaluation programme make the architecture inspectable. No robot

candidates.title: Traceable World State: A Provenance-Aware State Representation and Deterministic Replay Framework for Robotic Systems
candidates.abstract: Robotic systems operating over extended tasks must maintain a world state assembled from observations arriving at different times, with varying confidence and potential revisions. Conventional representations emphasize latest estimates, hindering fact provenance, decision reproduction, or execution auditing. We present Traceable World State (TWS), a middleware-neutral semantic representation and reference runtime for provenance-aware robot world state. A TWS snapshot captures entities, relations, observations, confidence, and revision metadata. Validated update operations transform snapshots immutably, ordered updates support deterministic replay, and a canonical SHA-256 hash chain ensures tamper-evident logs. We evaluate TWS through schema conformance, complete state lifecycles, deterministic replay, and fault injection. Passing 38 tests across Python 3.10-3.14, the framework detects record corruptions, broken hash links, sequence discontinuities, and world mismatches. Across ten public BEHAVIOR-1K task definitions, TWS imported 153 entities and 146 relations with successful validation. On 103 NVIDIA Unitree G1 simulated trajectories containing 78,369 frames, TWS achieved exact terminal-state replay in all episodes and detected 412/412 injected corruptions with a 1.72% storage overhead over Plain JSONL.

candidates.title: AI Companions and Loneliness: Conceptualizing and Operationalizing Synthetic Mindfulness and Exploring Its Role in Alleviating Loneliness
candidates.abstract: ABSTRACT The rise of AI companions has sparked interest in their potential to alleviate the growing social problem of loneliness, yet evidence of their effectiveness remains unsettled. Drawing on social surrogacy theory with a theories‐in‐use approach, this research introduces synthetic mindfulness, defined as consumers' judgment of an AI companion's capacity to maintain an attentive presence, engage in a non‐judgmental way, and respond with sensitive attunement to their needs. We argue that these judgments shape whether consumers experience AI companions as capable of reducing their loneliness. Across one qualitative and four quantitative studies, we develop and validate a three‐dimensional measure of synthetic mindfulness. Our final study demonstrates that higher judgments of synthetic mindfulness reduce loneliness via consumers' strengthened sense of belonging and self‐esteem. This research advances understanding of how AI companions can effectively address loneliness and provides a conceptual foundation for examining synthetic mindfulness in human–AI relationships.

candidates.title: Rethinking Diagnostic Assessment Through Culturally Embedded AI for Meaningful Learning
candidates.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence have accelerated the transformation of educational assessment, but most innovations remain focused on automating scoring rather than generating meaningful evidence of learning. This study aims to develop and validate the Meaningful Diagnostic Assessment Framework (MDAF), which integrates culturally contextualised diagnostic tasks, AI-based analysis, and pedagogical interpretation to generate meaningful evidence of learning in mathematics education. The study employed a controlled quasi-experimental design involving 178 junior high school students in Indonesia. Data were analysed using Structural Equation Modelling (SEM), mediation analysis, and tests of agreement between AI-generated diagnoses and expert assessments. The results indicate positive associations between the MDAF and symbolic mathematical performance and student engagement. Cultural Embeddedness Perception partially mediated these relationships, while AI-generated diagnoses showed high agreement with expert assessments. These findings suggest that AI's primary value in assessment lies not in automatically generating scores, but in transforming student responses into meaningful evidence of learning that supports pedagogical decision-making. This study offers a new paradigm for diagnostic assessment by shifting the focus from “assessment as measurement” to “assessment as the generation of meaningful learning evidence,” thereby providing a conceptual foundation for developing digital assessments that are more adaptive, transparent, and oriented toward the learning process.

candidates.title: Spa-Bench: A Real-Robot Benchmark for Spatial Grounding in Vision-Language-Action Models
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action models (VLAs) offer a promising route toward general-purpose robotics by transferring semantic knowledge from large-scale vision-language pretraining into language-conditioned control. However, most VLA evaluations emphasize aggregate manipulation success under changes in objects, instructions, or environments, leaving unclear how reliably these policies ground spatial descriptions in the physical scenes where they act. We therefore ask a sharper question: how reliably can current VLAs translate spatial descriptions into appropriate real-robot behavior? To investigate this, we introduce Spa-Bench, a real-robot benchmark that evaluates spatial grounding across six tabletop tasks covering Object State, Relative Size, Referential Description, Relational Placement, Ordinal Position, and Counting. Our primary evaluation compares in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) spatial configurations while retaining training support for the relevant objects, concepts, and actions, reducing object and motor unfamiliarity as alternative explanations for failure. Four diagnostic conditions further probe physical execution, sensitivity to wording, object-task associations, and recognition that no action is required. We release 4,092 episodes collected on the SO-101 robot arm: 1,200 human-teleoperated demonstrations and 2,892 real-robot evaluation rollouts from five state-of-the-art VLA policies. Across the three fully evaluated policies, success falls from 67.5-73.3% on ID spatial configurations to 40.7-52.0% on OOD spatial configurations, while matched direct instructions improve success by 28.3-40.0 percentage points. These results show that the evaluated VLAs can often execute the required manipulations but lack robust spatial grounding. Project materials, including videos, code, and benchmark data, are available at https://justintiensmith.github.io/Spa-Bench/.

candidates.title: OctoSense: Building a Unified Ecosystem for Open-Source Wireless Sensing
candidates.abstract: As AI enters the physical world, wireless sensing has emerged as a key modality for enabling non-intrusive physical intelligence. However, unlike the mature ecosystems of vision and language models, wireless sensing research remains highly fragmented. The field faces a growing "reproducibility wall" caused by heterogeneous data formats, non-interoperable processing pipelines, and the lack of standardized benchmarks. To dismantle this barrier, we present OctoSense, a unified platform designed to propel wireless sensing toward an "ImageNet-style" research ecosystem. OctoSense introduces a holistic framework that decouples high-level model logic from ad-hoc data nuances through three distinct components: a unified data abstraction for streamlined dataset access, standardized signal operators for efficient model development, and a rigorous benchmark engine for rapid and fair comparison. To support existing datasets and models, OctoSense integrates a comprehensive suite of widely used datasets and models, reducing the effort required for data and model adaptation to a few lines of declarative code. We demonstrate the efficacy of OctoSense through a set of usage examples that reproduce representative models on popular datasets. By providing a foundational open-source infrastructure, OctoSense enables community efforts to accumulate rather than fragment, paving the way for wireless sensing research that is interoperable, reusable, and reproducible by design.

candidates.title: Ritual Paraphernalia Toward a Modular Approach to Coptic Magic
candidates.abstract: This article explores the redactional strategies through which ritual experts in late antique and early medieval Egypt articulated their textual products. It adopts what is here heuristically termed a ‘modular approach’, which treats magical texts as assemblages of discrete textual segments that could be extracted, recombined, and adapted to different redactional agendas. Drawing on selected case studies from Coptic ritual manuscripts, the article offers a new model for understanding scribal practice and the transmission of ritual knowledge.

candidates.title: AgentEvolver: System-Wide Self-Evolution Through Task Execution
candidates.abstract: An agent can complete a task without improving how it works. Turning task experience into reusable capability requires connecting the changed component to its evaluation and subsequent use. We present AgentEvolver, a system for developing capabilities during task execution while keeping the foundation model fixed. Eight entity families expose reusable operations, methods, agents, control flow, interfaces, and supporting state to revision through a common versioned lifecycle. A shared Runtime coordinates ongoing work, while persistent planning and recoverable context preserve task direction and supporting evidence. We evaluate task outcomes on SWE-bench Pro Public and examine capability changes in six application cases. The team reports an 82.08\% resolution rate with evolution, exceeding its reported baseline without evolution. The cases show retained capabilities entering later website, game, and research work, while also documenting incomplete objectives and an unsuccessful strategy. These findings distinguish improvement in a reusable component from success on the final task. AgentEvolver provides a concrete basis for studying capability accumulation through execution; independent-task transfer and total development cost remain open questions.
